387	## Prototype invariants
388	
389	### PI-01 — Server behaviour is simulated
390	All server-side behaviour — authentication, API calls, persistence, email — is simulated by client-side stubs. Backend-shaped requirements describe user-visible behaviour, not real implementation.
391	
392	### PI-02 — Data is fixture-backed
393	All data is sourced from in-memory fixtures shipped with the build. Mutations persist within a session but do not survive a reload unless a "demo data" mode is specified. There is no real database.
394	
395	### PI-03 — Validation is visual only
396	Form-field validation and inline errors are rendered as specified, but no server-side enforcement is exercised.
397	
398	### PI-04 — Third-party integrations are visual
399	Any email/notification on submit or resolve appears as a UI confirmation only; no external network calls are made.
400	
401	### PI-05 — Role switcher
402	Every screen accessible to more than one role displays a role switcher in the prototype's surrounding chrome — outside the application UI under design — so reviewers can inspect each role's view without re-authenticating. It lists every role in §3; roles to whom the active screen is not accessible per §6.5 are shown disabled. Switching the active role immediately updates the screen's visible components and actions to match the requirements (RBAC entries, conditional visibility, role-gated actions).

1	# The `documentation/` Folder
2	
3	This is where you put anything that describes **what you want to build**. Claude Code reads this folder during Intake — the first stage of the workflow — and uses whatever it finds to produce a project brief for your approval.
4	
5	You don't need to put anything here. If the folder is empty, Claude Code will just ask you questions when you run `/start`. But the more you provide, the less you'll have to answer in chat.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## What to Put Here
10	
11	Anything you have. Claude Code recognises and uses these kinds of files automatically:
12	
13	| What | Why it helps |
14	|---|---|
15	| **A feature description** (any `.md` file) | The main thing — tells Claude Code what you want built and who it's for |
16	| **An OpenAPI spec** (`.yaml` / `.json` containing `openapi:` or `swagger:`) | Locks in the real endpoints your backend exposes, so Claude Code uses your actual API shape instead of guessing |
17	| **Sample data** (any `.json` / `.csv`) | Helps Claude Code understand the shape of your data |
18	| **Wireframes** (in a `wireframes/` subfolder) | Reference for layout and screen flow |
19	| **Brand or styling notes** | Logo files, colour palettes, fonts, a `tokens.css` file — anything that defines the look and feel |
20	| **A design** (a Claude Design or Figma export, an HTML mockup) | See [Working from an existing design](#working-from-an-existing-design) below |
21	
22	File names and folder structure don't matter — Claude Code scans the whole folder. The `documentation/` folder is read-only during the workflow; Claude Code never modifies what you put here.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## A Simple Feature Description
27	
28	If you're starting from scratch, the easiest thing is one markdown file describing your feature in plain language. Here's an example:
29	
30	```markdown
31	# User Profile Page
32	
33	A page where signed-in users can view and edit their profile.
34	
35	## What users should be able to do
36	
37	- View their name, email, and profile picture
38	- See when their account was created
39	- Edit their name and profile picture inline (no separate edit page)
40	- Get a confirmation message after saving changes
41	
42	## Things to keep in mind
43	
44	- Changing email address should require re-verification
45	- Use a card layout
46	- Accessible from the main navigation menu
47	```
48	
49	That's enough for Claude Code to produce a useful project brief. You can be more detailed if you like — include user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, or anything else you think matters — but you don't have to.
50	
51	---
52	
53	## If You Have a Backend
54	
55	Put your OpenAPI spec in this folder (any name ending `.yaml` or `.json` will be detected). Claude Code uses it as the source of truth for endpoints, request/response shapes, and authentication — so the generated code calls your real API, not invented endpoints.
56	
57	If your spec defines authentication (`securitySchemes`), Claude Code will run a quick connection test against your backend at the end of Intake to catch credential or URL problems before any code is written.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## Working from an existing design
62	
63	If you've already designed your app — in Claude Design, Figma, as wireframes, or even a hand-written HTML mockup — you can build from that design instead of writing a fresh spec, and Claude Code rebuilds your screens faithfully in this stack. There's no import step and nothing to point Claude Code at: **just put the design files in this folder.** If they came as a `.zip`, unzip it and drop the files into `documentation/` (or drop loose files in directly). That's the whole mechanism.
64	
65	When you run `/start`, Claude Code **reads** whatever design files it finds, works out what your screens are — their layout, fields, copy, validation, colours and fonts — and reads it all back to you at Intake for confirmation before anything is built. It also tells you plainly what it *couldn't* determine, so you can fill those gaps rather than have it guess.
66	
67	**File shape and layout don't matter.** Claude Code reads the design by understanding it, not by matching a fixed export format — so a folder of files, loose files, a renamed export, or a mix of formats all work the same way. You don't have to arrange anything into a particular structure, and it isn't tied to any one design tool.
68	
69	**What reads reliably.** Anything text-based — HTML, wireframes, notes, specs — is the dependable core and reads well. Images, screenshots, and PDFs are read too, but reconstructing exact text and layout from a picture is less certain; Claude Code uses what it can and is upfront about anything it's unsure of. If a file turns out to be unreadable — a single bundled export file, say — it tells you and asks for it in a form it can read. Either way, nothing is silently dropped — what it read and what it didn't both surface at Intake.
70	
71	**A design gives Claude Code your screens and look, not your requirements.** Files that come with your design might include a requirements doc — or just a logo, or nothing. If your design comes with requirements, Claude Code uses them; otherwise it asks a few short questions to fill the gaps, guided by the screens it read.
72	
73	**Updating later.** Changed your design? Drop the new versions into `documentation/`, then run `/start` — or `/plan` to line it up while something else builds — and describe what you want: *"rebuild the dashboard and settings screens to match my updated design."* Claude Code re-reads your design and builds only what you asked for, through the usual plan → build → review → merge flow. There's no special "refresh" mode.
74	
75	**Your decisions stick.** Claude Code keeps a written record of your design and adds to it every time you settle something it couldn't get from your files — a colour that wasn't in there, where a button should lead, or a change you asked for while testing ("actually, move that filter to the right"). Those decisions **override your design files**, so re-reading the design never quietly puts a screen back the way the design has it. When it re-reads, it updates that record rather than rewriting it, tells you in plain words what moved ("the Export button is now called Download CSV"), and if your new design contradicts something you'd decided, it asks you which one to build instead of picking for you.
76	
77	**Already built your app without a design?** You can still drop one in and rebuild against it. Claude Code will only change the screens you name — everything else is left alone — and if a screen you're rebuilding should keep the behaviour it has now rather than matching the design, say so and it's recorded.
78	
79	---
80	
81	## What Happens Next
82

7	file directly during agent runs to pick up project-level facts. The dashboard
8	and other automated consumers read state.json instead.

1	# Requirements: Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	**Domain:** Customer support — public enquiry capture and back-office triage **Created:** 2026-07-23 **Status:** final
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Application context
8	
9	**Name:** Contact & Enquiry Management
10	
11	**Purpose / business value:** Let a **Visitor** send a contact enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and receive immediate confirmation, while giving back-office staff a triage surface: a **Support Agent** works enquiries through a status lifecycle, and an **Admin** additionally curates the inbox (delete spam, reassign). A single public form feeds a role-gated review workflow.
12	
13	**Domain:** Generic customer-support / contact-us, applicable to any organisation that fields public enquiries.
14	
15	**Business goal:** Capture every enquiry with a confirmed hand-off, and ensure each one reaches a terminal, auditable state (Resolved with a reply note) without a Visitor ever seeing another person's enquiry or the back-office surfaces.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 2. Domain model
20	
21	> The business domain in **ubiquitous language**, implementation-free.
22	
23	### 2.1 Concepts
24	
25	| Concept          | Persistence | Definition (ubiquitous language) |
26	| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
27	| Enquiry          | persistent  | A contact message submitted by a Visitor, carrying contact details, a category, a comment, and its handling state. |
28	| User             | persistent  | An authenticated actor of the system, identified by email and bearing one of the system's roles. |
29	| Enquiry Status   | derived     | The lifecycle position of an Enquiry — `New`, `In Progress`, or `Resolved` — that gates the actions back-office roles may take. |
30	| Category         | enum        | The nature of an Enquiry as chosen by the Visitor — `Feedback`, `Question`, or `General Enquiry`. |
31	| Reply Note       | attribute   | The free-text response captured by a back-office role when an Enquiry is moved to `Resolved`. |
32	
33	### 2.2 Relationships
34	
35	- **User** *submits* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Visitor only
36	- **User** *handles* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Support Agent / Admin only
37	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Enquiry Status** [1 : 1]
38	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Category** [1 : 1]
39	
40	### 2.3 Aggregates & lifecycles
41	
42	#### Enquiry
43	
44	| Field            | Value |
45	| ---------------- | ----- |
46	| Member concepts  | Enquiry, Enquiry Status, Category, Reply Note |
47	| Lifecycle states | `New` → `In Progress` → `Resolved` — terminal state is `Resolved`; once terminal, status does not change. |

244	## 6. Requirements
245	
246	### 6.1 Functional
247	
248	- F-01 The system supports email-and-password authentication and routes the user to a role-specific landing surface on success.
249	- F-02 A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category, and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created in `New`.
250	- F-03 On successful submit, the system routes to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details, clears the form, and shows a "Message sent!" confirmation.
251	- F-04 A Visitor may view a read-only list of the Enquiries they submitted, and only those.
252	- F-05 A Support Agent or Admin may view all Enquiries in a sortable, paginated table.
253	- F-06 A Support Agent or Admin may filter Enquiries by Category, Status, and free-text search on Name and Comment.
254	- F-07 A Support Agent or Admin may move a non-terminal Enquiry from `New` to `In Progress`.
255	- F-08 A Support Agent or Admin may resolve a non-terminal Enquiry by submitting a non-empty Reply Note, transitioning it to `Resolved`.
256	- F-09 An Admin may delete an Enquiry.
257	- F-10 The system surfaces the Reply Note read-only on a `Resolved` Enquiry's detail.
258	
259	### 6.2 Business rules
260	
261	| ID | Statement (when / then) | Enforcement point | Severity |
262	| ---- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | -------- |
263	| BR-01 | When an Enquiry's Status is `Resolved`, then status-change actions must be hidden in the UI. | UI | blocker |
264	| BR-02 | When a back-office user resolves an Enquiry, then a non-empty Reply Note must be submitted; the submit control is disabled until a note is entered. | UI | blocker |
265	| BR-03 | When a destructive Delete is triggered, then a confirmation modal naming the Enquiry must be shown before removal. | UI | blocker |
266	| BR-04 | When a Visitor views their submissions, then only Enquiries they submitted may be shown. | UI | blocker |
267	| BR-05 | When a user without access reaches a role-restricted surface via a direct link, then an in-page permission-denied banner must be shown (never a generic 403 page). | UI | major |
268	| BR-06 | When the Contact form is submitted, then Email must match a valid email format and Comment must be non-empty (min 10 characters). | UI | major |
269	
270	### 6.3 Data
271	
272	- The Enquiry record carries the fields enumerated on the §7 Enquiry entity.
273	- Enquiry Status enum values are exactly `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved`.
274	- Category enum values are exactly `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry`.
275	- Reply Note is required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 characters.
276	
277	### 6.4 User-facing
278	
279	- UF-01 The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select), and Comment (multi-line) with a leading-asterisk convention on required fields and a single legend line.
280	- UF-02 Forms validate on blur for synchronous rules (format, required, length) and on submit for cross-field rules; never on keystroke. On success, the form resets and a success toast (auto-dismiss 4–8 s, top-right) confirms.
281	- UF-03 The confirmation page echoes the submitted Name, Email, Category, and Comment read-only, with a "Message sent!" heading and a control to send another.
282	- UF-04 The Inbox table renders Name, Category, Status, Submitted date, with a row-click to detail and (Admin-only) a Delete row action. Pagination ladder 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 (default 20); single-column sort, ascending then descending; the pagination control is always rendered.
283	- UF-05 Status badges colour-map: `New` (info / blue), `In Progress` (in-progress / amber), `Resolved` (success / green). Colour is always paired with an icon or text label; never relied on alone.
284	- UF-06 Empty states distinguish zero-data ("No enquiries yet" / "You haven't sent any messages yet") from zero-results-of-filter (active filter chips + Clear-all, no creation CTA).
285	- UF-07 The Resolve modal displays a mandatory Reply Note text field (multi-line) with a character counter and a clear ceiling.
286	- UF-08 Icon-only row actions carry tooltips on hover and focus plus an `aria-label` matching the tooltip; primary destructive actions are never icon-only.
287	- UF-09 Denied-access surfaces render an in-page permission-denied banner naming the missing permission and a path back to the user's own surface.
288	- UF-10 Top-level navigation is role-scoped: Visitor sees Contact + My messages; Agent/Admin see Inbox; Admin additionally sees Delete affordances.

387	## Prototype invariants
388	
389	### PI-01 — Server behaviour is simulated
390	All server-side behaviour — authentication, API calls, persistence, email — is simulated by client-side stubs. Backend-shaped requirements describe user-visible behaviour, not real implementation.
391	
392	### PI-02 — Data is fixture-backed
393	All data is sourced from in-memory fixtures shipped with the build. Mutations persist within a session but do not survive a reload unless a "demo data" mode is specified. There is no real database.
394	
395	### PI-03 — Validation is visual only
396	Form-field validation and inline errors are rendered as specified, but no server-side enforcement is exercised.
397	
398	### PI-04 — Third-party integrations are visual
399	Any email/notification on submit or resolve appears as a UI confirmation only; no external network calls are made.
400	
401	### PI-05 — Role switcher
402	Every screen accessible to more than one role displays a role switcher in the prototype's surrounding chrome — outside the application UI under design — so reviewers can inspect each role's view without re-authenticating. It lists every role in §3; roles to whom the active screen is not accessible per §6.5 are shown disabled. Switching the active role immediately updates the screen's visible components and actions to match the requirements (RBAC entries, conditional visibility, role-gated actions).

9	**Running dev tools:** Run the project's npm scripts from `web/` in a subshell — `(cd web && npm run <script>)` for tsc/eslint/build/etc. and `(cd web && npm test -- <pattern>)` for Vitest — all auto-approved. The `( … )` runs the command in `web/` (so `web/vitest.config.ts` and the `@/` alias resolve) while leaving the shell's cwd at the repo root. Never run these from the repo root: a bare `npx vitest` loads no `web/vitest.config.ts` (the `@/` alias breaks) and `npm --prefix web test` crashes Vitest 4's worker pool at collection ("No test suite found" on Windows/Node 24 — see `generated-docs/template-feedback.md`). Playwright is the same: `(cd web && npm run test:e2e -- <args>)`. Pass Node flags inside the subshell (`(cd web && NODE_OPTIONS=… npm test)`); a direct `node ./node_modules/<tool>/…` call is NOT auto-approved.

# Contact & Enquiry Management

A contact-and-enquiry app where a Visitor sends an enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and gets confirmation straight away. Back-office staff work through the enquiries: a Support Agent moves each one through New, In Progress and Resolved, and an Admin can also delete enquiries. Enquiries are scoped by role, so a Visitor sees only their own.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project slug | `contact-form` |
| Created | 2026-11-03T07:17:19Z |
| Intake source | docs (`documentation/requirements.md`) |
| Backend connectivity | mock-only |

---

## Roles & Permissions

**Template:** `custom`

| Permission | Visitor | Support Agent | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|
| View main dashboard | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

**Role definitions** (from intake and `requirements.md` §3 / §6.5):

- **Visitor:** can sign in, submit an enquiry and view their own submissions (read-only). Lands on the Contact form. Cannot see the Inbox or other people's enquiries, and cannot change status or delete.
- **Support Agent:** can view all enquiries, search and filter them, move status from New to In Progress to Resolved, and resolve an enquiry with a mandatory reply note. Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form or delete.
- **Admin:** has every Support Agent permission and can also delete an enquiry (behind a confirmation). Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form.

Denied actions are **hidden** in the UI, not shown as disabled. Opening a role-restricted page through a direct link shows a permission-denied banner on the page, not a generic 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05 / UF-09).

> Permissions extend during BUILD as new stories surface new actions. Additions are recorded here as they come up, with your approval. Removing a permission, or changing who the roles are, stops for you to review.

---

## Authentication

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Method | `server-side` (BFF: your own server) |
| Auth login endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Auth is simulated by client-side stubs (`requirements.md` PI-01); no real backend endpoint |
| Auth userinfo endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
| Auth logout endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
| Custom auth notes | Auth is simulated client-side, as the prototype invariants require. The BFF shape follows the template's server-side auth policy. Sign-in uses email and password, then sends each role to its landing page (Visitor to the Contact form; Support Agent and Admin to the Inbox). Seeded users: `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin). |

> Auth method is never inferred — the user must confirm explicitly per [authentication-intake.md](.claude/policies/authentication-intake.md).

---

## Data Source & Backend Integration

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Data source | `mock-only` |
| Backend status | `N/A` (none) |
| Mock layer required | yes. In-memory fixtures built from `requirements.md`: a few seeded enquiries covering all three categories (Feedback / Question / General Enquiry) and all three statuses (New / In Progress / Resolved), plus the three seeded users. Changes last for the session but not past a reload (PI-02). Emails and notifications show only as UI confirmations (PI-04). |

### API specs

No OpenAPI spec was provided. The domain entities (Enquiry, User) are defined in `documentation/requirements.md` §7.

---

## Compliance

**Applicable domains:** None (the user confirmed the project is not regulated)
**Region (if Personal data applies):** N/A

### Compliance Requirements

No compliance domains were identified during intake screening.

- Note: the app does collect personal data (name, email, optional address). Only authenticated back-office roles (Support Agent, Admin) can see enquiries. Visitors never see anyone else's (`requirements.md` §6.6.1, BR-04).

---

## Styling & Branding

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary brand color | `#2563eb` [INFERRED] the user asked for template defaults with no bespoke design system, so this is the styling-centralisation Pattern A default (Tailwind blue-600) |

| Background (light) | `#ffffff` [INFERRED] the default for a neutral light palette |

| Source | defaulted (user: "template Shadcn defaults with a clean, neutral palette and centralised styling tokens") |

> Component-specific styling (button radii, card shadows, etc.) emerges during BUILD. This section captures only palette intent and typography per [styling-centralisation.md](.claude/policies/styling-centralisation.md).

---

## Baseline NFRs

- **NFR-base-1:** Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 Level AA (`requirements.md` §6.6.3 raises this above the 2.1 AA baseline). Primary flows are keyboard-first, status colour is always paired with an icon or text, and icon-only controls have a tooltip and an `aria-label`
- **NFR-base-2:** Performance: First Contentful Paint < 2.5s on a mid-tier mobile network
- **NFR-base-3:** Responsive design: mobile (≥360px) / tablet (≥768px) / desktop (≥1280px) breakpoints
- **NFR-base-4:** Browser support: latest two versions of Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari
- **NFR-base-5:** Error UX: every async operation shows a visible error state with a way to retry
- **NFR-base-6:** [INFERRED] Session policy: 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout, and lockout for 15 minutes after 5 failed sign-in attempts. Carried over from `requirements.md` §6.6.1, which marks these values as inferred. Auth is simulated (PI-01), so this behaviour is shown in the UI only

1	# Requirements: Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	**Domain:** Customer support — public enquiry capture and back-office triage **Created:** 2026-07-23 **Status:** final
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Application context
8	
9	**Name:** Contact & Enquiry Management
10	
11	**Purpose / business value:** Let a **Visitor** send a contact enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and receive immediate confirmation, while giving back-office staff a triage surface: a **Support Agent** works enquiries through a status lifecycle, and an **Admin** additionally curates the inbox (delete spam, reassign). A single public form feeds a role-gated review workflow.
12	
13	**Domain:** Generic customer-support / contact-us, applicable to any organisation that fields public enquiries.
14	
15	**Business goal:** Capture every enquiry with a confirmed hand-off, and ensure each one reaches a terminal, auditable state (Resolved with a reply note) without a Visitor ever seeing another person's enquiry or the back-office surfaces.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 2. Domain model
20	
21	> The business domain in **ubiquitous language**, implementation-free.
22	
23	### 2.1 Concepts
24	
25	| Concept          | Persistence | Definition (ubiquitous language) |
26	| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
27	| Enquiry          | persistent  | A contact message submitted by a Visitor, carrying contact details, a category, a comment, and its handling state. |
28	| User             | persistent  | An authenticated actor of the system, identified by email and bearing one of the system's roles. |
29	| Enquiry Status   | derived     | The lifecycle position of an Enquiry — `New`, `In Progress`, or `Resolved` — that gates the actions back-office roles may take. |
30	| Category         | enum        | The nature of an Enquiry as chosen by the Visitor — `Feedback`, `Question`, or `General Enquiry`. |
31	| Reply Note       | attribute   | The free-text response captured by a back-office role when an Enquiry is moved to `Resolved`. |
32	
33	### 2.2 Relationships
34	
35	- **User** *submits* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Visitor only
36	- **User** *handles* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Support Agent / Admin only
37	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Enquiry Status** [1 : 1]
38	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Category** [1 : 1]
39	
40	### 2.3 Aggregates & lifecycles
41	
42	#### Enquiry
43	
44	| Field            | Value |
45	| ---------------- | ----- |
46	| Member concepts  | Enquiry, Enquiry Status, Category, Reply Note |
47	| Lifecycle states | `New` → `In Progress` → `Resolved` — terminal state is `Resolved`; once terminal, status does not change. |
48	| Key invariants   | Status-change actions are available only while the Enquiry is non-terminal. Moving an Enquiry to `Resolved` requires a non-empty Reply Note. A Visitor may read only Enquiries they submitted. |
49

55	      +Id

170	## 5. Task flows
171	
172	### Flow: Authentication
173	
174	| Field | Value |
175	| ----- | ----- |
176	| Actor | Visitor, Support Agent, or Admin |
177	| Trigger | User opens the application unauthenticated. |
178	| Steps | 1. Enter email + password. 2. Submit. 3. On success, route to the role's landing surface (Visitor → Contact form; Agent/Admin → Inbox). 4. On failure, inline error distinguishing credentials from connectivity. |
179	| Role-conditional behaviour | Post-login routing differs by role per §3. |
180	
181	### Flow: Submit Enquiry
182	
183	| Field | Value |
184	| ----- | ----- |
185	| Actor | Visitor |
186	| Trigger | Visitor wants to contact the organisation. |
187	| Steps | 1. Open the Contact form. 2. Enter Name, Email, optional Address, choose a Category, enter a Comment. 3. Submit. 4. System creates an Enquiry in `New`. 5. Route to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details; the form is cleared; a "Message sent!" confirmation shows. |
188	| Decision points | All required fields valid → submit succeeds. Any invalid → inline validation, submit blocked. |
189	| Exception paths | Email malformed → inline error. Comment empty / too short → inline error. |
190	| Role-conditional behaviour | Visitor-only — Agent/Admin do not see the public form in their navigation. |
191	
192	### Flow: My Submissions
193	
194	| Field | Value |
195	| ----- | ----- |
196	| Actor | Visitor |
197	| Trigger | Visitor wants to review enquiries they sent. |
198	| Steps | 1. Open "My messages". 2. See a read-only list of **their own** enquiries with category, status, and submitted date. |

244	## 6. Requirements
245	
246	### 6.1 Functional
247	
248	- F-01 The system supports email-and-password authentication and routes the user to a role-specific landing surface on success.
249	- F-02 A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category, and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created in `New`.
250	- F-03 On successful submit, the system routes to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details, clears the form, and shows a "Message sent!" confirmation.
251	- F-04 A Visitor may view a read-only list of the Enquiries they submitted, and only those.
252	- F-05 A Support Agent or Admin may view all Enquiries in a sortable, paginated table.
253	- F-06 A Support Agent or Admin may filter Enquiries by Category, Status, and free-text search on Name and Comment.
254	- F-07 A Support Agent or Admin may move a non-terminal Enquiry from `New` to `In Progress`.
255	- F-08 A Support Agent or Admin may resolve a non-terminal Enquiry by submitting a non-empty Reply Note, transitioning it to `Resolved`.

257	- F-10 The system surfaces the Reply Note read-only on a `Resolved` Enquiry's detail.

265	| BR-03 | When a destructive Delete is triggered, then a confirmation modal naming the Enquiry must be shown before removal. | UI | blocker |
266	| BR-04 | When a Visitor views their submissions, then only Enquiries they submitted may be shown. | UI | blocker |
267	| BR-05 | When a user without access reaches a role-restricted surface via a direct link, then an in-page permission-denied banner must be shown (never a generic 403 page). | UI | major |
268	| BR-06 | When the Contact form is submitted, then Email must match a valid email format and Comment must be non-empty (min 10 characters). | UI | major |

272	- The Enquiry record carries the fields enumerated on the §7 Enquiry entity.
273	- Enquiry Status enum values are exactly `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved`.
274	- Category enum values are exactly `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry`.
275	- Reply Note is required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 characters.

277	### 6.4 User-facing
278	
279	- UF-01 The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select), and Comment (multi-line) with a leading-asterisk convention on required fields and a single legend line.
280	- UF-02 Forms validate on blur for synchronous rules (format, required, length) and on submit for cross-field rules; never on keystroke. On success, the form resets and a success toast (auto-dismiss 4–8 s, top-right) confirms.
281	- UF-03 The confirmation page echoes the submitted Name, Email, Category, and Comment read-only, with a "Message sent!" heading and a control to send another.

335	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier. |
336	| Name | string | yes | non-empty; max 120 chars | Displayed as the primary identifier in the inbox. |
337	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | The reply-to; shown on detail. |
338	| Address | string | no | max 255 chars | Optional; shown on detail. |
339	| Category | enum | yes | one of `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` | Displayed as a column and filter. |
340	| Comment | string | yes | non-empty; min 10, max 2000 chars | The enquiry body; shown on detail. |
341	| Status | enum | yes | one of `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` | Displayed as a status badge. |
342	| ReplyNote | string | no | required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 chars | Captured via the Resolve modal; read-only after resolution. |
343	| SubmittedAt | datetime | yes | system-assigned (ISO-8601) | Displayed as the Submitted date column; sortable. |
344	| SubmittedByEmail | string | yes | mirrors submitting Visitor | Scopes "My submissions"; audit. |
345	| HandledBy | string | no | mirrors the acting back-office user | Set when status first changes; audit. |
346	
347	**Enums:** `Status` ∈ { `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` }; `Category` ∈ { `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` }
348	
349	### Entity: User
350	
351	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
352	| ----- | ---- | -------- | ---------- | ----- |
353	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier. |
354	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Login identifier. |
355	| FirstName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | Greeting / detail. |
356	| LastName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | Greeting / detail. |
357	| Password | string | yes | min complexity per policy | Write-only; never displayed. |
358	| Role | enum | yes | one of `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` | Drives post-login routing and RBAC. |
359	
360	**Enums:** `Role` ∈ { `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` }
361	
362	---
363	
364	## 8. Key terminology
365	
366	| Term | Definition |
367	| ---- | ---------- |
368	| Enquiry | A contact message submitted by a Visitor. → §2.1. |
369	| Visitor | The role that submits enquiries and views their own. → §3. |
370	| Support Agent | The role that triages and resolves enquiries. → §3. |
371	| Admin | The role that can do everything an Agent can, plus delete. → §3. |
372	| Reply Note | The free-text response captured when an Enquiry is resolved. → §2.1. |
373	| New / In Progress / Resolved | The Enquiry lifecycle states; `Resolved` is terminal. |
374	
375	---
376	
377	## 9. Volumes
378	
379	| Metric | Value | Source |
380	| ------ | ----- | ------ |
381	| Data volume | 10¹–10³ enquiries in scope for the prototype. | inferred |
382	| Frequency | Sporadic submissions; daily back-office triage. | inferred |
383	| Concurrency | 1–5 concurrent back-office users; small team. | inferred |
384	
385	---
386	
387	## Prototype invariants
388	
389	### PI-01 — Server behaviour is simulated
390	All server-side behaviour — authentication, API calls, persistence, email — is simulated by client-side stubs. Backend-shaped requirements describe user-visible behaviour, not real implementation.
391	
392	### PI-02 — Data is fixture-backed
393	All data is sourced from in-memory fixtures shipped with the build. Mutations persist within a session but do not survive a reload unless a "demo data" mode is specified. There is no real database.
394	
395	### PI-03 — Validation is visual only
396	Form-field validation and inline errors are rendered as specified, but no server-side enforcement is exercised.
397	
398	### PI-04 — Third-party integrations are visual
399	Any email/notification on submit or resolve appears as a UI confirmation only; no external network calls are made.
400	
401	### PI-05 — Role switcher
402	Every screen accessible to more than one role displays a role switcher in the prototype's surrounding chrome — outside the application UI under design — so reviewers can inspect each role's view without re-authenticating. It lists every role in §3; roles to whom the active screen is not accessible per §6.5 are shown disabled. Switching the active role immediately updates the screen's visible components and actions to match the requirements (RBAC entries, conditional visibility, role-gated actions).

    epic: enquiry-handling

    epic: enquiry-handling

DECOMPOSITION PROPOSAL
---
requirementInventory:
  - id: R1
    name: Sign in with email and password, landing on your role's page
    text: "F-01 — The system supports email-and-password authentication and routes the user to a role-specific landing surface on success (Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent / Admin → Inbox)."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R2
    name: Sign-in failure explains what went wrong
    text: "Authentication flow step 4 — on failure, an inline error distinguishes wrong credentials from a connection problem."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R3
    name: Session time limits and lockout after repeated failed sign-ins
    text: "§6.6.1 / NFR-base-6 — 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout, 5 failed attempts → 15-minute lockout (shown in the UI only; auth is simulated)."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R4
    name: Menu shows only what your role can use
    text: "UF-10 — Top-level navigation is role-scoped: Visitor sees Contact + My messages; Support Agent / Admin see Inbox. Denied actions are hidden, not disabled (§6.5 notes)."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R5
    name: Opening a page you can't use shows a 'no permission' message on the page
    text: "BR-05 / UF-09 — A user reaching a role-restricted surface via a direct link sees an in-page permission-denied banner naming the missing permission and a path back to their own surface — never a generic 403 page."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R6
    name: Role switcher for reviewers
    text: "PI-05 — Every screen accessible to more than one role shows a role switcher in the surrounding prototype chrome listing every role; roles that can't access the screen are shown disabled; switching immediately updates visible components and actions."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R7
    name: Enquiry record, categories and statuses, with seeded sample enquiries and users
    text: "§2 / §6.3 / §7 / PI-02 — Enquiry fields per §7; Status is exactly New / In Progress / Resolved; Category is exactly Feedback / Question / General Enquiry; in-memory seeded enquiries covering every category and status plus the three seeded users; changes last for the session but not past a reload."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R8
    name: Accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA across the app
    text: "§6.6.3 / NFR-base-1 — WCAG 2.2 AA; keyboard-first operation across all primary flows; status colour always paired with an icon or text."
    epic: sign-in-and-app-shell
  - id: R9
    name: Send an enquiry from the Contact form
    text: "F-02 — A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created in New."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R10
    name: Contact form layout
    text: "UF-01 — The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select) and Comment (multi-line), with a leading asterisk on required fields and a single legend line; fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R11
    name: Contact form checks email and comment before sending
    text: "BR-06 / §7 — Email must be a valid format; Comment non-empty, min 10 / max 2000 characters; Name max 120; Address max 255. Invalid input shows inline errors and blocks submit."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R12
    name: Form errors appear when you leave a field, not while typing
    text: "UF-02 — Validate on blur for single-field rules and on submit for cross-field rules, never on keystroke; on success the form resets and a success toast (auto-dismiss 4–8 s, top-right) confirms."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R13
    name: 'Message sent!' confirmation page echoing what you sent
    text: "F-03 / UF-03 — On successful submit, route to a confirmation page with a 'Message sent!' heading echoing Name, Email, Category and Comment read-only, clear the form, and offer a control to send another."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R14
    name: Sending an enquiry feels instant
    text: "§6.6.2 — Form submit → confirmation in ≤ 1 s."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R15
    name: 'My messages' list of your own enquiries
    text: "F-04 — A Visitor may view a read-only list of the Enquiries they submitted, with category, status and submitted date."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R16
    name: Visitors only ever see their own enquiries
    text: "BR-04 / NFR-base-7 (Visitor side) — A Visitor's submissions view shows only Enquiries they submitted; other people's names, emails and addresses are never shown to a Visitor."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R17
    name: Empty 'My messages' state with a link to the Contact form
    text: "UF-06 (Visitor) — No submissions → 'You haven't sent any messages yet' with a link to the Contact form."
    epic: visitor-enquiries
  - id: R18
    name: Inbox of all enquiries, sortable and paged
    text: "F-05 / UF-04 — Support Agent / Admin see all Enquiries in a table with Name, Category, Status and Submitted date; row click opens the detail; single-column sort (ascending then descending); page sizes 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 (default 20); pagination control always shown."
    epic: inbox
  - id: R19
    name: Colour-coded status badges with a text or icon label
    text: "UF-05 — New (blue), In Progress (amber), Resolved (green); colour always paired with an icon or text label."
    epic: inbox
  - id: R20
    name: Filter the Inbox by category, status or text
    text: "F-06 / Search & Filter flow — Filter by Category, Status, and free-text search on Name and Comment; active filters show as chips with Clear-all."
    epic: inbox
  - id: R21
    name: Inbox 'No enquiries yet' and 'no results' states
    text: "UF-06 (Inbox) — Zero data → 'No enquiries yet'; zero results after filtering → no-results state with active filter chips and Clear-all, no creation call-to-action."
    epic: inbox
  - id: R22
    name: Inbox loads quickly
    text: "§6.6.2 — Inbox page interactive at p95 ≤ 2 s with 100 rows."
    epic: inbox
  - id: R23
    name: Enquirer contact details visible only to Support Agents and Admins
    text: "§6.6.1 / NFR-base-7 (back-office side) — Name, Email and Address are visible only to authenticated back-office roles; a Visitor cannot reach the Inbox."
    epic: inbox
  - id: R24
    name: Enquiry detail page
    text: "Inbox flow step 3 / §7 — Opening an inbox row shows the Enquiry detail: Name, Email, Address, Category, Comment, Status and Submitted date."
    epic: enquiry-handling
  - id: R25
    name: Mark an enquiry In Progress
    text: "F-07 — A Support Agent or Admin may move a non-terminal Enquiry from New to In Progress; status updates with a toast confirmation; HandledBy is recorded when status first changes."
    epic: enquiry-handling
  - id: R26
    name: Resolve an enquiry with a required Reply Note
    text: "F-08 / BR-02 / UF-07 / §6.3 — Resolving opens a modal with a mandatory multi-line Reply Note (max 1000 characters, with a character counter); the submit control stays disabled until a note is entered; status becomes Resolved with a toast."
    epic: enquiry-handling
  - id: R27
    name: Resolved enquiries can't be changed and show their Reply Note
    text: "BR-01 / F-10 — When an Enquiry is Resolved, status-change actions are hidden and the Reply Note is shown read-only on the detail."
    epic: enquiry-handling
  - id: R28
    name: Admins can delete an enquiry after confirming
    text: "F-09 / BR-03 / Delete flow — Admin-only Delete on an inbox row or the detail; a confirmation modal names the Enquiry, uses a destructive-styled primary button and puts default focus on Cancel; the Enquiry is then removed. Support Agents never see Delete."
    epic: enquiry-handling
  - id: R29
    name: Icon-only buttons have hover labels
    text: "UF-08 — Icon-only row actions carry tooltips on hover and focus plus a matching accessible label; primary destructive actions are never icon-only."
    epic: enquiry-handling

epics:
  - slug: sign-in-and-app-shell
    name: Sign-in and App Shell
    goal: Everyone signs in with email and password, lands on the right page for their role, sees only the menu items their role allows, and gets a clear on-page message if they open a page they can't use.
    requirementIds: [R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8]
    dependsOn: []
  - slug: visitor-enquiries
    name: Contact Form and My Messages
    goal: A Visitor sends an enquiry, sees a 'Message sent!' confirmation of what they sent, and can look back over their own messages (and only theirs).
    requirementIds: [R9, R10, R11, R12, R13, R14, R15, R16, R17]
    dependsOn: [sign-in-and-app-shell]
  - slug: inbox
    name: Inbox
    goal: Support Agents and Admins see every enquiry in one sortable, paged table and can narrow it down by category, status or text.
    requirementIds: [R18, R19, R20, R21, R22, R23]
    dependsOn: [sign-in-and-app-shell]
  - slug: enquiry-handling
    name: Working an Enquiry
    goal: Support Agents and Admins open an enquiry, mark it In Progress, and resolve it with a Reply Note; Admins can also delete spam after confirming.
    requirementIds: [R24, R25, R26, R27, R28, R29]
    dependsOn: [inbox]

coverage:
  total: 29
  assigned: 29
  unassigned: []
  droppedByUserDecision: []
  droppedByUserDecisionNotes: []

blockers:
  - kind: conflict
    requirements: [R6, R16, R23]
    whatYouAskedFor: "_Role switcher for reviewers_ (R6), alongside _Visitors only ever see their own enquiries_ (R16) and _Enquirer contact details visible only to Support Agents and Admins_ (R23)"
    theSnag: "The spec asks for a role switcher on every shared screen so reviewers can flip between Visitor, Support Agent and Admin without signing in again. But at intake we set the app up with real sign-in for three separate users, and promised that a Visitor never sees anyone else's name, email or address. If any signed-in person can switch themselves to Admin, a Visitor could open the Inbox and see everyone's personal details — which breaks that promise and makes sign-in pointless."
    whatISuggest: "Leave the role switcher out. Reviewers can see each role's view by signing in as the three seeded users (visitor@, agent@ and admin@example.com). That keeps the privacy rules intact, and the menu and permission rules still get checked for every role."
    options:
      - "Leave the role switcher out; reviewers sign in as each seeded user"
      - "Add the switcher, but only in a separate demo mode that is off by default"

81:## Editable HTML Review Page (plan approvals)
82-
83-At **both plan approvals** — the **epic-plan approval** ([`start.md` §8b](../commands/start.md), on `main`) and the per-epic **stories approval** ([`continue.md` §P2](../commands/continue.md), on the `epic/<slug>` branch) — in addition to the in-chat summary, render the review page with a script and open it in the external browser. This is the user's preferred way to review and approve a plan.
84-
85-**You build the payload; the script builds the page.** Layout, editing controls, reordering, the collapsed detail disclosures, the clipboard hand-off and the visual style are all fixed — don't hand-write a page.
86-
87:Write the payload with `Write`, to `review-payload.json` beside the page (both names are git-ignored):
88-
89-```bash
90-# epic-plan approval (on main)
91:node .claude/scripts/render-epic-plan-review.js --in generated-docs/review-payload.json \
92-  --out generated-docs/epic-plan-review.html
93-
94-# stories approval (on the epic branch; /plan passes its worktree path to --out instead)
95:node .claude/scripts/render-stories-review.js --in generated-docs/epics/<slug>/review-payload.json \
96-  --out generated-docs/epics/<slug>/stories-review.html
97-
98-node .claude/scripts/open-page.js "<the --out path>"
99-```
100-
101-`--in` is required (`--in -` reads the payload from stdin). Each script resolves a relative `--out` against the repo root and prints `{"status":"ok","page":"…"}`. Payload shapes are documented in each script's header comment. On script failure, output a one-liner and fall back to the in-chat approval. Open in the **external browser** (`open-page.js`), never the VS Code Simple Browser — the embedded webview blocks clipboard-copy and downloads, and can't be auto-opened.
102-
103-**What the payload must carry (this part is your judgment):**
104-
105-1. **Only what the user decides at this approval** — the epic list, or the one epic and its stories. Never completed or unplanned epics. At the **stories** approval, roadmap context goes in `position` (`{ index, total, completed }`), which becomes a header pill and a progress bar; nothing more. (The epic-plan page has no `position` — it *is* the whole plan, and titles its own pill from the epic count.) The page is a focused decision surface.
106-2. **Plain, user-facing language** — the planner's Translation Rule already produced it. No coverage tags, requirement IDs, `targetFile`, or routes. Give each story a plain `scopeCue` ("New screen", "Updates the Transactions page") and its `roles`; the real route still travels in the approval payload for the build, not on the page.
107-3. **Design choices — only the ones that genuinely need the user.** Omit a decision if **either** holds: you're ≥80% sure of the right answer (pick it, apply it as a default), or it's answerable from the design source, brief, design system, or sample data (follow that source). What's left — genuinely open, consequential, unresolved by any source — is the only thing worth asking. If that set is empty, send `designChoices: []` and no section renders. Don't manufacture choices, don't pad with formatting the design system already governs, and don't re-ask what an earlier epic settled. Tell the user briefly which defaults you applied and why.
108-
109-   **Give each option a real, rendered example — not just a label.** Author a small mockup per option in `options[].previewHtml`, using realistic sample data and the already-applied format defaults (an actual mini table, the real interaction wired up). A one-word label isn't enough for a decision that genuinely needs attention. This is the one part of the page that can't be templated, which is why it travels as data.
110-
111-   **Name your recommendation in `recommended`** (the label of the option you'd pick). The script renders it pre-selected, so a user who agrees can approve without touching anything.
112-
113-When the user approves, fold any `designChoices` into the per-story context the developer receives (and, if a choice resolves a spec gap or sets a cross-epic convention, record it in the epic's `brief.md` — or `project.md` for a project-wide convention — so later epics stay consistent). **A choice that answers an open design-digest Uncertainty is also recorded in the digest's Your Decisions section** — see below.
114-
115-Both pages and both payloads are git-ignored and regenerable.
116-
117-## Recording a decision that overrides the design
118-
119-**Only applies when a design digest exists** (`generated-docs/design/digest.md`) — skip entirely on projects with no design. The orchestrator writes these; no agent does.
120-
121-**Why this exists.** The digest is what the developer builds every screen from, and it's re-read from `documentation/` whenever the design changes. So anything the user settled that *isn't in their design files* has to live in the digest itself — otherwise the next read finds the design's version and quietly rebuilds the screen back to it, undoing what they asked for.
122-
123-**Where.** The **Your Decisions** section at the top of `generated-docs/design/digest.md`. The interpreter always writes that section, so it's normally there to append to — replace its "nothing yet" line with your first bullet. (On a digest written before this existed, add the section above `Screens` yourself.)
124-
125-```markdown
--
151:node .claude/scripts/render-manual-tests.js --in generated-docs/epics/<slug>/review-payload.json \
152-  --out generated-docs/epics/<slug>/manual-tests.html
153-node .claude/scripts/open-page.js "generated-docs/epics/<slug>/manual-tests.html"
154-```
155-
156-
157-**What the payload must carry (this part is your judgment):**
158-
159-1. **The check-these-first ledger.** Pass `state.json.epic.unverifiedAssumptions` as `unverifiedAssumptions`; the script renders it above everything else, because these are the real-backend assumptions the automated tests couldn't verify. Omit the field when the array is empty. Each item is a plain string, or `{ text, priorPassed }` when a re-display needs to carry a confirmed one forward (step 5).
160-2. **Order the groups to minimise persona-switching.** The script renders the order you give it. Group all same-role checks together and put the single sign-out/sign-in for another role in **one** section at the end — never make the user log in and out repeatedly. Consolidate repeated negative checks ("role X can't see Y") into one short section rather than repeating them per story.
161-3. **One crisp *do this → expect that* line per check**, in plain language.
162-4. **Attach setup to the check it belongs to**, via that check's `setup` field — never a page-level banner the reader has to connect to the right test. When several checks share a setup, put it on the first and have the rest point at it. Where the values are already documented canonically — `web/.env.example`, the story file, the e2e spec — point there rather than restating them, so the hint can't drift from its source.
163-5. **Pre-tick from prior results on a re-display.** After a fix cycle, set `priorPassed: true` on every check whose prior result in `state.json.epic.manualTestResults` was `passed: true`, leaving **only the affected checks** unticked — the reported failure(s), every check belonging to a re-entered story, and (for a contract correction) the failed assumption plus the consuming stories' checks. Ledger items take it too, as `{ text, priorPassed }`, so a confirmed assumption doesn't come back unticked. On first display, send no `priorPassed` at all.
164-6. **`appUrl`** renders the "Open the app" button; **`logins`** renders one click-to-copy chip per role. Omit `logins` unless you have real sign-in details to copy.
165-
166-**Orchestrator handling of the result:** `allPassed: true` (or `all passed`) → mark the epic manual-test passed and transition to `COMPLETE-ON-BRANCH`. Otherwise → route each `failed` item (its `comment` + `story`) through the existing [§B7.1 fix-cycle integration](../commands/continue.md#fix-cycle-integration), re-rendering the page after the fix. Each item's `kind` says which branch it takes — `"assumption"` is a ledger item (data-contract failure, `story` is `null`), `"story"` is a per-story check. A non-empty `todo` is **not** a bug report — those checks have nothing to act on; ask the user whether they still want to run them or move on. Skip the page only for infrastructure-only stories / legacy epics, as today.
167-
168-## Visual Style and Page Wording
169-
170-Owned by [`lib/review-page.js`](../scripts/lib/review-page.js) and the three renderers, shared by all three pages — light, calm and airy, one accent colour, soft cards whose shadow deepens on hover (nothing moves), a short framing header with a progress bar, fully self-contained (no CDN, no external assets). To change how every review page feels, change that module; never restyle a single generated file.
171-
172-**The pages' own wording is fixed in the renderers too** — headings, button labels, the "tick what works" instructions — so you don't re-derive it per run; the text you write at an approval is the *in-chat* summary and the payload. If a user asks for different wording **on the page**, change the renderer so every future page carries it, rather than editing one generated file.

* render-epic-plan-review.js
 *
 * Renders the editable epic-plan review page shown at the INTAKE approval
 * (commands/start.md Step 8b), from the blocker-free DECOMPOSITION PROPOSAL.
 *

content.content:
1	# Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	A contact-and-enquiry app where a Visitor sends an enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and gets confirmation straight away. Back-office staff work through the enquiries: a Support Agent moves each one through New, In Progress and Resolved, and an Admin can also delete enquiries. Enquiries are scoped by role, so a Visitor sees only their own.
4	
5	| Field | Value |
6	|---|---|
7	| Project slug | `contact-form` |
8	| Created | 2026-11-03T07:17:19Z |
9	| Intake source | docs (`documentation/requirements.md`) |
10	| Backend connectivity | mock-only |
11	
12	---
13

6	
7	## 1. Application context
8	
9	**Name:** Contact & Enquiry Management
10	
11	**Purpose / business value:** Let a **Visitor** send a contact enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and receive immediate confirmation, while giving back-office staff a triage surface: a **Support Agent** works enquiries through a status lifecycle, and an **Admin** additionally curates the inbox (delete spam, reassign). A single public form feeds a role-gated review workflow.
12	
13	**Domain:** Generic customer-support / contact-us, applicable to any organisation that fields public enquiries.
14	
15	**Business goal:** Capture every enquiry with a confirmed hand-off, and ensure each one reaches a terminal, auditable state (Resolved with a reply note) without a Visitor ever seeing another person's enquiry or the back-office surfaces.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 2. Domain model
20	
21	> The business domain in **ubiquitous language**, implementation-free.
22	
23	### 2.1 Concepts
24	
25	| Concept          | Persistence | Definition (ubiquitous language) |
26	| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
27	| Enquiry          | persistent  | A contact message submitted by a Visitor, carrying contact details, a category, a comment, and its handling state. |
28	| User             | persistent  | An authenticated actor of the system, identified by email and bearing one of the system's roles. |
29	| Enquiry Status   | derived     | The lifecycle position of an Enquiry — `New`, `In Progress`, or `Resolved` — that gates the actions back-office roles may take. |
30	| Category         | enum        | The nature of an Enquiry as chosen by the Visitor — `Feedback`, `Question`, or `General Enquiry`. |
31	| Reply Note       | attribute   | The free-text response captured by a back-office role when an Enquiry is moved to `Resolved`. |
32	
33	### 2.2 Relationships
34	
35	- **User** *submits* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Visitor only
36	- **User** *handles* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Support Agent / Admin only
37	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Enquiry Status** [1 : 1]
38	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Category** [1 : 1]
39	
40	### 2.3 Aggregates & lifecycles
41	
42	#### Enquiry
43	
44	| Field            | Value |
45	| ---------------- | ----- |
46	| Member concepts  | Enquiry, Enquiry Status, Category, Reply Note |
47	| Lifecycle states | `New` → `In Progress` → `Resolved` — terminal state is `Resolved`; once terminal, status does not change. |
48	| Key invariants   | Status-change actions are available only while the Enquiry is non-terminal. Moving an Enquiry to `Resolved` requires a non-empty Reply Note. A Visitor may read only Enquiries they submitted. |

244	## 6. Requirements
245	
246	### 6.1 Functional
247	
248	- F-01 The system supports email-and-password authentication and routes the user to a role-specific landing surface on success.
249	- F-02 A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category, and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created in `New`.
250	- F-03 On successful submit, the system routes to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details, clears the form, and shows a "Message sent!" confirmation.
251	- F-04 A Visitor may view a read-only list of the Enquiries they submitted, and only those.
252	- F-05 A Support Agent or Admin may view all Enquiries in a sortable, paginated table.
253	- F-06 A Support Agent or Admin may filter Enquiries by Category, Status, and free-text search on Name and Comment.
254	- F-07 A Support Agent or Admin may move a non-terminal Enquiry from `New` to `In Progress`.
255	- F-08 A Support Agent or Admin may resolve a non-terminal Enquiry by submitting a non-empty Reply Note, transitioning it to `Resolved`.
256	- F-09 An Admin may delete an Enquiry.
257	- F-10 The system surfaces the Reply Note read-only on a `Resolved` Enquiry's detail.
258	
259	### 6.2 Business rules
260	
261	| ID | Statement (when / then) | Enforcement point | Severity |
262	| ---- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | -------- |
263	| BR-01 | When an Enquiry's Status is `Resolved`, then status-change actions must be hidden in the UI. | UI | blocker |
264	| BR-02 | When a back-office user resolves an Enquiry, then a non-empty Reply Note must be submitted; the submit control is disabled until a note is entered. | UI | blocker |
265	| BR-03 | When a destructive Delete is triggered, then a confirmation modal naming the Enquiry must be shown before removal. | UI | blocker |
266	| BR-04 | When a Visitor views their submissions, then only Enquiries they submitted may be shown. | UI | blocker |
267	| BR-05 | When a user without access reaches a role-restricted surface via a direct link, then an in-page permission-denied banner must be shown (never a generic 403 page). | UI | major |
268	| BR-06 | When the Contact form is submitted, then Email must match a valid email format and Comment must be non-empty (min 10 characters). | UI | major |
269	
270	### 6.3 Data
271	
272	- The Enquiry record carries the fields enumerated on the §7 Enquiry entity.
273	- Enquiry Status enum values are exactly `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved`.
274	- Category enum values are exactly `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry`.
275	- Reply Note is required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 characters.
276	
277	### 6.4 User-facing
278	
279	- UF-01 The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select), and Comment (multi-line) with a leading-asterisk convention on required fields and a single legend line.
280	- UF-02 Forms validate on blur for synchronous rules (format, required, length) and on submit for cross-field rules; never on keystroke. On success, the form resets and a success toast (auto-dismiss 4–8 s, top-right) confirms.
281	- UF-03 The confirmation page echoes the submitted Name, Email, Category, and Comment read-only, with a "Message sent!" heading and a control to send another.
282	- UF-04 The Inbox table renders Name, Category, Status, Submitted date, with a row-click to detail and (Admin-only) a Delete row action. Pagination ladder 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 (default 20); single-column sort, ascending then descending; the pagination control is always rendered.
283	- UF-05 Status badges colour-map: `New` (info / blue), `In Progress` (in-progress / amber), `Resolved` (success / green). Colour is always paired with an icon or text label; never relied on alone.
284	- UF-06 Empty states distinguish zero-data ("No enquiries yet" / "You haven't sent any messages yet") from zero-results-of-filter (active filter chips + Clear-all, no creation CTA).
285	- UF-07 The Resolve modal displays a mandatory Reply Note text field (multi-line) with a character counter and a clear ceiling.
286	- UF-08 Icon-only row actions carry tooltips on hover and focus plus an `aria-label` matching the tooltip; primary destructive actions are never icon-only.
287	- UF-09 Denied-access surfaces render an in-page permission-denied banner naming the missing permission and a path back to the user's own surface.
288	- UF-10 Top-level navigation is role-scoped: Visitor sees Contact + My messages; Agent/Admin see Inbox; Admin additionally sees Delete affordances.

345	| HandledBy | string | no | mirrors the acting back-office user | Set when status first changes; audit. |
346	
347	**Enums:** `Status` ∈ { `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` }; `Category` ∈ { `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` }
348	
349	### Entity: User
350	
351	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
352	| ----- | ---- | -------- | ---------- | ----- |
353	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier. |
354	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Login identifier. |
355	| FirstName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | Greeting / detail. |
356	| LastName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | Greeting / detail. |
357	| Password | string | yes | min complexity per policy | Write-only; never displayed. |
358	| Role | enum | yes | one of `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` | Drives post-login routing and RBAC. |
359	
360	**Enums:** `Role` ∈ { `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` }
361	
362	---
363	
364	## 8. Key terminology
365	
366	| Term | Definition |
367	| ---- | ---------- |
368	| Enquiry | A contact message submitted by a Visitor. → §2.1. |
369	| Visitor | The role that submits enquiries and views their own. → §3. |
370	| Support Agent | The role that triages and resolves enquiries. → §3. |
371	| Admin | The role that can do everything an Agent can, plus delete. → §3. |
372	| Reply Note | The free-text response captured when an Enquiry is resolved. → §2.1. |
373	| New / In Progress / Resolved | The Enquiry lifecycle states; `Resolved` is terminal. |
374	
375	---
376	
377	## 9. Volumes
378	
379	| Metric | Value | Source |
380	| ------ | ----- | ------ |
381	| Data volume | 10¹–10³ enquiries in scope for the prototype. | inferred |
382	| Frequency | Sporadic submissions; daily back-office triage. | inferred |
383	| Concurrency | 1–5 concurrent back-office users; small team. | inferred |
384	
385	---
386	
387	## Prototype invariants
388	
389	### PI-01 — Server behaviour is simulated
390	All server-side behaviour — authentication, API calls, persistence, email — is simulated by client-side stubs. Backend-shaped requirements describe user-visible behaviour, not real implementation.
391	
392	### PI-02 — Data is fixture-backed
393	All data is sourced from in-memory fixtures shipped with the build. Mutations persist within a session but do not survive a reload unless a "demo data" mode is specified. There is no real database.
394	
395	### PI-03 — Validation is visual only
396	Form-field validation and inline errors are rendered as specified, but no server-side enforcement is exercised.
397	
398	### PI-04 — Third-party integrations are visual
399	Any email/notification on submit or resolve appears as a UI confirmation only; no external network calls are made.
400	
401	### PI-05 — Role switcher
402	Every screen accessible to more than one role displays a role switcher in the prototype's surrounding chrome — outside the application UI under design — so reviewers can inspect each role's view without re-authenticating. It lists every role in §3; roles to whom the active screen is not accessible per §6.5 are shown disabled. Switching the active role immediately updates the screen's visible components and actions to match the requirements (RBAC entries, conditional visibility, role-gated actions).

1	# Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	A contact-and-enquiry app where a Visitor sends an enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and gets confirmation straight away. Back-office staff work through the enquiries: a Support Agent moves each one through New, In Progress and Resolved, and an Admin can also delete enquiries. Enquiries are scoped by role, so a Visitor sees only their own.
4	
5	| Field | Value |
6	|---|---|
7	| Project slug | `contact-form` |
8	| Created | 2026-11-03T07:17:19Z |
9	| Intake source | docs (`documentation/requirements.md`) |
10	| Backend connectivity | mock-only |
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Roles & Permissions
15	
16	**Template:** `custom`
17	
18	| Permission | Visitor | Support Agent | Admin |
19	|---|---|---|---|
20	| View main dashboard | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
21	
22	**Role definitions** (from intake and `requirements.md` §3 / §6.5):
23	
24	- **Visitor:** can sign in, submit an enquiry and view their own submissions (read-only). Lands on the Contact form. Cannot see the Inbox or other people's enquiries, and cannot change status or delete.
25	- **Support Agent:** can view all enquiries, search and filter them, move status from New to In Progress to Resolved, and resolve an enquiry with a mandatory reply note. Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form or delete.
26	- **Admin:** has every Support Agent permission and can also delete an enquiry (behind a confirmation). Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form.
27	
28	Denied actions are **hidden** in the UI, not shown as disabled. Opening a role-restricted page through a direct link shows a permission-denied banner on the page, not a generic 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05 / UF-09).
29	
30	> Permissions extend during BUILD as new stories surface new actions. Additions are recorded here as they come up, with your approval. Removing a permission, or changing who the roles are, stops for you to review.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Authentication
35	
36	| Field | Value |
37	|---|---|
38	| Method | `server-side` (BFF: your own server) |
39	| Auth login endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Auth is simulated by client-side stubs (`requirements.md` PI-01); no real backend endpoint |
40	| Auth userinfo endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
41	| Auth logout endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
42	| Custom auth notes | Auth is simulated client-side, as the prototype invariants require. The BFF shape follows the template's server-side auth policy. Sign-in uses email and password, then sends each role to its landing page (Visitor to the Contact form; Support Agent and Admin to the Inbox). Seeded users: `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin). |
43	
44	> Auth method is never inferred — the user must confirm explicitly per [authentication-intake.md](.claude/policies/authentication-intake.md).
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Data Source & Backend Integration
49	
50	| Field | Value |
51	|---|---|
52	| Data source | `mock-only` |
53	| Backend status | `N/A` (none) |
54	| Mock layer required | yes. In-memory fixtures built from `requirements.md`: a few seeded enquiries covering all three categories (Feedback / Question / General Enquiry) and all three statuses (New / In Progress / Resolved), plus the three seeded users. Changes last for the session but not past a reload (PI-02). Emails and notifications show only as UI confirmations (PI-04). |
55	
56	### API specs
57	
58	No OpenAPI spec was provided. The domain entities (Enquiry, User) are defined in `documentation/requirements.md` §7.
59	
60	---
61	
62	## Compliance
63	
64	**Applicable domains:** None (the user confirmed the project is not regulated)
65	**Region (if Personal data applies):** N/A
66	
67	### Compliance Requirements
68	
69	No compliance domains were identified during intake screening.
70	
71	- Note: the app does collect personal data (name, email, optional address). Only authenticated back-office roles (Support Agent, Admin) can see enquiries. Visitors never see anyone else's (`requirements.md` §6.6.1, BR-04).
72	
73	---
74	
75	## Styling & Branding
76	
77	| Field | Value |
78	|---|---|
79	| Primary brand color | `#2563eb` [INFERRED] the user asked for template defaults with no bespoke design system, so this is the styling-centralisation Pattern A default (Tailwind blue-600) |
80	| Accent / secondary | `#64748b` [INFERRED] a neutral accent from Tailwind `slate`, per the Pattern A default |
81	| Background (light) | `#ffffff` [INFERRED] the default for a neutral light palette |
82	| Background (dark, if applicable) | N/A |
83	| Font family (headings) | [INFERRED] system UI stack (Pattern A default; no font named in the sources) |
84	| Font family (body) | [INFERRED] system UI stack (Pattern A default; no font named in the sources) |
85	| Theme | [INFERRED] light only (Pattern A default; dark mode can be added later) |
86	| Source | defaulted (user: "template Shadcn defaults with a clean, neutral palette and centralised styling tokens") |
87	
88	> Component-specific styling (button radii, card shadows, etc.) emerges during BUILD. This section captures only palette intent and typography per [styling-centralisation.md](.claude/policies/styling-centralisation.md).
89	
90	---
91	
92	## Baseline NFRs
93	
94	- **NFR-base-1:** Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 Level AA (`requirements.md` §6.6.3 raises this above the 2.1 AA baseline). Primary flows are keyboard-first, status colour is always paired with an icon or text, and icon-only controls have a tooltip and an `aria-label`
95	- **NFR-base-2:** Performance: First Contentful Paint < 2.5s on a mid-tier mobile network
96	- **NFR-base-3:** Responsive design: mobile (≥360px) / tablet (≥768px) / desktop (≥1280px) breakpoints
97	- **NFR-base-4:** Browser support: latest two versions of Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari
98	- **NFR-base-5:** Error UX: every async operation shows a visible error state with a way to retry
99	- **NFR-base-6:** [INFERRED] Session policy: 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout, and lockout for 15 minutes after 5 failed sign-in attempts. Carried over from `requirements.md` §6.6.1, which marks these values as inferred. Auth is simulated (PI-01), so this behaviour is shown in the UI only
100	- **NFR-base-7:** Personal-data visibility: an enquirer's name, email and address are shown only to authenticated back-office roles and never to other Visitors (`requirements.md` §6.6.1, confirmed at intake)

1	# Requirements: Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	**Domain:** Customer support — public enquiry capture and back-office triage **Created:** 2026-07-23 **Status:** final
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Application context
8	
9	**Name:** Contact & Enquiry Management
10	
11	**Purpose / business value:** Let a **Visitor** send a contact enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and receive immediate confirmation, while giving back-office staff a triage surface: a **Support Agent** works enquiries through a status lifecycle, and an **Admin** additionally curates the inbox (delete spam, reassign). A single public form feeds a role-gated review workflow.
12	
13	**Domain:** Generic customer-support / contact-us, applicable to any organisation that fields public enquiries.
14	
15	**Business goal:** Capture every enquiry with a confirmed hand-off, and ensure each one reaches a terminal, auditable state (Resolved with a reply note) without a Visitor ever seeing another person's enquiry or the back-office surfaces.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 2. Domain model
20	
21	> The business domain in **ubiquitous language**, implementation-free.
22	
23	### 2.1 Concepts
24	
25	| Concept          | Persistence | Definition (ubiquitous language) |
26	| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |

182	
183	| Field | Value |
184	| ----- | ----- |
185	| Actor | Visitor |
186	| Trigger | Visitor wants to contact the organisation. |
187	| Steps | 1. Open the Contact form. 2. Enter Name, Email, optional Address, choose a Category, enter a Comment. 3. Submit. 4. System creates an Enquiry in `New`. 5. Route to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details; the form is cleared; a "Message sent!" confirmation shows. |

193	
194	| Field | Value |
195	| ----- | ----- |
196	| Actor | Visitor |

244	## 6. Requirements
245	
246	### 6.1 Functional
247	
248	- F-01 The system supports email-and-password authentication and routes the user to a role-specific landing surface on success.
249	- F-02 A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category, and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created in `New`.
250	- F-03 On successful submit, the system routes to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details, clears the form, and shows a "Message sent!" confirmation.
251	- F-04 A Visitor may view a read-only list of the Enquiries they submitted, and only those.
252	- F-05 A Support Agent or Admin may view all Enquiries in a sortable, paginated table.
253	- F-06 A Support Agent or Admin may filter Enquiries by Category, Status, and free-text search on Name and Comment.
254	- F-07 A Support Agent or Admin may move a non-terminal Enquiry from `New` to `In Progress`.
255	- F-08 A Support Agent or Admin may resolve a non-terminal Enquiry by submitting a non-empty Reply Note, transitioning it to `Resolved`.
256	- F-09 An Admin may delete an Enquiry.
257	- F-10 The system surfaces the Reply Note read-only on a `Resolved` Enquiry's detail.
258	
259	### 6.2 Business rules
260	
261	| ID | Statement (when / then) | Enforcement point | Severity |
262	| ---- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | -------- |
263	| BR-01 | When an Enquiry's Status is `Resolved`, then status-change actions must be hidden in the UI. | UI | blocker |
264	| BR-02 | When a back-office user resolves an Enquiry, then a non-empty Reply Note must be submitted; the submit control is disabled until a note is entered. | UI | blocker |
265	| BR-03 | When a destructive Delete is triggered, then a confirmation modal naming the Enquiry must be shown before removal. | UI | blocker |
266	| BR-04 | When a Visitor views their submissions, then only Enquiries they submitted may be shown. | UI | blocker |
267	| BR-05 | When a user without access reaches a role-restricted surface via a direct link, then an in-page permission-denied banner must be shown (never a generic 403 page). | UI | major |
268	| BR-06 | When the Contact form is submitted, then Email must match a valid email format and Comment must be non-empty (min 10 characters). | UI | major |
269	
270	### 6.3 Data
271	
272	- The Enquiry record carries the fields enumerated on the §7 Enquiry entity.
273	- Enquiry Status enum values are exactly `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved`.
274	- Category enum values are exactly `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry`.
275	- Reply Note is required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 characters.
276	
277	### 6.4 User-facing
278	
279	- UF-01 The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select), and Comment (multi-line) with a leading-asterisk convention on required fields and a single legend line.
280	- UF-02 Forms validate on blur for synchronous rules (format, required, length) and on submit for cross-field rules; never on keystroke. On success, the form resets and a success toast (auto-dismiss 4–8 s, top-right) confirms.
281	- UF-03 The confirmation page echoes the submitted Name, Email, Category, and Comment read-only, with a "Message sent!" heading and a control to send another.
282	- UF-04 The Inbox table renders Name, Category, Status, Submitted date, with a row-click to detail and (Admin-only) a Delete row action. Pagination ladder 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 (default 20); single-column sort, ascending then descending; the pagination control is always rendered.
283	- UF-05 Status badges colour-map: `New` (info / blue), `In Progress` (in-progress / amber), `Resolved` (success / green). Colour is always paired with an icon or text label; never relied on alone.
284	- UF-06 Empty states distinguish zero-data ("No enquiries yet" / "You haven't sent any messages yet") from zero-results-of-filter (active filter chips + Clear-all, no creation CTA).
285	- UF-07 The Resolve modal displays a mandatory Reply Note text field (multi-line) with a character counter and a clear ceiling.
286	- UF-08 Icon-only row actions carry tooltips on hover and focus plus an `aria-label` matching the tooltip; primary destructive actions are never icon-only.
287	- UF-09 Denied-access surfaces render an in-page permission-denied banner naming the missing permission and a path back to the user's own surface.
288	- UF-10 Top-level navigation is role-scoped: Visitor sees Contact + My messages; Agent/Admin see Inbox; Admin additionally sees Delete affordances.
