387	## Prototype invariants
388	
389	### PI-01 — Server behaviour is simulated
390	All server-side behaviour — authentication, API calls, persistence, email — is simulated by client-side stubs. Backend-shaped requirements describe user-visible behaviour, not real implementation.
391	
392	### PI-02 — Data is fixture-backed
393	All data is sourced from in-memory fixtures shipped with the build. Mutations persist within a session but do not survive a reload unless a "demo data" mode is specified. There is no real database.
394	
395	### PI-03 — Validation is visual only
396	Form-field validation and inline errors are rendered as specified, but no server-side enforcement is exercised.
397	
398	### PI-04 — Third-party integrations are visual
399	Any email/notification on submit or resolve appears as a UI confirmation only; no external network calls are made.
400	
401	### PI-05 — Role switcher
402	Every screen accessible to more than one role displays a role switcher in the prototype's surrounding chrome — outside the application UI under design — so reviewers can inspect each role's view without re-authenticating. It lists every role in §3; roles to whom the active screen is not accessible per §6.5 are shown disabled. Switching the active role immediately updates the screen's visible components and actions to match the requirements (RBAC entries, conditional visibility, role-gated actions).

Back-office staff work through the enquiries: a Support Agent moves each one through New, In Progress and Resolved, and an Admin can also delete enquiries. 1	# Requirements: Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	**Domain:** Customer support — public enquiry capture and back-office triage **Created:** 2026-07-23 **Status:** final
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Application context
8	
9	**Name:** Contact & Enquiry Management
10	
11	**Purpose / business value:** Let a **Visitor** send a contact enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and receive immediate confirmation, while giving back-office staff a triage surface: a **Support Agent** works enquiries through a status lifecycle, and an **Admin** additionally curates the inbox (delete spam, reassign). A single public form feeds a role-gated review workflow.
12	
13	**Domain:** Generic customer-support / contact-us, applicable to any organisation that fields public enquiries.
14	
15	**Business goal:** Capture every enquiry with a confirmed hand-off, and ensure each one reaches a terminal, auditable state (Resolved with a reply note) without a Visitor ever seeing another person's enquiry or the back-office surfaces.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 2. Domain model
20	
21	> The business domain in **ubiquitous language**, implementation-free.
22	
23	### 2.1 Concepts
24	
25	| Concept          | Persistence | Definition (ubiquitous language) |
26	| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
27	| Enquiry          | persistent  | A contact message submitted by a Visitor, carrying contact details, a category, a comment, and its handling state. |
28	| User             | persistent  | An authenticated actor of the system, identified by email and bearing one of the system's roles. |
29	| Enquiry Status   | derived     | The lifecycle position of an Enquiry — `New`, `In Progress`, or `Resolved` — that gates the actions back-office roles may take. |
30	| Category         | enum        | The nature of an Enquiry as chosen by the Visitor — `Feedback`, `Question`, or `General Enquiry`. |
31	| Reply Note       | attribute   | The free-text response captured by a back-office role when an Enquiry is moved to `Resolved`. |
32	
33	### 2.2 Relationships
34	
35	- **User** *submits* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Visitor only
36	- **User** *handles* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Support Agent / Admin only
37	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Enquiry Status** [1 : 1]
38	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Category** [1 : 1]
39	
40	### 2.3 Aggregates & lifecycles
41	
42	#### Enquiry
43	
44	| Field            | Value |
45	| ---------------- | ----- |
46	| Member concepts  | Enquiry, Enquiry Status, Category, Reply Note |
47	| Lifecycle states | `New` → `In Progress` → `Resolved` — terminal state is `Resolved`; once terminal, status does not change. |
48	| Key invariants   | Status-change actions are available only while the Enquiry is non-terminal. Moving an Enquiry to `Resolved` requires a non-empty Reply Note. A Visitor may read only Enquiries they submitted. |

171	
172	### Flow: Authentication
173	
174	| Field | Value |
175	| ----- | ----- |
176	| Actor | Visitor, Support Agent, or Admin |
177	| Trigger | User opens the application unauthenticated. |
178	| Steps | 1. Enter email + password. 2. Submit. 3. On success, route to the role's landing surface (Visitor → Contact form; Agent/Admin → Inbox). 4. On failure, inline error distinguishing credentials from connectivity. |

182	
183	| Field | Value |
184	| ----- | ----- |
185	| Actor | Visitor |
186	| Trigger | Visitor wants to contact the organisation. |
187	| Steps | 1. Open the Contact form. 2. Enter Name, Email, optional Address, choose a Category, enter a Comment. 3. Submit. 4. System creates an Enquiry in `New`. 5. Route to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details; the form is cleared; a "Message sent!" confirmation shows. |
188	| Decision points | All required fields valid → submit succeeds. Any invalid → inline validation, submit blocked. |

193	
194	| Field | Value |
195	| ----- | ----- |
196	| Actor | Visitor |

244	## 6. Requirements
245	
246	### 6.1 Functional
247	
248	- F-01 The system supports email-and-password authentication and routes the user to a role-specific landing surface on success.
249	- F-02 A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category, and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created in `New`.
250	- F-03 On successful submit, the system routes to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details, clears the form, and shows a "Message sent!" confirmation.
251	- F-04 A Visitor may view a read-only list of the Enquiries they submitted, and only those.
252	- F-05 A Support Agent or Admin may view all Enquiries in a sortable, paginated table.
253	- F-06 A Support Agent or Admin may filter Enquiries by Category, Status, and free-text search on Name and Comment.
254	- F-07 A Support Agent or Admin may move a non-terminal Enquiry from `New` to `In Progress`.
255	- F-08 A Support Agent or Admin may resolve a non-terminal Enquiry by submitting a non-empty Reply Note, transitioning it to `Resolved`.
256	- F-09 An Admin may delete an Enquiry.
257	- F-10 The system surfaces the Reply Note read-only on a `Resolved` Enquiry's detail.
258	
259	### 6.2 Business rules
260	
261	| ID | Statement (when / then) | Enforcement point | Severity |
262	| ---- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | -------- |
263	| BR-01 | When an Enquiry's Status is `Resolved`, then status-change actions must be hidden in the UI. | UI | blocker |
264	| BR-02 | When a back-office user resolves an Enquiry, then a non-empty Reply Note must be submitted; the submit control is disabled until a note is entered. | UI | blocker |
265	| BR-03 | When a destructive Delete is triggered, then a confirmation modal naming the Enquiry must be shown before removal. | UI | blocker |
266	| BR-04 | When a Visitor views their submissions, then only Enquiries they submitted may be shown. | UI | blocker |
267	| BR-05 | When a user without access reaches a role-restricted surface via a direct link, then an in-page permission-denied banner must be shown (never a generic 403 page). | UI | major |
268	| BR-06 | When the Contact form is submitted, then Email must match a valid email format and Comment must be non-empty (min 10 characters). | UI | major |
269	
270	### 6.3 Data
271	
272	- The Enquiry record carries the fields enumerated on the §7 Enquiry entity.
273	- Enquiry Status enum values are exactly `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved`.
274	- Category enum values are exactly `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry`.
275	- Reply Note is required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 characters.
276	
277	### 6.4 User-facing
278	
279	- UF-01 The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select), and Comment (multi-line) with a leading-asterisk convention on required fields and a single legend line.
280	- UF-02 Forms validate on blur for synchronous rules (format, required, length) and on submit for cross-field rules; never on keystroke. On success, the form resets and a success toast (auto-dismiss 4–8 s, top-right) confirms.
281	- UF-03 The confirmation page echoes the submitted Name, Email, Category, and Comment read-only, with a "Message sent!" heading and a control to send another.
282	- UF-04 The Inbox table renders Name, Category, Status, Submitted date, with a row-click to detail and (Admin-only) a Delete row action. Pagination ladder 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 (default 20); single-column sort, ascending then descending; the pagination control is always rendered.
283	- UF-05 Status badges colour-map: `New` (info / blue), `In Progress` (in-progress / amber), `Resolved` (success / green). Colour is always paired with an icon or text label; never relied on alone.
284	- UF-06 Empty states distinguish zero-data ("No enquiries yet" / "You haven't sent any messages yet") from zero-results-of-filter (active filter chips + Clear-all, no creation CTA).
285	- UF-07 The Resolve modal displays a mandatory Reply Note text field (multi-line) with a character counter and a clear ceiling.
286	- UF-08 Icon-only row actions carry tooltips on hover and focus plus an `aria-label` matching the tooltip; primary destructive actions are never icon-only.
287	- UF-09 Denied-access surfaces render an in-page permission-denied banner naming the missing permission and a path back to the user's own surface.
288	- UF-10 Top-level navigation is role-scoped: Visitor sees Contact + My messages; Agent/Admin see Inbox; Admin additionally sees Delete affordances.
289	
290	### 6.5 Access control (RBAC)
291	
292	> Roles-×-resources matrix. **Action vocabulary:** `C` create · `R` read · `U` update · `D` delete · `X` execute · `—` no access. Suffix with a BR ref for conditional access.
293	
294	| Role (→ §3) | Enquiry (entity) | User (entity) | Authentication (flow) | Submit Enquiry (flow) | My Submissions (flow) | Inbox (flow) | Change Status (flow) | Delete Enquiry (flow) | Search & Filter (flow) |
295	| ----------- | ---------------- | ------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- | ------------ | -------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------- |
296	| Visitor       | C R (own)          | R (self) | X | X | R (own) | — | — | — | — |
297	| Support Agent | R U†BR-01          | R (self) | X | — | — | R | X†BR-01,BR-02 | — | X |
298	| Admin         | R U†BR-01 D        | R (self) | X | — | — | R | X†BR-01,BR-02 | X†BR-03 | X |
299	
300	> Notes:
301	> - Denied actions must be **hidden** in the UI, not rendered as disabled controls.
302	> - Direct-link access by a denied persona surfaces the §6.4 UF-09 permission-denied banner, not a 403 page.
303	> - `Enquiry U†BR-01` reflects that a back-office mutation is restricted to Status/Reply Note and gated by BR-01 (must be non-terminal).
304	
305	### 6.6 Non-functional
306	
307	#### 6.6.1 Security & session
308	
309	| Field | Value | Source |
310	| ----- | ----- | ------ |
311	| Idle session timeout | 30 minutes — general web-app default | inferred |
312	| Absolute session timeout | 12 hours | inferred |
313	| Account lockout policy | 5 failed attempts → 15-minute cooldown | inferred |
314	| PII handling | Name, Email, and optional Address are personal data — visible only to authenticated back-office roles; not exposed to other Visitors | inferred |
315	
316	#### 6.6.2 Performance
317	
318	| Metric | Target | Source |
319	| ------ | ------ | ------ |
320	| Page TTI (Inbox, 100 rows) | p95 ≤ 2 s | inferred |
321	| Form submit → confirmation | ≤ 1 s | inferred |
322	
323	#### 6.6.3 Accessibility
324	
325	- Target: WCAG 2.2 AA. Status badges pair colour with icon/text; icon-only controls have tooltips + `aria-label`; keyboard-first operation across all primary flows; the Contact form is fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable.
326	
327	---
328	
329	## 7. Data entities
330	
331	### Entity: Enquiry
332	
333	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
334	| ----- | ---- | -------- | ---------- | ----- |
335	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier. |
336	| Name | string | yes | non-empty; max 120 chars | Displayed as the primary identifier in the inbox. |
337	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | The reply-to; shown on detail. |
338	| Address | string | no | max 255 chars | Optional; shown on detail. |
339	| Category | enum | yes | one of `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` | Displayed as a column and filter. |
340	| Comment | string | yes | non-empty; min 10, max 2000 chars | The enquiry body; shown on detail. |
341	| Status | enum | yes | one of `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` | Displayed as a status badge. |
342	| ReplyNote | string | no | required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 chars | Captured via the Resolve modal; read-only after resolution. |
343	| SubmittedAt | datetime | yes | system-assigned (ISO-8601) | Displayed as the Submitted date column; sortable. |
344	| SubmittedByEmail | string | yes | mirrors submitting Visitor | Scopes "My submissions"; audit. |
345	| HandledBy | string | no | mirrors the acting back-office user | Set when status first changes; audit. |
346	
347	**Enums:** `Status` ∈ { `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` }; `Category` ∈ { `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` }
348	
349	### Entity: User
350	
351	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
352	| ----- | ---- | -------- | ---------- | ----- |
353	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier. |
354	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Login identifier. |
355	| FirstName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | Greeting / detail. |
356	| LastName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | Greeting / detail. |
357	| Password | string | yes | min complexity per policy | Write-only; never displayed. |
358	| Role | enum | yes | one of `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` | Drives post-login routing and RBAC. |
359	
360	**Enums:** `Role` ∈ { `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` }
361	
362	---
363	
364	## 8. Key terminology
365	
366	| Term | Definition |
367	| ---- | ---------- |
368	| Enquiry | A contact message submitted by a Visitor. → §2.1. |
369	| Visitor | The role that submits enquiries and views their own. → §3. |
370	| Support Agent | The role that triages and resolves enquiries. → §3. |
371	| Admin | The role that can do everything an Agent can, plus delete. → §3. |
372	| Reply Note | The free-text response captured when an Enquiry is resolved. → §2.1. |
373	| New / In Progress / Resolved | The Enquiry lifecycle states; `Resolved` is terminal. |
374	
375	---
376	
377	## 9. Volumes
378	
379	| Metric | Value | Source |
380	| ------ | ----- | ------ |
381	| Data volume | 10¹–10³ enquiries in scope for the prototype. | inferred |
382	| Frequency | Sporadic submissions; daily back-office triage. | inferred |
383	| Concurrency | 1–5 concurrent back-office users; small team. | inferred |
384	
385	---
386	
387	## Prototype invariants
388	
389	### PI-01 — Server behaviour is simulated
390	All server-side behaviour — authentication, API calls, persistence, email — is simulated by client-side stubs. Backend-shaped requirements describe user-visible behaviour, not real implementation.
391	
392	### PI-02 — Data is fixture-backed
393	All data is sourced from in-memory fixtures shipped with the build. Mutations persist within a session but do not survive a reload unless a "demo data" mode is specified. There is no real database.
394	
395	### PI-03 — Validation is visual only
396	Form-field validation and inline errors are rendered as specified, but no server-side enforcement is exercised.
397	
398	### PI-04 — Third-party integrations are visual
399	Any email/notification on submit or resolve appears as a UI confirmation only; no external network calls are made.
400	
401	### PI-05 — Role switcher
402	Every screen accessible to more than one role displays a role switcher in the prototype's surrounding chrome — outside the application UI under design — so reviewers can inspect each role's view without re-authenticating. It lists every role in §3; roles to whom the active screen is not accessible per §6.5 are shown disabled. Switching the active role immediately updates the screen's visible components and actions to match the requirements (RBAC entries, conditional visibility, role-gated actions).

2	
3	A contact-and-enquiry app where a Visitor sends an enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and gets confirmation straight away. Back-office staff work through the enquiries: a Support Agent moves each one through New, In Progress and Resolved, and an Admin can also delete enquiries. Enquiries are scoped by role, so a Visitor sees only their own.

1	# Requirements: Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	**Domain:** Customer support — public enquiry capture and back-office triage **Created:** 2026-07-23 **Status:** final
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Application context
8	
9	**Name:** Contact & Enquiry Management
10	
11	**Purpose / business value:** Let a **Visitor** send a contact enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and receive immediate confirmation, while giving back-office staff a triage surface: a **Support Agent** works enquiries through a status lifecycle, and an **Admin** additionally curates the inbox (delete spam, reassign). A single public form feeds a role-gated review workflow.
12	
13	**Domain:** Generic customer-support / contact-us, applicable to any organisation that fields public enquiries.
14	
15	**Business goal:** Capture every enquiry with a confirmed hand-off, and ensure each one reaches a terminal, auditable state (Resolved with a reply note) without a Visitor ever seeing another person's enquiry or the back-office surfaces.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 2. Domain model
20	
21	> The business domain in **ubiquitous language**, implementation-free.
22	
23	### 2.1 Concepts
24	
25	| Concept          | Persistence | Definition (ubiquitous language) |
26	| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
27	| Enquiry          | persistent  | A contact message submitted by a Visitor, carrying contact details, a category, a comment, and its handling state. |
28	| User             | persistent  | An authenticated actor of the system, identified by email and bearing one of the system's roles. |
29	| Enquiry Status   | derived     | The lifecycle position of an Enquiry — `New`, `In Progress`, or `Resolved` — that gates the actions back-office roles may take. |
30	| Category         | enum        | The nature of an Enquiry as chosen by the Visitor — `Feedback`, `Question`, or `General Enquiry`. |
31	| Reply Note       | attribute   | The free-text response captured by a back-office role when an Enquiry is moved to `Resolved`. |
32	
33	### 2.2 Relationships
34	
35	- **User** *submits* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Visitor only
36	- **User** *handles* **Enquiry** [1 : *] — Support Agent / Admin only
37	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Enquiry Status** [1 : 1]
38	- **Enquiry** *carries* **Category** [1 : 1]
39	
40	### 2.3 Aggregates & lifecycles
41	
42	#### Enquiry
43	
44	| Field            | Value |
45	| ---------------- | ----- |
46	| Member concepts  | Enquiry, Enquiry Status, Category, Reply Note |
47	| Lifecycle states | `New` → `In Progress` → `Resolved` — terminal state is `Resolved`; once terminal, status does not change. |
48	| Key invariants   | Status-change actions are available only while the Enquiry is non-terminal. Moving an Enquiry to `Resolved` requires a non-empty Reply Note. A Visitor may read only Enquiries they submitted. |
49	
50	### 2.4 Diagram
51	
52	```mermaid
53	classDiagram
54	    class Enquiry {
55	      +Id
56	      +Name
57	      +Email
58	      +Address
59	      +Category
60	      +Comment
61	      +Status
62	      +ReplyNote
63	      +SubmittedAt
64	      +HandledBy
65	      +changeStatus()
66	      +resolve()
67	    }
68	    class User {
69	      +Email
70	      +FirstName
71	      +LastName
72	      +Role
73	      +login()
74	    }
75	    class EnquiryStatus {
76	      <<enumeration>>
77	      New
78	      InProgress
79	      Resolved
80	    }
81	    class Category {
82	      <<enumeration>>
83	      Feedback
84	      Question
85	      GeneralEnquiry
86	    }
87	
88	    Enquiry "1" --> "1" EnquiryStatus : carries
89	    Enquiry "1" --> "1" Category : carries
90	    User "1" --> "*" Enquiry : submits (Visitor)
91	    User "1" --> "*" Enquiry : handles (Agent/Admin)
92	```
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 3. Target users
97	
98	### Visitor
99	
100	| Field | Value |
101	| ----- | ----- |
102	| Role / job title | A member of the public contacting the organisation. |
103	| Expertise level | None assumed — first-time, occasional user. |
104	| Stakes | Low, but wants confidence the message was received. |
105	| Frequency of use | Rare / one-off. |
106	| Driving forces — wants | A short form, clear confirmation that the message sent, a record of what they submitted. |
107	| Driving forces — fears | Submitting into a void; not knowing if it went through; losing what they typed. |
108	
109	### Support Agent
110	
111	| Field | Value |
112	| ----- | ----- |
113	| Role / job title | Front-line support staff who read and resolve incoming enquiries. |
114	| Expertise level | Comfortable with an inbox / ticket-list workflow. |
115	| Stakes | Medium — a mishandled or lost enquiry is a poor customer experience. |
116	| Frequency of use | Daily — works the inbox throughout the day. |
117	| Driving forces — wants | Fast triage; filter by category and status; a frictionless resolve-with-note path. |
118	| Driving forces — fears | Missing an enquiry; resolving without a recorded reply; losing context across many enquiries. |
119	
120	### Admin
121	
122	| Field | Value |
123	| ----- | ----- |
124	| Role / job title | Support lead responsible for inbox hygiene and oversight. |
125	| Expertise level | Domain-fluent; trusted with destructive actions. |
126	| Stakes | High for delete — removal is irreversible. |
127	| Frequency of use | Occasional — curation rather than day-to-day triage. |
128	| Driving forces — wants | Everything an Agent can do, plus removing spam/duplicates cleanly. |
129	| Driving forces — fears | Deleting a legitimate enquiry by accident. |
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 4. User goals & stories
134	
135	### 4.1 Goals catalogue
136	
137	| ID   | Goal statement | Quality signals | Goal kind | Layout pref | UX-pattern pref |
138	| ---- | -------------- | --------------- | --------- | ----------- | --------------- |
139	| G-01 | Send an enquiry and be sure it was received. | Confidence of completion; visible confirmation; form resets. | top-level | Single-form contact screen | Validated form → confirmation page + success toast |
140	| G-02 | Review what I submitted. | Recall of my own enquiries; read-only clarity. | sub-level | Simple list of my submissions | Read-only cards / table, own-records only |
141	| G-03 | Triage incoming enquiries and drive each to resolution. | Speed of triage; auditability of the reply; terminal-state clarity. | top-level | Inbox table-first surface | Filterable/sortable table with status actions |
142	| G-04 | Find a specific enquiry by category, status, or text. | Recall + precision; clearable filters. | sub-level | Filter bar above the inbox | Category/status chips + free-text search |
143	| G-05 | Keep the inbox clean by removing spam or duplicates. | Safety (confirm before delete); admin-only. | interaction-level | Row action on the inbox | Destructive-confirm modal |
144	| G-06 | Sign in to the right surface for my role. | One step; failure feedback. | top-level | Single login screen | Email + password with role-based routing |
145	
146	### 4.2 Stories by persona
147	
148	#### Visitor
149	
150	- **As a Visitor, I want to submit an enquiry (name, email, optional address, category, comment), so that I can contact the organisation.** → G-01
151	- **As a Visitor, I want a confirmation page showing what I sent, with the form cleared and a "Message sent!" message, so that I know it went through.** → G-01
152	- **As a Visitor, I want to see the enquiries I have submitted (read-only, mine only), so that I can check what I sent.** → G-02
153	- **As a Visitor, I want to sign in and land on the contact surface, so that I don't see back-office screens.** → G-06
154	
155	#### Support Agent
156	
157	- **As a Support Agent, I want a sortable, filterable, paginated inbox of all enquiries, so that I can work them in order.** → G-03
158	- **As a Support Agent, I want to open an enquiry and move it New → In Progress, so that I can show I've picked it up.** → G-03
159	- **As a Support Agent, I want to resolve an enquiry with a mandatory reply note, so that the resolution is auditable.** → G-03
160	- **As a Support Agent, I want to filter the inbox by category, status, or free text, so that I can find an enquiry quickly.** → G-04
161	- **As a Support Agent, I want to sign in and land on the inbox, so that I start where my work is.** → G-06
162	
163	#### Admin
164	
165	- **As an Admin, I want everything a Support Agent can do, so that I can triage as well as oversee.** → G-03
166	- **As an Admin, I want to delete an enquiry behind a confirmation, so that I can remove spam without leaving clutter.** → G-05
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 5. Task flows
171	
172	### Flow: Authentication
173	
174	| Field | Value |
175	| ----- | ----- |
176	| Actor | Visitor, Support Agent, or Admin |
177	| Trigger | User opens the application unauthenticated. |
178	| Steps | 1. Enter email + password. 2. Submit. 3. On success, route to the role's landing surface (Visitor → Contact form; Agent/Admin → Inbox). 4. On failure, inline error distinguishing credentials from connectivity. |
179	| Role-conditional behaviour | Post-login routing differs by role per §3. |
180	
181	### Flow: Submit Enquiry
182	
183	| Field | Value |
184	| ----- | ----- |
185	| Actor | Visitor |
186	| Trigger | Visitor wants to contact the organisation. |
187	| Steps | 1. Open the Contact form. 2. Enter Name, Email, optional Address, choose a Category, enter a Comment. 3. Submit. 4. System creates an Enquiry in `New`. 5. Route to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details; the form is cleared; a "Message sent!" confirmation shows. |
188	| Decision points | All required fields valid → submit succeeds. Any invalid → inline validation, submit blocked. |
189	| Exception paths | Email malformed → inline error. Comment empty / too short → inline error. |
190	| Role-conditional behaviour | Visitor-only — Agent/Admin do not see the public form in their navigation. |
191	
192	### Flow: My Submissions
193	
194	| Field | Value |
195	| ----- | ----- |
196	| Actor | Visitor |
197	| Trigger | Visitor wants to review enquiries they sent. |
198	| Steps | 1. Open "My messages". 2. See a read-only list of **their own** enquiries with category, status, and submitted date. |
199	| Exception paths | No submissions → entity-specific empty state ("You haven't sent any messages yet") with a link to the Contact form. |
200	| Role-conditional behaviour | A Visitor sees only Enquiries they submitted; never anyone else's. |
201	
202	### Flow: Inbox
203	
204	| Field | Value |
205	| ----- | ----- |
206	| Actor | Support Agent or Admin |
207	| Trigger | Back-office user wants to work incoming enquiries. |
208	| Steps | 1. Open the Inbox. 2. Table renders Name, Category, Status, Submitted date, and (Admin) a Delete action. 3. Click a row to open the Enquiry detail. |
209	| Decision points | Status `New`/`In Progress` → status actions available on detail. Status `Resolved` → status actions hidden; Reply Note shown read-only. |
210	| Exception paths | No enquiries → empty state ("No enquiries yet"). Zero results after filtering → no-results state with active filter chips and Clear-all. |
211	| Role-conditional behaviour | Visitor cannot access the Inbox. Only Admin sees the Delete action. |
212	
213	### Flow: Change Status
214	
215	| Field | Value |
216	| ----- | ----- |
217	| Actor | Support Agent or Admin |
218	| Trigger | Back-office user progresses an enquiry. |
219	| Steps | 1. Open a non-terminal Enquiry. 2. Move `New → In Progress`, or `→ Resolved`. 3. Resolving opens a modal with a **mandatory Reply Note**. 4. Submit; status updates; toast confirmation. |
220	| Decision points | Non-terminal → actions allowed. Terminal (`Resolved`) → actions hidden. Reply Note empty → submit disabled. |
221	| Role-conditional behaviour | Agent and Admin only. |
222	
223	### Flow: Delete Enquiry
224	
225	| Field | Value |
226	| ----- | ----- |
227	| Actor | Admin |
228	| Trigger | An enquiry is spam or a duplicate. |
229	| Steps | 1. Click Delete on an inbox row or the detail. 2. Confirm via a destructive-action gate (modal naming the enquiry; destructive-styled primary; default focus on Cancel). 3. Enquiry is removed. |
230	| Role-conditional behaviour | Admin-only — Agent never sees Delete. |
231	
232	### Flow: Search & Filter
233	
234	| Field | Value |
235	| ----- | ----- |
236	| Actor | Support Agent or Admin |
237	| Trigger | User wants to narrow the inbox. |
238	| Steps | 1. Open the filter controls. 2. Filter by Category, Status, or free text (Name, Comment). 3. Active filters render as chips with a Clear-all action. |
239	| Exception paths | Zero results → no-results state including active filter chips + Clear-all. |
240	| Role-conditional behaviour | Same controls for Agent and Admin. |
241	
242	---
243	
244	## 6. Requirements
245	
246	### 6.1 Functional
247	
248	- F-01 The system supports email-and-password authentication and routes the user to a role-specific landing surface on success.
249	- F-02 A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category, and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created in `New`.
250	- F-03 On successful submit, the system routes to a confirmation page echoing the submitted details, clears the form, and shows a "Message sent!" confirmation.
251	- F-04 A Visitor may view a read-only list of the Enquiries they submitted, and only those.
252	- F-05 A Support Agent or Admin may view all Enquiries in a sortable, paginated table.
253	- F-06 A Support Agent or Admin may filter Enquiries by Category, Status, and free-text search on Name and Comment.
254	- F-07 A Support Agent or Admin may move a non-terminal Enquiry from `New` to `In Progress`.
255	- F-08 A Support Agent or Admin may resolve a non-terminal Enquiry by submitting a non-empty Reply Note, transitioning it to `Resolved`.
256	- F-09 An Admin may delete an Enquiry.
257	- F-10 The system surfaces the Reply Note read-only on a `Resolved` Enquiry's detail.
258	
259	### 6.2 Business rules
260	
261	| ID | Statement (when / then) | Enforcement point | Severity |
262	| ---- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | -------- |
263	| BR-01 | When an Enquiry's Status is `Resolved`, then status-change actions must be hidden in the UI. | UI | blocker |
264	| BR-02 | When a back-office user resolves an Enquiry, then a non-empty Reply Note must be submitted; the submit control is disabled until a note is entered. | UI | blocker |
265	| BR-03 | When a destructive Delete is triggered, then a confirmation modal naming the Enquiry must be shown before removal. | UI | blocker |
266	| BR-04 | When a Visitor views their submissions, then only Enquiries they submitted may be shown. | UI | blocker |
267	| BR-05 | When a user without access reaches a role-restricted surface via a direct link, then an in-page permission-denied banner must be shown (never a generic 403 page). | UI | major |
268	| BR-06 | When the Contact form is submitted, then Email must match a valid email format and Comment must be non-empty (min 10 characters). | UI | major |
269	
270	### 6.3 Data
271	
272	- The Enquiry record carries the fields enumerated on the §7 Enquiry entity.
273	- Enquiry Status enum values are exactly `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved`.
274	- Category enum values are exactly `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry`.
275	- Reply Note is required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 characters.
276	
277	### 6.4 User-facing
278	
279	- UF-01 The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select), and Comment (multi-line) with a leading-asterisk convention on required fields and a single legend line.
280	- UF-02 Forms validate on blur for synchronous rules (format, required, length) and on submit for cross-field rules; never on keystroke. On success, the form resets and a success toast (auto-dismiss 4–8 s, top-right) confirms.
281	- UF-03 The confirmation page echoes the submitted Name, Email, Category, and Comment read-only, with a "Message sent!" heading and a control to send another.
282	- UF-04 The Inbox table renders Name, Category, Status, Submitted date, with a row-click to detail and (Admin-only) a Delete row action. Pagination ladder 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 (default 20); single-column sort, ascending then descending; the pagination control is always rendered.
283	- UF-05 Status badges colour-map: `New` (info / blue), `In Progress` (in-progress / amber), `Resolved` (success / green). Colour is always paired with an icon or text label; never relied on alone.
284	- UF-06 Empty states distinguish zero-data ("No enquiries yet" / "You haven't sent any messages yet") from zero-results-of-filter (active filter chips + Clear-all, no creation CTA).
285	- UF-07 The Resolve modal displays a mandatory Reply Note text field (multi-line) with a character counter and a clear ceiling.
286	- UF-08 Icon-only row actions carry tooltips on hover and focus plus an `aria-label` matching the tooltip; primary destructive actions are never icon-only.
287	- UF-09 Denied-access surfaces render an in-page permission-denied banner naming the missing permission and a path back to the user's own surface.
288	- UF-10 Top-level navigation is role-scoped: Visitor sees Contact + My messages; Agent/Admin see Inbox; Admin additionally sees Delete affordances.
289	
290	### 6.5 Access control (RBAC)
291	
292	> Roles-×-resources matrix. **Action vocabulary:** `C` create · `R` read · `U` update · `D` delete · `X` execute · `—` no access. Suffix with a BR ref for conditional access.
293	
294	| Role (→ §3) | Enquiry (entity) | User (entity) | Authentication (flow) | Submit Enquiry (flow) | My Submissions (flow) | Inbox (flow) | Change Status (flow) | Delete Enquiry (flow) | Search & Filter (flow) |
295	| ----------- | ---------------- | ------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------- | ------------ | -------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------- |
296	| Visitor       | C R (own)          | R (self) | X | X | R (own) | — | — | — | — |
297	| Support Agent | R U†BR-01          | R (self) | X | — | — | R | X†BR-01,BR-02 | — | X |
298	| Admin         | R U†BR-01 D        | R (self) | X | — | — | R | X†BR-01,BR-02 | X†BR-03 | X |
299	
300	> Notes:
301	> - Denied actions must be **hidden** in the UI, not rendered as disabled controls.
302	> - Direct-link access by a denied persona surfaces the §6.4 UF-09 permission-denied banner, not a 403 page.
303	> - `Enquiry U†BR-01` reflects that a back-office mutation is restricted to Status/Reply Note and gated by BR-01 (must be non-terminal).
304	
305	### 6.6 Non-functional
306	
307	#### 6.6.1 Security & session
308	
309	| Field | Value | Source |

# Epic Brief: Sign-in and App Shell

*Inherits roles, auth, data source, compliance, and styling from project.md.*

---

## Goal

Everyone signs in with email and password, lands on the right page for their role, sees only the menu items their role allows, and gets a clear on-page message if they open a page they can't use.

This epic delivers the shared foundation the rest of the app builds on: the sign-in screen and its failure handling, the session rules (idle and absolute timeouts, lockout after repeated failures), the role-scoped app shell and top-level navigation, the in-page permission-denied banner, and the in-memory data layer (the Enquiry and User records with seeded sample data) that later epics read from and write to (`requirements.md` §5 Flow: Authentication, G-06, F-01, UF-09, UF-10, BR-05, §6.6.1, §7, PI-01, PI-02).

---

## Data Model

Source: `documentation/requirements.md` §2 and §7. No OpenAPI spec or design was provided.

### Enquiry

| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
| Name | string | yes | non-empty; max 120 chars | Primary identifier in the inbox |
| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Reply-to |
| Address | string | no | max 255 chars | Optional |
| Category | enum | yes | exactly one of `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` | |
| Comment | string | yes | non-empty; min 10, max 2000 chars | Enquiry body |
| Status | enum | yes | exactly one of `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` | `Resolved` is terminal |
| ReplyNote | string | no | required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 chars | Read-only after resolution |
| SubmittedAt | datetime | yes | system-assigned (ISO-8601) | |
| SubmittedByEmail | string | yes | mirrors the submitting Visitor | Scopes "My messages" |
| HandledBy | string | no | mirrors the acting back-office user | Set when status first changes |

### User

| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Sign-in identifier |
| FirstName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
| LastName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
| Password | string | yes | min complexity per policy | Write-only; never displayed |
| Role | enum | yes | exactly one of `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` | Drives landing page, navigation and access |

### Seeded data

- **Users:** `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin) (project.md §Authentication).
- **Enquiries:** a small set that together covers every Category (Feedback, Question, General Enquiry) and every Status (New, In Progress, Resolved). Resolved enquiries carry a Reply Note. At least one enquiry is submitted by the seeded Visitor so "My messages" has content.
- **Persistence:** changes last for the browser session and are lost on reload (PI-02).

---

## Functional Requirements

- **R1:** A user can sign in with an email and password; on success a Visitor lands on the Contact form and a Support Agent or Admin lands on the Inbox.
- **R2:** When sign-in fails, an inline error on the sign-in screen tells the user whether the email/password was wrong or whether there was a connection problem.
- **R3:** A signed-in session ends after 30 minutes of inactivity or 12 hours in total, whichever comes first, and the user is returned to the sign-in screen.
- **R4:** After 5 failed sign-in attempts for an account, that account is locked for 15 minutes and the sign-in screen says it is locked and for how long.
- **R5:** The top-level navigation shows a Visitor only "Contact" and "My messages", and shows a Support Agent or Admin only "Inbox"; menu items a role can't use are hidden, not shown disabled.
- **R6:** A signed-in user who opens a page their role can't use through a direct link sees an in-page permission-denied banner that names the missing permission and gives a link back to their own landing page, never a generic 403 page.
- **R7:** The app holds Enquiry records with the fields listed in the Data Model, where Status is exactly New / In Progress / Resolved and Category is exactly Feedback / Question / General Enquiry.
- **R8:** The app starts with seeded sample enquiries covering every category and every status, plus the three seeded users; changes made during a session persist until the page is reloaded.
- **R9:** Every screen this epic delivers meets WCAG 2.2 AA, can be operated with the keyboard alone, and never uses status colour without an accompanying icon or text label.

---

## Business Rules

- **BR1:** A user who is not signed in and opens any app page is sent to the sign-in screen.
- **BR2:** After sign-in, routing is decided only by the user's role: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent or Admin → Inbox.
- **BR3:** Actions and menu items a role is denied are hidden, never rendered disabled (`requirements.md` §6.5 notes).
- **BR4:** Reaching a role-restricted page by direct link shows the permission-denied banner in the page, not a 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05).
- **BR5:** A locked account cannot sign in, even with the correct password, until the 15-minute lockout has passed.
- **BR6:** Session timeouts and lockout are simulated in the browser (PI-01); there is no server-side enforcement.

---

## Key Workflows

### Sign in

1. An unauthenticated user opens the app and is shown the sign-in screen.
2. They enter their email and password and submit.
3. On success they land on their role's page: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent / Admin → Inbox.
4. On failure an inline error explains whether the credentials were wrong or the connection failed; the entered email is kept.
5. On the 5th consecutive failure the account is locked for 15 minutes and the screen says so.

### Navigate the app shell

1. A signed-in user sees a top navigation with only the items their role allows (Visitor: Contact, My messages; Support Agent / Admin: Inbox).
2. They can sign out from the shell and return to the sign-in screen.

### Open a page you can't use

1. A signed-in user follows a direct link to a page outside their role (for example, a Visitor opens the Inbox).
2. The page shows a permission-denied banner naming the missing permission.
3. The banner offers a link back to their own landing page.

### Session expiry

1. A signed-in user is inactive for 30 minutes, or has been signed in for 12 hours.
2. The session ends and they are returned to the sign-in screen with a message that their session expired.

---

## Feature NFRs

- **NFR1:** The sign-in form is fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: labelled fields, errors announced to assistive technology and linked to their fields, focus moved to the error summary on a failed submit.
- **NFR2:** The permission-denied banner is announced to assistive technology when the page loads and its "back" link is reachable by keyboard.
- **NFR3:** Password field input is masked and the password is never shown or logged.

---

## Out of Scope

- The Contact form, confirmation page, My messages list, Inbox table, enquiry detail, status changes and delete. Later epics deliver these; this epic only routes to their pages and guards access to them.
- The reviewer role switcher (`requirements.md` PI-05), dropped by user decision. Reviewers sign in as each seeded user instead.
- Real authentication, password reset, registration, and account management.

---

## Notes & Caveats

- **Landing pages before their epics exist:** the Contact form, My messages and Inbox are built in later epics. This epic needs a minimal destination for each so that sign-in routing, navigation and the permission-denied banner can be tested. Later epics replace these placeholders.
- **"Connection problem" under simulated auth:** auth is simulated in the browser (PI-01), so there is no real network failure. The way BUILD triggers and tests the connection-problem error (for example, a stub failure mode) still needs deciding.
- **Session and lockout values are inferred:** `requirements.md` §6.6.1 marks the 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout and 5-failure / 15-minute lockout as inferred defaults (project.md NFR-base-6). Confirm before BUILD if they matter.
- **Server-side auth vs. simulated auth:** project.md records the method as `server-side` (BFF), but every auth endpoint is N/A because auth is simulated client-side. Confirm the stub follows the server-side auth pattern's shape (for example, session handling behind a route) rather than a purely client-side flag.
- **Wording of the "missing permission":** the banner must name the missing permission (UF-09), but project.md's permissions matrix only has "View main dashboard" so far. Permission names such as "View inbox" or "Submit an enquiry" will be added to project.md during BUILD, with your approval.
- **Seed data is defined here, used later:** the seeded enquiries are only displayed in later epics. This epic delivers the data layer and seed. Its tests can check the seed's shape (every category and status present) but not how it is shown on screen.

# Epic Brief: Inbox

*Inherits roles, auth, data source, compliance, and styling from project.md.*

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic slug | `inbox` |
| Epic name | Inbox |
| Depends on | `sign-in-and-app-shell` (sign-in, role-scoped navigation, permission-denied banner, Enquiry fixtures) |
| Sources | `documentation/requirements.md` §4 (G-03, G-04), §5 (Inbox, Search & Filter flows), §6.1 F-05 / F-06, §6.4 UF-04 / UF-05 / UF-06, §6.6.1, §6.6.2 |

---

## Goal

Support Agents and Admins see every enquiry in one sortable, paged table and can narrow it down by category, status or text.

The Inbox is the landing page for both back-office roles (project.md §Authentication) and is where they triage incoming enquiries (`requirements.md` G-03, G-04). This epic delivers the table, its status badges, sorting, paging, filtering and its empty and no-results states. Opening an enquiry's detail, changing its status, resolving it and deleting it belong to the next epic (`enquiry-handling`).

---

## Data Model

No new entities. This epic reads the **Enquiry** entity that `sign-in-and-app-shell` sets up as in-memory fixtures (`requirements.md` §7; no OpenAPI spec exists).

| Field | Type | Used by this epic |
|---|---|---|
| Id | integer | Row identity; the target of the row click |
| Name | string (max 120) | Table column; free-text search |
| Category | enum: `Feedback` / `Question` / `General Enquiry` | Table column; Category filter |
| Comment | string (10 to 2000) | Free-text search only (not a column) |
| Status | enum: `New` / `In Progress` / `Resolved` | Table column shown as a badge; Status filter |
| SubmittedAt | datetime (ISO-8601) | "Submitted" column; sortable |
| Email, Address | string | Not shown in the table. Personal data that back-office roles only can see (R6) |

Derived view state (not persisted): sort column and direction, page size, current page, active Category / Status filters, search text.

---

## Functional Requirements

- **R1:** A Support Agent or Admin sees all Enquiries in a table with Name, Category, Status and Submitted date columns.
- **R2:** Clicking a row in the Inbox opens that Enquiry's detail.
- **R3:** The table supports single-column sort: choosing a column sorts it ascending, choosing it again sorts it descending.
- **R4:** The table is paged with page sizes 5, 10, 20 and 50, defaulting to 20, and the pagination control is always shown, even when the results fit on one page.
- **R5:** Each Status is shown as a colour-coded badge: New is blue, In Progress is amber, Resolved is green, and the colour is always paired with an icon or text label.
- **R6:** A Support Agent or Admin can filter the Inbox by Category.
- **R7:** A Support Agent or Admin can filter the Inbox by Status.
- **R8:** A Support Agent or Admin can search the Inbox by free text, matching an Enquiry's Name or Comment.
- **R9:** Each active filter and search is shown as a chip, and a Clear-all action removes them all and restores the full list.
- **R10:** When there are no Enquiries at all, the Inbox shows a "No enquiries yet" empty state.
- **R11:** When filters or search return no Enquiries, the Inbox shows a no-results state that keeps the active filter chips and Clear-all, with no call-to-action to create an enquiry.
- **R12:** Enquirers' contact details (Name, Email, Address) are visible only to signed-in Support Agents and Admins, and a Visitor cannot reach the Inbox.

---

## Business Rules

- **BR1:** Only Support Agent and Admin can open the Inbox. A Visitor who opens it from a direct link sees the in-page permission-denied banner from `sign-in-and-app-shell`, never the table or a generic 403 page (`requirements.md` §6.5, BR-05).
- **BR2:** The Inbox lists every Enquiry, whoever submitted it. It is not scoped to the signed-in user (`requirements.md` F-05).
- **BR3:** Filters and search apply together: an Enquiry is shown only if it matches every active filter (`[INFERRED]` the sources list the filters but don't say how they combine; combining with AND is the usual inbox behaviour).
- **BR4:** Changing a filter, the search text or the page size returns the table to page 1 (`[INFERRED]` standard paging behaviour; not stated in the sources).
- **BR5:** Status colour is never the only signal: every badge carries the status name or an icon (`requirements.md` UF-05, NFR-base-1).
- **BR6:** Support Agents and Admins see the same table, filters and search (`requirements.md` Search & Filter flow). The Admin-only Delete row action is added by `enquiry-handling`, not here.

---

## Key Workflows

### Work the Inbox
1. A Support Agent or Admin signs in and lands on the Inbox.
2. The table shows all Enquiries, 20 per page, with a status badge on each row.
3. They choose a column header to sort it ascending, then again for descending.
4. They change the page size (5 / 10 / 20 / 50) or move between pages.
5. They click a row to open that Enquiry's detail.

### Find an enquiry
1. On the Inbox, they open the filter controls.
2. They choose a Category and/or a Status and/or type search text.
3. The table narrows to matching Enquiries, and each active filter shows as a chip.
4. They remove one chip, or choose Clear-all to restore the full list.
5. If nothing matches, the no-results state shows, keeping the chips and Clear-all.

### Visitor blocked from the Inbox
1. A signed-in Visitor opens the Inbox address directly.
2. The in-page permission-denied banner shows, with a path back to the Contact form; no enquiry data is shown.

---

## Feature NFRs

- **NFR1:** The Inbox page is interactive at p95 ≤ 2 s with 100 rows (`requirements.md` §6.6.2; marked inferred in the source).
- **NFR2:** Sorting, paging, filtering, search, chip removal and row opening all work from the keyboard, and sorted columns announce their sort direction to screen readers (NFR-base-1).
- **NFR3:** The table stays usable at the mobile breakpoint (≥360px) (NFR-base-3).

---

## Out of Scope

- The Enquiry detail page, moving an Enquiry to In Progress, resolving with a Reply Note, and deleting an Enquiry (including the Admin-only Delete row action and icon-only action tooltips) are delivered by `enquiry-handling`.
- Sign-in, role-scoped navigation, the permission-denied banner and the Enquiry fixtures are delivered by `sign-in-and-app-shell`.
- Sorting by more than one column at a time.
- A role switcher for reviewers (left out at the epic-plan approval; reviewers sign in as each seeded user).

---

## Notes & Caveats

- **Row click target:** R2 needs the detail page, which `enquiry-handling` builds. Until then the row click needs a destination, such as a route that `enquiry-handling` fills in. Confirm how this epic should treat it.
- **Default sort order:** the sources don't give an initial sort. `[INFERRED]` Submitted date, newest first, so new enquiries appear at the top.
- **Category and Status filters: one value or several?** The sources don't say whether a user can pick more than one Category or Status at once. `[INFERRED]` one value per filter.
- **Free-text search matching:** the sources don't specify. `[INFERRED]` case-insensitive "contains" matching on Name and Comment.
- **Mock data:** the table reads in-memory fixtures (PI-02). To check NFR1 with 100 rows, a larger fixture set than the few seeded enquiries is needed for the performance check.

# Contact Form and My Messages

*Inherits roles, auth, data source, compliance, and styling from project.md.*

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic slug | `visitor-enquiries` |
| Depends on | `sign-in-and-app-shell` (sign-in, role-scoped navigation, permission-denied banner, Enquiry fixtures) |
| Source | `documentation/requirements.md` (F-02, F-03, F-04, BR-04, BR-06, UF-01, UF-02, UF-03, UF-06, §6.6.2, §7) |

---

## Goal

A Visitor sends an enquiry, sees a 'Message sent!' confirmation of what they sent, and can look back over their own messages (and only theirs).

This covers the Visitor's two surfaces from the role-scoped navigation: **Contact** (the enquiry form and its confirmation page) and **My messages** (a read-only list of the Visitor's own enquiries). Sign-in, navigation, the permission-denied banner and the seeded fixtures come from the `sign-in-and-app-shell` epic; the back-office Inbox and enquiry handling come from later epics.

---

## Data Model

No OpenAPI spec exists. The entity comes from `requirements.md` §7. The Enquiry record and its fixtures are set up by `sign-in-and-app-shell`. This epic **creates** Enquiry records and **reads** the signed-in Visitor's own records.

### Enquiry (fields this epic writes or reads)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Used here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Assigned on create |
| Name | string | yes | non-empty; max 120 chars | Form input; echoed on the confirmation page |
| Email | string | yes | valid email format (RFC-5322) | Form input; echoed on the confirmation page |
| Address | string | no | max 255 chars | Optional form input |
| Category | enum | yes | one of `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` | Form select; echoed on the confirmation page; a column in My messages |
| Comment | string | yes | non-empty; min 10, max 2000 chars | Form input (multi-line); echoed on the confirmation page |
| Status | enum | yes | one of `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` | Set to `New` on create; shown in My messages |
| SubmittedAt | datetime | yes | system-assigned (ISO-8601) | Set on create; shown as the submitted date in My messages |
| SubmittedByEmail | string | yes | the signed-in Visitor's account email | Set on create; scopes My messages |

Fields not used by this epic: `ReplyNote` and `HandledBy` (handled in `enquiry-handling`).

---

## Functional Requirements

- **R1:** A Visitor may submit an Enquiry with Name, Email, Category and Comment (required) and Address (optional); the Enquiry is created with Status `New`. (F-02)
- **R2:** The Contact form presents Name, Email, Address (optional), Category (select) and Comment (multi-line), with a leading asterisk on required fields and a single legend line explaining it, and is fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable. (UF-01)
- **R3:** The Contact form requires a valid email format; a non-empty Comment of 10 to 2000 characters; a Name of at most 120 characters; and an Address of at most 255 characters. Invalid input shows inline errors and blocks submission. (BR-06 / §7)
- **R4:** Form errors appear when the user leaves a field (single-field rules) or on submit (cross-field rules), never while typing. On success the form resets and a success toast appears top-right and dismisses itself after 4 to 8 seconds. (UF-02)
- **R5:** On a successful submit, the Visitor is taken to a confirmation page headed "Message sent!" that shows the submitted Name, Email, Category and Comment read-only, the form is cleared, and a control lets the Visitor send another enquiry. (F-03 / UF-03)
- **R6:** Submitting an enquiry reaches the confirmation page within 1 second. (§6.6.2)
- **R7:** A Visitor may view a read-only "My messages" list of the Enquiries they submitted, showing category, status and submitted date for each. (F-04)
- **R8:** A Visitor's "My messages" list shows only Enquiries they submitted; other people's names, emails and addresses are never shown to a Visitor. (BR-04 / NFR-base-7, Visitor side)
- **R9:** When a Visitor has no submissions, "My messages" shows "You haven't sent any messages yet" with a link to the Contact form. (UF-06, Visitor)

---

## Business Rules

- **BR1:** A new Enquiry always starts in Status `New`. (F-02)
- **BR2:** Submission is blocked while any field fails validation: Email format invalid; Comment empty, under 10 or over 2000 characters; Name empty or over 120 characters; Address over 255 characters; Category not chosen. (BR-06 / §7)
- **BR3:** Validation runs on blur and on submit, never on keystroke. (UF-02)
- **BR4:** "My messages" lists only Enquiries whose `SubmittedByEmail` matches the signed-in Visitor. (BR-04)
- **BR5:** "My messages" is read-only: a Visitor cannot edit, change status of, or delete an Enquiry. Those actions are hidden, not disabled. (§6.5)
- **BR6:** Only Visitors can reach the Contact form and My messages. A Support Agent or Admin opening either through a direct link sees the in-page permission-denied banner from `sign-in-and-app-shell`. (§5 Submit Enquiry / My Submissions role notes; §6.5; BR-05)
- **BR7:** Enquiries submitted in this session appear in My messages (and in the back-office Inbox) for the rest of the session but do not survive a page reload. (PI-02)

---

## Key Workflows

### Submit an enquiry

1. The Visitor signs in and lands on the Contact form (or opens Contact from the navigation).
2. The Visitor enters Name, Email, optional Address, chooses a Category and enters a Comment.
3. Leaving a field with invalid input shows an inline error for that field.
4. The Visitor submits. If any field is invalid, inline errors show and nothing is sent.
5. If all fields are valid, an Enquiry is created in `New`, the form is cleared, a success toast appears, and the Visitor is taken to the "Message sent!" confirmation page showing Name, Email, Category and Comment.
6. The Visitor can choose "send another" to return to an empty Contact form.

### Review my messages

1. The Visitor opens "My messages" from the navigation.
2. A read-only list of their own enquiries shows category, status and submitted date.
3. If they have none, the page shows "You haven't sent any messages yet" with a link to the Contact form.

---

## Feature NFRs

- **NFR1:** Form submit to confirmation page in 1 second or less. (§6.6.2)
- **NFR2:** The Contact form is fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: every field has a programmatic label, required fields are announced as required, and inline errors are linked to their fields and announced. (UF-01 / §6.6.3; WCAG 2.2 AA per NFR-base-1)
- **NFR3:** The status shown in My messages pairs colour with a text or icon label, never colour alone. (UF-05 / NFR-base-1)

---

## Out of Scope

- Signing in, role-scoped navigation, the permission-denied banner and the seeded fixtures (`sign-in-and-app-shell`).
- The back-office Inbox, filtering and status badges as an Inbox feature (`inbox`).
- Viewing an enquiry's detail, changing status, Reply Notes and deleting (`enquiry-handling`).
- Editing or withdrawing an enquiry after it is sent. The requirements describe My messages as read-only only.
- Real email delivery or notifications on submit. Any such confirmation is a UI message only (PI-04).
- Server-side validation; validation is visual only (PI-03).
- The reviewer role switcher (R6 in the epic plan), dropped at the user's decision.

---

## Notes & Caveats

- **Toast and confirmation page together.** UF-02 asks for a success toast and a form reset on success, while F-03 / UF-03 ask for a move to a "Message sent!" confirmation page. Both are carried as written: the toast shows over the confirmation page. Confirm during BUILD that both are wanted.
- **Which email scopes My messages.** The form has its own Email field, but `requirements.md` §7 scopes My submissions by `SubmittedByEmail`, the signed-in Visitor's account. This brief assumes My messages matches on the **account email**, not the email typed into the form, so an enquiry sent with a different contact email still appears for the sender. [INFERRED] from the §7 field notes.
- **Email prefill not specified.** The requirements do not say whether Name or Email are prefilled from the signed-in account. This brief assumes empty fields. [INFERRED]
- **Address is not echoed.** UF-03 lists Name, Email, Category and Comment for the confirmation page and leaves out Address. This brief follows UF-03 exactly.
- **No cross-field rules exist on this form.** UF-02 mentions cross-field rules on submit, but none of the Contact form fields depend on each other. On submit, every field is re-checked and all errors are shown together.
- **My messages sort order not specified.** This brief assumes newest first by submitted date. [INFERRED]
- **Fixtures needed for the empty state.** To show both a populated and an empty My messages list, the seeded data from `sign-in-and-app-shell` must give `visitor@example.com` some enquiries and also allow the empty state to be reached. Today there is only one seeded Visitor, so the empty-state test needs a Visitor with no enquiries (for example, a test fixture override). Settle this during BUILD.

# Epic Brief: Working an Enquiry

*Inherits roles, auth, data source, compliance, and styling from project.md.*

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Epic slug | `enquiry-handling` |
| Depends on | `inbox` (the Inbox table and row-click navigation this epic opens from) |
| Source | `documentation/requirements.md` (no design provided) |

---

## Goal

Support Agents and Admins open an enquiry, mark it In Progress, and resolve it with a Reply Note; Admins can also delete spam after confirming.

This epic delivers the Enquiry detail page reached from an Inbox row, the status lifecycle actions on it (`New` → `In Progress` → `Resolved`), the Resolve modal with its mandatory Reply Note, the read-only view of a Resolved enquiry, and the Admin-only Delete with its confirmation gate (on both the Inbox row and the detail). It serves goals G-03 (triage and drive each enquiry to resolution) and G-05 (keep the inbox clean) from `requirements.md` §4.1.

---

## Data Model

This epic modifies the existing **Enquiry** entity (introduced by `sign-in-and-app-shell`, `requirements.md` §7). No new entities.

| Field | Type | Role in this epic |
|---|---|---|
| Id | integer | Identifies the enquiry in the detail route and the delete action |
| Name | string (max 120) | Shown on detail; named in the Delete confirmation modal |
| Email | string (RFC-5322) | Shown on detail |
| Address | string (optional, max 255) | Shown on detail |
| Category | enum `Feedback` / `Question` / `General Enquiry` | Shown on detail |
| Comment | string (10-2000) | Shown on detail |
| Status | enum `New` / `In Progress` / `Resolved` | Shown on detail as a status badge; **updated** by Mark In Progress and Resolve; `Resolved` is terminal |
| ReplyNote | string (max 1000) | **Written** by the Resolve modal; required when Status is `Resolved`; read-only afterwards |
| SubmittedAt | datetime (ISO-8601) | Shown on detail as the Submitted date |
| HandledBy | string | **Written** with the acting back-office user when status first changes; audit |

**Operations introduced (mock layer, session-only per PI-02):**

- Get one enquiry by Id
- Change status `New` → `In Progress` (sets HandledBy if not yet set)
- Resolve with Reply Note (non-terminal → `Resolved`; sets HandledBy if not yet set)
- Delete enquiry by Id (Admin only)

---

## Functional Requirements

- **R1:** Opening an Inbox row shows the Enquiry detail with the enquiry's Name, Email, Address, Category, Comment, Status and Submitted date.
- **R2:** A Support Agent or Admin can move a non-terminal Enquiry from `New` to `In Progress`. The status updates, a toast confirms the change, and HandledBy is recorded when the status first changes.
- **R3:** Resolving an enquiry opens a modal with a required multi-line Reply Note (max 1000 characters, with a character counter). The submit control stays disabled until a note is entered. On submit the status becomes `Resolved` and a toast confirms.
- **R4:** When an Enquiry is `Resolved`, the status-change actions are hidden and the Reply Note is shown read-only on the detail.
- **R5:** An Admin can delete an Enquiry from an Inbox row or from the detail. A confirmation modal names the Enquiry, uses a destructive-styled primary button and puts default focus on Cancel. Confirming removes the Enquiry. Support Agents never see Delete.
- **R6:** Icon-only row actions show a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus, plus an accessible label that matches the tooltip. Primary destructive actions are never icon-only.

---

## Business Rules

- **BR1:** Status-change actions (Mark In Progress, Resolve) are available only while the Enquiry is non-terminal (`New` or `In Progress`). When the Enquiry is `Resolved`, they are hidden, not disabled (`requirements.md` BR-01, §6.5 notes).
- **BR2:** Moving an Enquiry to `Resolved` requires a non-empty Reply Note of at most 1000 characters. The Resolve modal's submit control is disabled until a note is entered (`requirements.md` BR-02, §6.3).
- **BR3:** Delete is preceded by a confirmation modal that names the Enquiry, with a destructive-styled primary button and default focus on Cancel. Nothing is removed until the user confirms (`requirements.md` BR-03).
- **BR4:** Only Admins see the Delete action. It is hidden for Support Agents, not shown disabled (`requirements.md` §6.5, F-09).
- **BR5:** HandledBy is set to the acting back-office user the first time the Enquiry's status changes and is not overwritten by later changes (`requirements.md` §7).
- **BR6:** Status moves forward only (`New` → `In Progress` → `Resolved`). `Resolved` is terminal and its Reply Note cannot be edited (`requirements.md` §2.3).
- **BR7:** A Visitor cannot reach the Enquiry detail. Opening it through a direct link shows the in-page permission-denied banner from `sign-in-and-app-shell` (`requirements.md` BR-05 / UF-09).

---

## Key Workflows

### W1: Open an enquiry

1. A Support Agent or Admin is on the Inbox.
2. They click (or activate with the keyboard) an enquiry row.
3. The Enquiry detail opens, showing Name, Email, Address, Category, Comment, a Status badge and the Submitted date.
4. Actions on the detail reflect the role and status: Mark In Progress (only when `New`), Resolve (when `New` or `In Progress`), and Delete (Admin only).

### W2: Mark In Progress

1. On a `New` enquiry's detail, the user selects Mark In Progress.
2. The status badge changes to `In Progress`, and a toast confirms the change.
3. HandledBy is recorded if this is the first status change.
4. Mark In Progress is no longer offered. Resolve remains.

### W3: Resolve with a Reply Note

1. On a non-terminal enquiry's detail, the user selects Resolve.
2. A modal opens with a multi-line Reply Note field, a character counter showing the 1000-character limit, and a disabled submit button.
3. The user types a note, and the submit button becomes enabled.
4. The user submits. The modal closes, the status badge changes to `Resolved`, and a toast confirms.
5. The status-change actions disappear, and the Reply Note is shown read-only on the detail.
6. Cancelling the modal leaves the enquiry unchanged.

### W4: Delete (Admin only)

1. An Admin selects Delete on an Inbox row or on the enquiry detail.
2. A confirmation modal opens, naming the enquiry. Focus starts on Cancel, and the primary button uses destructive styling.
3. Cancel (or Escape) closes the modal, and nothing changes.
4. Confirming removes the enquiry. It no longer appears in the Inbox.

---

## Feature NFRs

- **NFR1:** Every action in this epic can be done with the keyboard alone: opening a row, the status actions, the Resolve modal (focus moves into the modal and returns to the trigger when it closes), and the Delete confirmation (focus starts on Cancel). This applies NFR-base-1 to this epic.
- **NFR2:** The Reply Note character counter is announced to assistive technology, and the reason the submit button is disabled is clear without relying on colour.
- **NFR3:** The status badge on the detail pairs colour with a text or icon label (UF-05, shared with the `inbox` epic's badge component).

---

## Out of Scope

- Reassigning enquiries. `requirements.md` §1 mentions it as an Admin duty, but no functional requirement, flow or RBAC entry defines it.
- Editing an enquiry's contact details, category or comment. Back-office changes are limited to Status and Reply Note (§6.5 notes).
- Moving a status backwards, or reopening a Resolved enquiry.
- Sending a real email or notification when an enquiry is resolved. Confirmation appears in the UI only (PI-04).
- The Inbox table itself, plus sorting, filtering and pagination (`inbox` epic).

---

## Notes & Caveats

- **Resolve directly from `New`:** the Change Status flow ("Move New → In Progress, or → Resolved") and F-08 ("resolve a non-terminal Enquiry") both allow Resolve from `New` as well as from `In Progress`. This brief offers Resolve in both states. Please confirm that you don't require `In Progress` first.
- **[INFERRED] What happens after deleting from the detail:** the spec only says "Enquiry is removed." This brief assumes the user is returned to the Inbox with a toast confirming the deletion. Deleting from an Inbox row keeps the user on the Inbox.
- **[INFERRED] A whitespace-only Reply Note counts as empty:** "non-empty" is read as non-blank after trimming, so a note containing only spaces keeps submit disabled.
- **[INFERRED] Enquiry not found:** the spec doesn't cover opening the detail for an enquiry that no longer exists (for example, a link to an enquiry deleted in this session). This brief assumes a "not found" message on the page with a link back to the Inbox.
- **HandledBy display:** §7 says to record HandledBy for audit, but no requirement says where to show it. It is stored but not shown on the detail unless you want it shown.
- **Delete row action is shared with the `inbox` epic:** UF-04 places the Admin-only Delete action in the Inbox table, but the delete behaviour belongs to this epic. This epic adds the row action to the existing table. The row Delete can be icon-only (with tooltip and accessible label, R6), but the confirmation modal's destructive button must have a text label.
- **Session-only changes:** status changes, Reply Notes and deletions persist only for the session and are lost on reload (PI-02). Tests should not expect them to survive a page reload.

# Project Overview section (`CLAUDE.md`)

The `## Project Overview` section of `CLAUDE.md` describes the project being built. Written at INTAKE, then checked against `project.md` at every epic merge — the only two points it is ever written.

## What it contains

A two-sentence lead-in (what the app is, what each role does with it), three bullets, one pointer line — **within 12 lines and 150 words**.

| Bullet | From `project.md` | Ends with |
|---|---|---|
| Roles | column headings of §Roles & Permissions | closed list; exact string form |
| Auth | §Authentication `Method` | session mechanism; what it forbids |
| Data source | §Data Source & Backend Integration `Data source` + `Mock layer required` | mocks or live |

Each bullet ends in the constraint that makes the fact actionable — a few words, never more than a short sentence, always derived from this project's `project.md`.

Pointer line, exactly three: `generated-docs/project.md` (facts and detail), `generated-docs/epics/` (epics and briefs), `generated-docs/architecture.md` (reusable code and conventions).

**Never present:** permissions, endpoints, palette, compliance domains or requirements, theme, backend connectivity, epics, stories, build progress, timestamps, slugs, NFRs.

### Shape to match

```markdown
## Project Overview

Transaction Import & Approval System: an internal financial-operations console. A File Importer uploads bank-transaction files and tracks processing; an Approver reviews, approves, rejects (with a note) or exports the resulting transactions.

- Roles: `File Importer`, `Approver` (exact backend strings; no other role exists).
- Auth: server-side, browser-managed session cookie. No token in frontend code.
- Data source: existing API, two live backend services. No mocks.

Facts and detail: `generated-docs/project.md`. Epics and briefs: `generated-docs/epics/`. Reusable code and conventions: `generated-docs/architecture.md`.
```

The shape, not the wording — no clause above transfers to another project, except the pointer line.

## Writing it

- **Never from an `epic/*` branch** — only where `project.md` itself is written.
- **Correct, don't rewrite.** Stale means it contradicts `project.md`, or a stated fact is missing. Worded differently from how you would have written it is **not** stale.
- **Write nothing when nothing is stale** — leave `CLAUDE.md` byte-for-byte untouched.
- **Never trim the user's own words to fit the budget.** The budget binds what you write; correct the facts in place and leave the rest.
- **Silent** — no prompt, no message, including when correcting words the user wrote.
