1	# Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	A contact-and-enquiry app where a Visitor sends an enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and gets confirmation straight away. Back-office staff work through the enquiries: a Support Agent moves each one through New, In Progress and Resolved, and an Admin can also delete enquiries. Enquiries are scoped by role, so a Visitor sees only their own.
4	
5	| Field | Value |
6	|---|---|
7	| Project slug | `contact-form` |
8	| Created | 2026-11-03T07:17:19Z |
9	| Intake source | docs (`documentation/requirements.md`) |
10	| Backend connectivity | mock-only |
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Roles & Permissions
15	
16	**Template:** `custom`
17	
18	| Permission | Visitor | Support Agent | Admin |
19	|---|---|---|---|
20	| View main dashboard | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
21	
22	**Role definitions** (from intake and `requirements.md` §3 / §6.5):
23	
24	- **Visitor:** can sign in, submit an enquiry and view their own submissions (read-only). Lands on the Contact form. Cannot see the Inbox or other people's enquiries, and cannot change status or delete.
25	- **Support Agent:** can view all enquiries, search and filter them, move status from New to In Progress to Resolved, and resolve an enquiry with a mandatory reply note. Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form or delete.
26	- **Admin:** has every Support Agent permission and can also delete an enquiry (behind a confirmation). Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form.
27	
28	Denied actions are **hidden** in the UI, not shown as disabled. Opening a role-restricted page through a direct link shows a permission-denied banner on the page, not a generic 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05 / UF-09).
29	
30	> Permissions extend during BUILD as new stories surface new actions. Additions are recorded here as they come up, with your approval. Removing a permission, or changing who the roles are, stops for you to review.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Authentication
35	
36	| Field | Value |
37	|---|---|
38	| Method | `server-side` (BFF: your own server) |
39	| Auth login endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Auth is simulated by client-side stubs (`requirements.md` PI-01); no real backend endpoint |
40	| Auth userinfo endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
41	| Auth logout endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
42	| Custom auth notes | Auth is simulated client-side, as the prototype invariants require. The BFF shape follows the template's server-side auth policy. Sign-in uses email and password, then sends each role to its landing page (Visitor to the Contact form; Support Agent and Admin to the Inbox). Seeded users: `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin). |
43	
44	> Auth method is never inferred — the user must confirm explicitly per [authentication-intake.md](.claude/policies/authentication-intake.md).
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Data Source & Backend Integration
49	
50	| Field | Value |
51	|---|---|
52	| Data source | `mock-only` |
53	| Backend status | `N/A` (none) |
54	| Mock layer required | yes. In-memory fixtures built from `requirements.md`: a few seeded enquiries covering all three categories (Feedback / Question / General Enquiry) and all three statuses (New / In Progress / Resolved), plus the three seeded users. Changes last for the session but not past a reload (PI-02). Emails and notifications show only as UI confirmations (PI-04). |
55	
56	### API specs
57	
58	No OpenAPI spec was provided. The domain entities (Enquiry, User) are defined in `documentation/requirements.md` §7.
59	
60	---
61	
62	## Compliance
63	
64	**Applicable domains:** None (the user confirmed the project is not regulated)
65	**Region (if Personal data applies):** N/A
66	
67	### Compliance Requirements
68	
69	No compliance domains were identified during intake screening.
70	
71	- Note: the app does collect personal data (name, email, optional address). Only authenticated back-office roles (Support Agent, Admin) can see enquiries. Visitors never see anyone else's (`requirements.md` §6.6.1, BR-04).
72	
73	---
74	
75	## Styling & Branding
76	
77	| Field | Value |
78	|---|---|
79	| Primary brand color | `#2563eb` [INFERRED] the user asked for template defaults with no bespoke design system, so this is the styling-centralisation Pattern A default (Tailwind blue-600) |
80	| Accent / secondary | `#64748b` [INFERRED] a neutral accent from Tailwind `slate`, per the Pattern A default |
81	| Background (light) | `#ffffff` [INFERRED] the default for a neutral light palette |
82	| Background (dark, if applicable) | N/A |
83	| Font family (headings) | [INFERRED] system UI stack (Pattern A default; no font named in the sources) |
84	| Font family (body) | [INFERRED] system UI stack (Pattern A default; no font named in the sources) |
85	| Theme | [INFERRED] light only (Pattern A default; dark mode can be added later) |
86	| Source | defaulted (user: "template Shadcn defaults with a clean, neutral palette and centralised styling tokens") |
87	
88	> Component-specific styling (button radii, card shadows, etc.) emerges during BUILD. This section captures only palette intent and typography per [styling-centralisation.md](.claude/policies/styling-centralisation.md).
89	
90	---
91	
92	## Baseline NFRs
93	
94	- **NFR-base-1:** Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 Level AA (`requirements.md` §6.6.3 raises this above the 2.1 AA baseline). Primary flows are keyboard-first, status colour is always paired with an icon or text, and icon-only controls have a tooltip and an `aria-label`
95	- **NFR-base-2:** Performance: First Contentful Paint < 2.5s on a mid-tier mobile network
96	- **NFR-base-3:** Responsive design: mobile (≥360px) / tablet (≥768px) / desktop (≥1280px) breakpoints
97	- **NFR-base-4:** Browser support: latest two versions of Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari
98	- **NFR-base-5:** Error UX: every async operation shows a visible error state with a way to retry
99	- **NFR-base-6:** [INFERRED] Session policy: 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout, and lockout for 15 minutes after 5 failed sign-in attempts. Carried over from `requirements.md` §6.6.1, which marks these values as inferred. Auth is simulated (PI-01), so this behaviour is shown in the UI only
100	- **NFR-base-7:** Personal-data visibility: an enquirer's name, email and address are shown only to authenticated back-office roles and never to other Visitors (`requirements.md` §6.6.1, confirmed at intake)
101

1	# Epic Brief: Sign-in and App Shell
2	
3	*Inherits roles, auth, data source, compliance, and styling from project.md.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	Everyone signs in with email and password, lands on the right page for their role, sees only the menu items their role allows, and gets a clear on-page message if they open a page they can't use.
10	
11	This epic delivers the shared foundation the rest of the app builds on: the sign-in screen and its failure handling, the session rules (idle and absolute timeouts, lockout after repeated failures), the role-scoped app shell and top-level navigation, the in-page permission-denied banner, and the in-memory data layer (the Enquiry and User records with seeded sample data) that later epics read from and write to (`requirements.md` §5 Flow: Authentication, G-06, F-01, UF-09, UF-10, BR-05, §6.6.1, §7, PI-01, PI-02).
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Data Model
16	
17	Source: `documentation/requirements.md` §2 and §7. No OpenAPI spec or design was provided.
18	
19	### Enquiry
20	
21	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
22	|---|---|---|---|---|
23	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
24	| Name | string | yes | non-empty; max 120 chars | Primary identifier in the inbox |
25	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Reply-to |
26	| Address | string | no | max 255 chars | Optional |
27	| Category | enum | yes | exactly one of `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` | |
28	| Comment | string | yes | non-empty; min 10, max 2000 chars | Enquiry body |
29	| Status | enum | yes | exactly one of `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` | `Resolved` is terminal |
30	| ReplyNote | string | no | required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 chars | Read-only after resolution |
31	| SubmittedAt | datetime | yes | system-assigned (ISO-8601) | |
32	| SubmittedByEmail | string | yes | mirrors the submitting Visitor | Scopes "My messages" |
33	| HandledBy | string | no | mirrors the acting back-office user | Set when status first changes |
34	
35	### User
36	
37	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
38	|---|---|---|---|---|
39	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
40	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Sign-in identifier |
41	| FirstName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
42	| LastName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
43	| Password | string | yes | min complexity per policy | Write-only; never displayed |
44	| Role | enum | yes | exactly one of `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` | Drives landing page, navigation and access |
45	
46	### Seeded data
47	
48	- **Users:** `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin) (project.md §Authentication).
49	- **Enquiries:** a small set that together covers every Category (Feedback, Question, General Enquiry) and every Status (New, In Progress, Resolved). Resolved enquiries carry a Reply Note. At least one enquiry is submitted by the seeded Visitor so "My messages" has content.
50	- **Persistence:** changes last for the browser session and are lost on reload (PI-02).
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Functional Requirements
55	
56	- **R1:** A user can sign in with an email and password; on success a Visitor lands on the Contact form and a Support Agent or Admin lands on the Inbox.
57	- **R2:** When sign-in fails, an inline error on the sign-in screen tells the user whether the email/password was wrong or whether there was a connection problem.
58	- **R3:** A signed-in session ends after 30 minutes of inactivity or 12 hours in total, whichever comes first, and the user is returned to the sign-in screen.
59	- **R4:** After 5 failed sign-in attempts for an account, that account is locked for 15 minutes and the sign-in screen says it is locked and for how long.
60	- **R5:** The top-level navigation shows a Visitor only "Contact" and "My messages", and shows a Support Agent or Admin only "Inbox"; menu items a role can't use are hidden, not shown disabled.
61	- **R6:** A signed-in user who opens a page their role can't use through a direct link sees an in-page permission-denied banner that names the missing permission and gives a link back to their own landing page, never a generic 403 page.
62	- **R7:** The app holds Enquiry records with the fields listed in the Data Model, where Status is exactly New / In Progress / Resolved and Category is exactly Feedback / Question / General Enquiry.
63	- **R8:** The app starts with seeded sample enquiries covering every category and every status, plus the three seeded users; changes made during a session persist until the page is reloaded.
64	- **R9:** Every screen this epic delivers meets WCAG 2.2 AA, can be operated with the keyboard alone, and never uses status colour without an accompanying icon or text label.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Business Rules
69	
70	- **BR1:** A user who is not signed in and opens any app page is sent to the sign-in screen.
71	- **BR2:** After sign-in, routing is decided only by the user's role: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent or Admin → Inbox.
72	- **BR3:** Actions and menu items a role is denied are hidden, never rendered disabled (`requirements.md` §6.5 notes).
73	- **BR4:** Reaching a role-restricted page by direct link shows the permission-denied banner in the page, not a 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05).
74	- **BR5:** A locked account cannot sign in, even with the correct password, until the 15-minute lockout has passed.
75	- **BR6:** Session timeouts and lockout are simulated in the browser (PI-01); there is no server-side enforcement.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## Key Workflows
80	
81	### Sign in
82	
83	1. An unauthenticated user opens the app and is shown the sign-in screen.
84	2. They enter their email and password and submit.
85	3. On success they land on their role's page: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent / Admin → Inbox.
86	4. On failure an inline error explains whether the credentials were wrong or the connection failed; the entered email is kept.
87	5. On the 5th consecutive failure the account is locked for 15 minutes and the screen says so.
88	
89	### Navigate the app shell
90	
91	1. A signed-in user sees a top navigation with only the items their role allows (Visitor: Contact, My messages; Support Agent / Admin: Inbox).
92	2. They can sign out from the shell and return to the sign-in screen.
93	
94	### Open a page you can't use
95	
96	1. A signed-in user follows a direct link to a page outside their role (for example, a Visitor opens the Inbox).
97	2. The page shows a permission-denied banner naming the missing permission.
98	3. The banner offers a link back to their own landing page.
99	
100	### Session expiry
101	
102	1. A signed-in user is inactive for 30 minutes, or has been signed in for 12 hours.
103	2. The session ends and they are returned to the sign-in screen with a message that their session expired.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## Feature NFRs
108	
109	- **NFR1:** The sign-in form is fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: labelled fields, errors announced to assistive technology and linked to their fields, focus moved to the error summary on a failed submit.
110	- **NFR2:** The permission-denied banner is announced to assistive technology when the page loads and its "back" link is reachable by keyboard.
111	- **NFR3:** Password field input is masked and the password is never shown or logged.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Out of Scope
116	
117	- The Contact form, confirmation page, My messages list, Inbox table, enquiry detail, status changes and delete. Later epics deliver these; this epic only routes to their pages and guards access to them.
118	- The reviewer role switcher (`requirements.md` PI-05), dropped by user decision. Reviewers sign in as each seeded user instead.
119	- Real authentication, password reset, registration, and account management.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Notes & Caveats
124	
125	- **Landing pages before their epics exist:** the Contact form, My messages and Inbox are built in later epics. This epic needs a minimal destination for each so that sign-in routing, navigation and the permission-denied banner can be tested. Later epics replace these placeholders.
126	- **"Connection problem" under simulated auth:** auth is simulated in the browser (PI-01), so there is no real network failure. The way BUILD triggers and tests the connection-problem error (for example, a stub failure mode) still needs deciding.
127	- **Session and lockout values are inferred:** `requirements.md` §6.6.1 marks the 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout and 5-failure / 15-minute lockout as inferred defaults (project.md NFR-base-6). Confirm before BUILD if they matter.
128	- **Server-side auth vs. simulated auth:** project.md records the method as `server-side` (BFF), but every auth endpoint is N/A because auth is simulated client-side. Confirm the stub follows the server-side auth pattern's shape (for example, session handling behind a route) rather than a purely client-side flag.
129	- **Wording of the "missing permission":** the banner must name the missing permission (UF-09), but project.md's permissions matrix only has "View main dashboard" so far. Permission names such as "View inbox" or "Submit an enquiry" will be added to project.md during BUILD, with your approval.
130	- **Seed data is defined here, used later:** the seeded enquiries are only displayed in later epics. This epic delivers the data layer and seed. Its tests can check the seed's shape (every category and status present) but not how it is shown on screen.
131

    data layer. Auth follows a server-side (BFF) session shape; the backend is

          $ref: "#/components/responses/ServerError"

            $ref: "#/components/schemas/EnquiryCategory"

          in: query
          schema:

            maximum: 100
            default: 20

            type: integer
            minimum: 0

Cookies will be sent only if the API is same-origin with the web app. The API base URL is `http://localhost:3001/api`, so if the web app runs on a different origin, the session cookie will not be sent. I did not change `client.ts`, per the rules.

1	# Agent Startup (shared)
2	
3	Rules every workflow agent follows. Referenced from individual agent files.
4	
5	---
6	
7	**File operations:** Use `Read` / `Grep` / `Glob` / `Write` / `Edit` for file work — including inspecting installed packages under `node_modules/`. Reserve Bash for `node` *scripts* (not `node -e`), `git`, and `ls`. Do NOT use `find`, `sed`, `awk`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `python3`, `perl`, `cut`, or `grep` via Bash, and never use an interpreter to read, modify, or inspect files or packages — `node -e` / `python3 -c` / `find -exec` / `perl -i` / `sed -i` (use `Edit`/`Write` to change a file — never `node -e "fs.writeFileSync(...)"` or `perl -i`/`sed -i`). Inline / in-place code execution is never auto-approved. Full policy: [`.claude/policies/file-operations.md`](../policies/file-operations.md).
8	
9	**Running dev tools:** Run the project's npm scripts from `web/` in a subshell — `(cd web && npm run <script>)` for tsc/eslint/build/etc. and `(cd web && npm test -- <pattern>)` for Vitest — all auto-approved. The `( … )` runs the command in `web/` (so `web/vitest.config.ts` and the `@/` alias resolve) while leaving the shell's cwd at the repo root. Never run these from the repo root: a bare `npx vitest` loads no `web/vitest.config.ts` (the `@/` alias breaks) and `npm --prefix web test` crashes Vitest 4's worker pool at collection ("No test suite found" on Windows/Node 24 — see `generated-docs/template-feedback.md`). Playwright is the same: `(cd web && npm run test:e2e -- <args>)`. Pass Node flags inside the subshell (`(cd web && NODE_OPTIONS=… npm test)`); a direct `node ./node_modules/<tool>/…` call is NOT auto-approved.
10	
11	**Canonical dirs live at the repo root — never under `web/`.** `generated-docs/` and `.claude/` belong at the project root only. Two rules keep them there: (1) never leave the shell parked in `web/` — the bash CWD persists across calls, so a stray bare `cd web` makes a later relative write land in `web/generated-docs/` (always use the **subshell** form `(cd web && …)` for commands that must run in `web/` — the parentheses scope the `cd` to that one command and never move the persistent cwd); (2) when writing artifacts, prefer the repo-root-relative path (`generated-docs/…`) or an absolute path. The workflow scripts self-anchor to the repo root via [`lib/project-root.js`](../scripts/lib/project-root.js), so you never pass `--root`. A PreToolUse guard blocks writes that nest a canonical dir under `web/`, but don't rely on it — get the path right.
12	
13	**AskUserQuestion:** Subagents cannot call `AskUserQuestion` — return findings to the orchestrator instead.

1	# Epic Brief: Sign-in and App Shell
2	
3	*Inherits roles, auth, data source, compliance, and styling from project.md.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	Everyone signs in with email and password, lands on the right page for their role, sees only the menu items their role allows, and gets a clear on-page message if they open a page they can't use.
10	
11	This epic delivers the shared foundation the rest of the app builds on: the sign-in screen and its failure handling, the session rules (idle and absolute timeouts, lockout after repeated failures), the role-scoped app shell and top-level navigation, the in-page permission-denied banner, and the in-memory data layer (the Enquiry and User records with seeded sample data) that later epics read from and write to (`requirements.md` §5 Flow: Authentication, G-06, F-01, UF-09, UF-10, BR-05, §6.6.1, §7, PI-01, PI-02).
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Data Model
16	
17	Source: `documentation/requirements.md` §2 and §7. No OpenAPI spec or design was provided.
18	
19	### Enquiry
20	
21	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
22	|---|---|---|---|---|
23	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
24	| Name | string | yes | non-empty; max 120 chars | Primary identifier in the inbox |
25	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Reply-to |
26	| Address | string | no | max 255 chars | Optional |
27	| Category | enum | yes | exactly one of `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` | |
28	| Comment | string | yes | non-empty; min 10, max 2000 chars | Enquiry body |
29	| Status | enum | yes | exactly one of `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` | `Resolved` is terminal |
30	| ReplyNote | string | no | required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 chars | Read-only after resolution |
31	| SubmittedAt | datetime | yes | system-assigned (ISO-8601) | |
32	| SubmittedByEmail | string | yes | mirrors the submitting Visitor | Scopes "My messages" |
33	| HandledBy | string | no | mirrors the acting back-office user | Set when status first changes |
34	
35	### User
36	
37	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
38	|---|---|---|---|---|
39	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
40	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Sign-in identifier |
41	| FirstName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
42	| LastName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
43	| Password | string | yes | min complexity per policy | Write-only; never displayed |
44	| Role | enum | yes | exactly one of `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` | Drives landing page, navigation and access |
45	
46	### Seeded data
47	
48	- **Users:** `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin) (project.md §Authentication).
49	- **Enquiries:** a small set that together covers every Category (Feedback, Question, General Enquiry) and every Status (New, In Progress, Resolved). Resolved enquiries carry a Reply Note. At least one enquiry is submitted by the seeded Visitor so "My messages" has content.
50	- **Persistence:** changes last for the browser session and are lost on reload (PI-02).
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Functional Requirements
55	
56	- **R1:** A user can sign in with an email and password; on success a Visitor lands on the Contact form and a Support Agent or Admin lands on the Inbox.
57	- **R2:** When sign-in fails, an inline error on the sign-in screen tells the user whether the email/password was wrong or whether there was a connection problem.
58	- **R3:** A signed-in session ends after 30 minutes of inactivity or 12 hours in total, whichever comes first, and the user is returned to the sign-in screen.
59	- **R4:** After 5 failed sign-in attempts for an account, that account is locked for 15 minutes and the sign-in screen says it is locked and for how long.
60	- **R5:** The top-level navigation shows a Visitor only "Contact" and "My messages", and shows a Support Agent or Admin only "Inbox"; menu items a role can't use are hidden, not shown disabled.
61	- **R6:** A signed-in user who opens a page their role can't use through a direct link sees an in-page permission-denied banner that names the missing permission and gives a link back to their own landing page, never a generic 403 page.
62	- **R7:** The app holds Enquiry records with the fields listed in the Data Model, where Status is exactly New / In Progress / Resolved and Category is exactly Feedback / Question / General Enquiry.
63	- **R8:** The app starts with seeded sample enquiries covering every category and every status, plus the three seeded users; changes made during a session persist until the page is reloaded.
64	- **R9:** Every screen this epic delivers meets WCAG 2.2 AA, can be operated with the keyboard alone, and never uses status colour without an accompanying icon or text label.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Business Rules
69	
70	- **BR1:** A user who is not signed in and opens any app page is sent to the sign-in screen.
71	- **BR2:** After sign-in, routing is decided only by the user's role: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent or Admin → Inbox.
72	- **BR3:** Actions and menu items a role is denied are hidden, never rendered disabled (`requirements.md` §6.5 notes).
73	- **BR4:** Reaching a role-restricted page by direct link shows the permission-denied banner in the page, not a 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05).
74	- **BR5:** A locked account cannot sign in, even with the correct password, until the 15-minute lockout has passed.
75	- **BR6:** Session timeouts and lockout are simulated in the browser (PI-01); there is no server-side enforcement.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## Key Workflows
80	
81	### Sign in
82	
83	1. An unauthenticated user opens the app and is shown the sign-in screen.
84	2. They enter their email and password and submit.
85	3. On success they land on their role's page: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent / Admin → Inbox.
86	4. On failure an inline error explains whether the credentials were wrong or the connection failed; the entered email is kept.
87	5. On the 5th consecutive failure the account is locked for 15 minutes and the screen says so.
88	
89	### Navigate the app shell
90	
91	1. A signed-in user sees a top navigation with only the items their role allows (Visitor: Contact, My messages; Support Agent / Admin: Inbox).
92	2. They can sign out from the shell and return to the sign-in screen.
93	
94	### Open a page you can't use
95	
96	1. A signed-in user follows a direct link to a page outside their role (for example, a Visitor opens the Inbox).
97	2. The page shows a permission-denied banner naming the missing permission.
98	3. The banner offers a link back to their own landing page.
99	
100	### Session expiry
101	
102	1. A signed-in user is inactive for 30 minutes, or has been signed in for 12 hours.
103	2. The session ends and they are returned to the sign-in screen with a message that their session expired.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## Feature NFRs
108	
109	- **NFR1:** The sign-in form is fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: labelled fields, errors announced to assistive technology and linked to their fields, focus moved to the error summary on a failed submit.
110	- **NFR2:** The permission-denied banner is announced to assistive technology when the page loads and its "back" link is reachable by keyboard.
111	- **NFR3:** Password field input is masked and the password is never shown or logged.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Out of Scope
116	
117	- The Contact form, confirmation page, My messages list, Inbox table, enquiry detail, status changes and delete. Later epics deliver these; this epic only routes to their pages and guards access to them.
118	- The reviewer role switcher (`requirements.md` PI-05), dropped by user decision. Reviewers sign in as each seeded user instead.
119	- Real authentication, password reset, registration, and account management.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Notes & Caveats
124	
125	- **Landing pages before their epics exist:** the Contact form, My messages and Inbox are built in later epics. This epic needs a minimal destination for each so that sign-in routing, navigation and the permission-denied banner can be tested. Later epics replace these placeholders.
126	- **"Connection problem" under simulated auth:** auth is simulated in the browser (PI-01), so there is no real network failure. The way BUILD triggers and tests the connection-problem error (for example, a stub failure mode) still needs deciding.
127	- **Session and lockout values are inferred:** `requirements.md` §6.6.1 marks the 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout and 5-failure / 15-minute lockout as inferred defaults (project.md NFR-base-6). Confirm before BUILD if they matter.
128	- **Server-side auth vs. simulated auth:** project.md records the method as `server-side` (BFF), but every auth endpoint is N/A because auth is simulated client-side. Confirm the stub follows the server-side auth pattern's shape (for example, session handling behind a route) rather than a purely client-side flag.
129	- **Wording of the "missing permission":** the banner must name the missing permission (UF-09), but project.md's permissions matrix only has "View main dashboard" so far. Permission names such as "View inbox" or "Submit an enquiry" will be added to project.md during BUILD, with your approval.
130	- **Seed data is defined here, used later:** the seeded enquiries are only displayed in later epics. This epic delivers the data layer and seed. Its tests can check the seed's shape (every category and status present) but not how it is shown on screen.
131

316-
317-Mock data has **one home per entity, shared project-wide** — not one file per epic. A per-epic file just relocates duplication to the epic boundary: three epics that all touch `Transaction` would each redefine it and drift apart — the same all-green-all-wrong failure, moved one level up. Two layers instead:
318-
319-**Entity factories — `web/src/mocks/data/<entity>.ts`, one per entity, project-wide.** The single source of truth for an entity's shape **and** its canonical default values: a `create<Entity>(overrides?)` factory typed against `web/src/types/api-generated.ts` when it exists (else the brief's Data Model). Every epic and every test layer that touches that entity imports the same factory.
320-
321-```typescript
322-// web/src/mocks/data/transaction.ts
323-import type { Transaction } from '@/types/api-generated';
324-
325-export const createTransaction = (overrides: Partial<Transaction> = {}): Transaction => ({
326-  id: 'TXN-0001',
327-  amount: 125430.5,
328-  status: 'pending',

One definition, exercised identically by both test layers and the manual-test approval — this is exactly the contract the v07 nav bug diverged on.

Compose the entity factories inline in tests (`createTransaction({ status: 'approved' })`); only promote a composition to a named export (in the entity file, or a small `web/src/mocks/scenarios/epic-<slug>.ts`) when it's reused across stories or across the Vitest/Playwright boundary. 1	# Contact & Enquiry Management
2	
3	A contact-and-enquiry app where a Visitor sends an enquiry (name, email, optional address, a category, and a comment) and gets confirmation straight away. Back-office staff work through the enquiries: a Support Agent moves each one through New, In Progress and Resolved, and an Admin can also delete enquiries. Enquiries are scoped by role, so a Visitor sees only their own.
4	
5	| Field | Value |
6	|---|---|
7	| Project slug | `contact-form` |
8	| Created | 2026-11-03T07:17:19Z |
9	| Intake source | docs (`documentation/requirements.md`) |
10	| Backend connectivity | mock-only |
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Roles & Permissions
15	
16	**Template:** `custom`
17	
18	| Permission | Visitor | Support Agent | Admin |
19	|---|---|---|---|
20	| View main dashboard | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
21	
22	**Role definitions** (from intake and `requirements.md` §3 / §6.5):
23	
24	- **Visitor:** can sign in, submit an enquiry and view their own submissions (read-only). Lands on the Contact form. Cannot see the Inbox or other people's enquiries, and cannot change status or delete.
25	- **Support Agent:** can view all enquiries, search and filter them, move status from New to In Progress to Resolved, and resolve an enquiry with a mandatory reply note. Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form or delete.
26	- **Admin:** has every Support Agent permission and can also delete an enquiry (behind a confirmation). Lands on the Inbox. Cannot submit through the public form.
27	
28	Denied actions are **hidden** in the UI, not shown as disabled. Opening a role-restricted page through a direct link shows a permission-denied banner on the page, not a generic 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05 / UF-09).
29	
30	> Permissions extend during BUILD as new stories surface new actions. Additions are recorded here as they come up, with your approval. Removing a permission, or changing who the roles are, stops for you to review.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Authentication
35	
36	| Field | Value |
37	|---|---|
38	| Method | `server-side` (BFF: your own server) |
39	| Auth login endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Auth is simulated by client-side stubs (`requirements.md` PI-01); no real backend endpoint |
40	| Auth userinfo endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
41	| Auth logout endpoint (if server-side) | N/A. Simulated (PI-01) |
42	| Custom auth notes | Auth is simulated client-side, as the prototype invariants require. The BFF shape follows the template's server-side auth policy. Sign-in uses email and password, then sends each role to its landing page (Visitor to the Contact form; Support Agent and Admin to the Inbox). Seeded users: `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin). |
43	
44	> Auth method is never inferred — the user must confirm explicitly per [authentication-intake.md](.claude/policies/authentication-intake.md).
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Data Source & Backend Integration
49	
50	| Field | Value |
51	|---|---|
52	| Data source | `mock-only` |
53	| Backend status | `N/A` (none) |
54	| Mock layer required | yes. In-memory fixtures built from `requirements.md`: a few seeded enquiries covering all three categories (Feedback / Question / General Enquiry) and all three statuses (New / In Progress / Resolved), plus the three seeded users. Changes last for the session but not past a reload (PI-02). Emails and notifications show only as UI confirmations (PI-04). |
55	
56	### API specs
57	
58	No OpenAPI spec was provided. The domain entities (Enquiry, User) are defined in `documentation/requirements.md` §7.
59

337	**Both test layers consume the same factories.** Vitest imports via the `@/` alias (`@/mocks/data/transaction`); Playwright imports via a **relative** path from `e2e/` (`../src/mocks/data/identity`) to dodge alias resolution at Playwright runtime. So every module under `web/src/mocks/` that the e2e layer can import — entity factories in `data/` **and** scenario fixtures in `scenarios/` — must import **types** with `import type` only (erased at compile) and import **sibling/peer factories** by relative path (`./user`, or `../data/transaction` from a `scenarios/` file), never the `@/` alias — that keeps each module importable from the e2e layer without any alias plumbing. (The `@/` alias is fine in Vitest test files and in app-runtime code like `web/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, which Playwright never imports relatively — the rule is only for the modules an e2e spec reaches through a relative import.)
338	
339	**The runtime mock layer consumes them too.** When the project ships MSW handlers (`web/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, the running-app mock used in mock mode), they compose the same factories — `createX(overrides)` for entity bodies, `userInfoFor(role)` for auth — so the dev/demo app and the tests can't drift onto different contracts. The handler keeps the *serving* logic (filtering, pagination, ≥2-per-enum dataset sizing); only the entity *shape + defaults* come from the factory. So all three mock surfaces — Vitest, Playwright, and the MSW runtime — draw from one source. See [mock-setup-agent § Generate handlers](../agents/mock-setup-agent.md#step-3--generate-websrcmockshandlersts).
340	
341	**Evolving an entity:** when an epic genuinely adds a field, **extend** the one entity file (a deliberate, reviewable edit — journal it as a Tier-2 factual addition); never copy the entity into a new file. The per-entity files are a coordinated shared surface across epic branches: real edit-conflicts are rare (definitions are append-mostly), and when they do happen they're a genuine shared-contract change governed by [epic-branch-concurrency §6.2](./epic-branch-concurrency.md). Duplication, by contrast, guarantees silent drift.

import type { Enquiry } from '@/types/api-generated';

export const createEnquiry = (overrides: Partial<Enquiry> = {}): Enquiry => ({
  id: 1,
  name: 'Vera Visitor',
  email: 'visitor@example.com',
  address: '12 Harbour Road, Cape Town',
  category: 'Question',
  comment: 'Could you tell me when your support desk is open over the holidays?',
  status: 'New',
  replyNote: null,
  submittedAt: '2026-10-28T09:15:00.000Z',
  submittedByEmail: 'visitor@example.com',
  handledBy: null,
  ...overrides,
});

/**
 * Seed set (brief §Seeded data): every Category and every Status appears at least twice,
 * Resolved enquiries carry a Reply Note, and the seeded Visitor owns several so
 * "My messages" has content.
 */
export const seededEnquiries: readonly Enquiry[] = [
  createEnquiry({
    id: 1,
    category: 'Question',
    status: 'New',
  }),
  createEnquiry({
    id: 2,
    name: 'Vera Visitor',
    category: 'Feedback',
    comment: 'The new opening hours are much more convenient — thank you for the change.',
    status: 'Resolved',
    replyNote: 'Thanks for letting us know. We have shared your feedback with the team.',
    submittedAt: '2026-10-20T14:02:00.000Z',
    handledBy: 'agent@example.com',
  }),
  createEnquiry({
    id: 3,
    name: 'Daniel Mokoena',
    email: 'daniel.mokoena@example.org',
    address: null,
    category: 'General Enquiry',
    comment: 'I would like to know whether you offer group bookings for schools.',
    status: 'In Progress',
    submittedAt: '2026-10-25T11:40:00.000Z',
    submittedByEmail: 'daniel.mokoena@example.org',
    handledBy: 'agent@example.com',
  }),
  createEnquiry({
    id: 4,
    name: 'Priya Naidoo',
    email: 'priya.naidoo@example.org',
    address: '7 Long Street, Durban',
    category: 'Feedback',
    comment: 'The checkout page kept timing out on my phone yesterday evening.',
    status: 'New',
    submittedAt: '2026-10-30T18:25:00.000Z',
    submittedByEmail: 'priya.naidoo@example.org',
  }),
  createEnquiry({
    id: 5,
    name: 'Vera Visitor',
    category: 'General Enquiry',
    comment: 'Please update the postal address on my account to the new one.',
    status: 'In Progress',
    submittedAt: '2026-10-26T08:05:00.000Z',
    handledBy: 'admin@example.com',
  }),
  createEnquiry({
    id: 6,
    name: 'Tom Fischer',
    email: 'tom.fischer@example.net',
    address: null,
    category: 'Question',
    comment: 'Is there a way to download my past invoices as a PDF?',
    status: 'Resolved',
    replyNote: 'Yes — open Billing, choose an invoice and select Download PDF.',
    submittedAt: '2026-10-18T10:30:00.000Z',
    submittedByEmail: 'tom.fischer@example.net',
    handledBy: 'admin@example.com',
  }),
];

102:### `generated-docs/architecture.md` — the architecture & reuse registry
103-
104-A project-wide, cumulative registry of what the codebase already provides, so later stories **reuse instead of reinventing**. It is **read at the start of every story** and **edited inline** when a story adds a reusable surface — the same pattern as inline `brief.md` updates: the developer edits the file, the orchestrator stages it at commit time. It is **not** the per-epic journal — no narrative, no history, no dates.
105-
106-Fixed shape — three sections, nothing else:
107-
108-```
109-# Architecture & Reuse Registry
110-> One line per durable thing. Edit the line when it changes; delete it when the thing is gone.
111-> No story narrative, no dates, no rationale.
112-
113:## Shared utilities & components
114-| Export | Location | Capability |
115-| ... | ... | ... |
116-
117-## Conventions
118-- ...
119-
120-## Cross-epic debt
121-- ...
122-```
123-
124-**Keep it lean — five rules. The registry is worthless if it bloats past the point of being read at story start:**
125-
126-1. **One row per durable thing.** A new capability on an existing export is an **edit to its row**, never a new row. (`post()` gaining a params arg *then* Blob support is still one row.)
127-2. **Registry, not narrative.** No "Story N…", no dates, no rationale prose. If it reads like a journal entry, it does not belong here.
128-3. **Entry bar.** Only three kinds qualify: a reusable export later stories should consume; a cross-cutting convention; cross-epic debt. Tooling, test infra, one-offs, and speculation ("might be useful later") are excluded by definition.
129-4. **Delete on removal.** Remove or rename an export and its row goes in the same change. A row pointing at a non-existent export — or a new helper that duplicates an existing row — is a registry-hygiene regression, and a likely finding at the epic-end `/code-review` pass.
130-5. **Length is a signal.** It must stay short enough to read at story start. A section past ~12 rows, or a file past ~1 screen, is a consolidation signal — usually overlapping utilities that should be merged.
131-
132-### `state.json.epic.unverifiedAssumptions` — the user's confirm-before-merge ledger
133-
134-Already floated **first** at the manual-test approval ([continue.md](../commands/continue.md) B7.1) under "⚠️ Check these first." `feature-planner` seeds it; **BUILD agents append to it** whenever they make a call that depends on unverified external reality, or interpret a debatable requirement the user should confirm. This is the single user-facing channel for boundary uncertainty — it replaces the old `[review]` epic-summary callout, which the user saw only *after* merge.
135-
136-### `generated-docs/template-feedback.md` — maintainer channel
137-
138-Append-only, repo-global, release-ignored. The agent **works around** the template bug and logs it here — it **never halts** for a template bug. One entry per bug:
--

209-| **Structural contradiction** — what the code needs is incompatible with what the brief states | Tier 4 | Halt. User updates brief or confirms the change. |

213-- No, just extends or refines it → Tier 2
214-- No, but the interpretation might be wrong, or it depends on unverified reality → Tier 3 (route to the right audience)
215-- Yes — proceeding ships something the user didn't agree to → Tier 4

1	# Sign in, land on your page, and sign out
2	
3	Epic: Sign-in and App Shell (`sign-in-and-app-shell`)
4	
5	## Story metadata
6	
7	```yaml
8	index: 1
9	  title: Sign in, land on your page, and sign out
10	  slug: story-1-sign-in-and-sign-out
11	  plainSummary: You open the app, sign in with your email and password, and land on your role's page (a Visitor on the Contact form, a Support Agent or Admin on the Inbox). If sign-in fails you see a clear message on the sign-in screen, and you can sign out from any page.
12	  summary: Replaces the template's public welcome page with a sign-in screen at /login and an (authenticated) route group whose layout guards every app page through a server-side session check (BFF shape per the server-side auth pattern, backed by a simulated in-memory user store holding the three seeded users). Successful sign-in routes by role only (Visitor to /contact, Support Agent/Admin to /inbox); minimal placeholder pages for /contact, /my-messages and /inbox are created for later epics to replace. Failure shows an inline, accessible error (wrong credentials vs connection problem) with the email kept and focus moved to the error summary; sign-out clears the session and returns to sign-in, including on browser Back.
13	  requirementIds: [R1, R2, R8, R9, BR1, BR2, BR6, NFR1, NFR3]
14	  roles: [Visitor, Support Agent, Admin]
15	  route: /login
16	  targetFile: web/src/app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx
17	  pageAction: create_new
18	  isInfrastructureOnly: false
19	  acceptanceCriteria:
20	    - id: AC-1
21	      text: Signing in with a seeded account's correct email and password takes a Visitor to the Contact page and a Support Agent or Admin to the Inbox
22	      coverage: playwright
23	    - id: AC-2
24	      text: Submitting a wrong email or password shows an inline "email or password is incorrect" error on the sign-in screen, keeps the entered email, clears the password and moves focus to the error summary
25	      coverage: vitest
26	    - id: AC-3
27	      text: When sign-in cannot reach the sign-in service, the sign-in screen shows a connection-problem error that is distinct from the wrong-credentials error
28	      coverage: vitest
29	    - id: AC-4
30	      text: While signed out, any app URL typed into the address bar, including the app root, sends the user to the sign-in screen instead of the welcome page or the requested page
31	      coverage: playwright
32	    - id: AC-5
33	      text: After signing out, pressing the browser Back button returns the user to the sign-in screen rather than revealing the previous app page
34	      coverage: playwright
35	    - id: AC-6
36	      text: The sign-in screen has no automated accessibility violations, every field is labelled, and the whole form can be completed with the keyboard alone
37	      coverage: playwright
38	  manualTestChecklist:
39	    - Open the app while signed out → you land on the sign-in page, not a welcome page
40	    - Sign in as visitor@example.com / Test123 → you land on the Contact page
41	    - Sign in as agent@example.com (or admin@example.com) / Test123 → you land on the Inbox
42	    - Sign in with the wrong password → you see a message saying the email or password is incorrect, and your email is still filled in
43	    - Type the password → it is shown as dots, never as plain text
44	    - Sign in, click Sign out, then press the browser Back button → you're sent to sign-in, not back into the app
45	    - Using only the Tab and Enter keys, sign in successfully
46	  additionalTechnicalChecksCount: 2
47	
48	```
49	
50	## Resolved design choices
51	
52	None.
53	
54	## Infrastructure reuse notes (epic-wide)
55	
56	  - "API client in web/src/lib/api/client.ts — route the simulated sign-in, session and enquiry calls through it rather than calling fetch directly"
57	  - "Shadcn primitives already present in web/src/components/ui/ (button, card, input, label) — compose the sign-in form and banner from these; add alert via the Shadcn CLI if needed"
58	  - "Toast system in web/src/contexts/ToastContext.tsx and web/src/components/toast/ — reuse for any transient confirmation; the permission-denied banner and sign-in errors stay inline on the page"
59	  - "Zod schemas live in web/src/lib/validation/schemas.ts — add the sign-in and Enquiry schemas there"
60	  - "Template root web/src/app/page.tsx is a public welcome page — replace it with a redirect into the sign-in / role-landing flow (do not keep it reachable)"
61	  - "Follow the server-side auth pattern's file shape (lib/auth/authClient.ts, lib/auth/requireSession.ts, app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx, app/login/page.tsx, app/logout/route.ts) with the simulated user store behind it"

5	---
6	
7	**File operations:** Use `Read` / `Grep` / `Glob` / `Write` / `Edit` for file work — including inspecting installed packages under `node_modules/`. Reserve Bash for `node` *scripts* (not `node -e`), `git`, and `ls`. Do NOT use `find`, `sed`, `awk`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `python3`, `perl`, `cut`, or `grep` via Bash, and never use an interpreter to read, modify, or inspect files or packages — `node -e` / `python3 -c` / `find -exec` / `perl -i` / `sed -i` (use `Edit`/`Write` to change a file — never `node -e "fs.writeFileSync(...)"` or `perl -i`/`sed -i`). Inline / in-place code execution is never auto-approved. Full policy: [`.claude/policies/file-operations.md`](../policies/file-operations.md).
8	
9	**Running dev tools:** Run the project's npm scripts from `web/` in a subshell — `(cd web && npm run <script>)` for tsc/eslint/build/etc. and `(cd web && npm test -- <pattern>)` for Vitest — all auto-approved. The `( … )` runs the command in `web/` (so `web/vitest.config.ts` and the `@/` alias resolve) while leaving the shell's cwd at the repo root. Never run these from the repo root: a bare `npx vitest` loads no `web/vitest.config.ts` (the `@/` alias breaks) and `npm --prefix web test` crashes Vitest 4's worker pool at collection ("No test suite found" on Windows/Node 24 — see `generated-docs/template-feedback.md`). Playwright is the same: `(cd web && npm run test:e2e -- <args>)`. Pass Node flags inside the subshell (`(cd web && NODE_OPTIONS=… npm test)`); a direct `node ./node_modules/<tool>/…` call is NOT auto-approved.
10	
11	**Canonical dirs live at the repo root — never under `web/`.** `generated-docs/` and `.claude/` belong at the project root only. Two rules keep them there: (1) never leave the shell parked in `web/` — the bash CWD persists across calls, so a stray bare `cd web` makes a later relative write land in `web/generated-docs/` (always use the **subshell** form `(cd web && …)` for commands that must run in `web/` — the parentheses scope the `cd` to that one command and never move the persistent cwd); (2) when writing artifacts, prefer the repo-root-relative path (`generated-docs/…`) or an absolute path. The workflow scripts self-anchor to the repo root via [`lib/project-root.js`](../scripts/lib/project-root.js), so you never pass `--root`. A PreToolUse guard blocks writes that nest a canonical dir under `web/`, but don't rely on it — get the path right.
12	
13	**AskUserQuestion:** Subagents cannot call `AskUserQuestion` — return findings to the orchestrator instead.

1	# Epic Brief: Sign-in and App Shell
2	
3	*Inherits roles, auth, data source, compliance, and styling from project.md.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	Everyone signs in with email and password, lands on the right page for their role, sees only the menu items their role allows, and gets a clear on-page message if they open a page they can't use.
10	
11	This epic delivers the shared foundation the rest of the app builds on: the sign-in screen and its failure handling, the session rules (idle and absolute timeouts, lockout after repeated failures), the role-scoped app shell and top-level navigation, the in-page permission-denied banner, and the in-memory data layer (the Enquiry and User records with seeded sample data) that later epics read from and write to (`requirements.md` §5 Flow: Authentication, G-06, F-01, UF-09, UF-10, BR-05, §6.6.1, §7, PI-01, PI-02).
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Data Model
16	
17	Source: `documentation/requirements.md` §2 and §7. No OpenAPI spec or design was provided.
18	
19	### Enquiry
20	
21	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
22	|---|---|---|---|---|
23	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
24	| Name | string | yes | non-empty; max 120 chars | Primary identifier in the inbox |
25	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Reply-to |
26	| Address | string | no | max 255 chars | Optional |
27	| Category | enum | yes | exactly one of `Feedback`, `Question`, `General Enquiry` | |
28	| Comment | string | yes | non-empty; min 10, max 2000 chars | Enquiry body |
29	| Status | enum | yes | exactly one of `New`, `In Progress`, `Resolved` | `Resolved` is terminal |
30	| ReplyNote | string | no | required when Status is `Resolved`; max 1000 chars | Read-only after resolution |
31	| SubmittedAt | datetime | yes | system-assigned (ISO-8601) | |
32	| SubmittedByEmail | string | yes | mirrors the submitting Visitor | Scopes "My messages" |
33	| HandledBy | string | no | mirrors the acting back-office user | Set when status first changes |
34	
35	### User
36	
37	| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Notes |
38	|---|---|---|---|---|
39	| Id | integer | yes | system-assigned | Internal identifier |
40	| Email | string | yes | RFC-5322 email format | Sign-in identifier |
41	| FirstName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
42	| LastName | string | yes | non-empty; max 64 chars | |
43	| Password | string | yes | min complexity per policy | Write-only; never displayed |
44	| Role | enum | yes | exactly one of `Visitor`, `Support Agent`, `Admin` | Drives landing page, navigation and access |
45	
46	### Seeded data
47	
48	- **Users:** `visitor@example.com` / `Test123` (Visitor), `agent@example.com` / `Test123` (Support Agent), `admin@example.com` / `Test123` (Admin) (project.md §Authentication).
49	- **Enquiries:** a small set that together covers every Category (Feedback, Question, General Enquiry) and every Status (New, In Progress, Resolved). Resolved enquiries carry a Reply Note. At least one enquiry is submitted by the seeded Visitor so "My messages" has content.
50	- **Persistence:** changes last for the browser session and are lost on reload (PI-02).
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Functional Requirements
55	
56	- **R1:** A user can sign in with an email and password; on success a Visitor lands on the Contact form and a Support Agent or Admin lands on the Inbox.
57	- **R2:** When sign-in fails, an inline error on the sign-in screen tells the user whether the email/password was wrong or whether there was a connection problem.
58	- **R3:** A signed-in session ends after 30 minutes of inactivity or 12 hours in total, whichever comes first, and the user is returned to the sign-in screen.
59	- **R4:** After 5 failed sign-in attempts for an account, that account is locked for 15 minutes and the sign-in screen says it is locked and for how long.
60	- **R5:** The top-level navigation shows a Visitor only "Contact" and "My messages", and shows a Support Agent or Admin only "Inbox"; menu items a role can't use are hidden, not shown disabled.
61	- **R6:** A signed-in user who opens a page their role can't use through a direct link sees an in-page permission-denied banner that names the missing permission and gives a link back to their own landing page, never a generic 403 page.
62	- **R7:** The app holds Enquiry records with the fields listed in the Data Model, where Status is exactly New / In Progress / Resolved and Category is exactly Feedback / Question / General Enquiry.
63	- **R8:** The app starts with seeded sample enquiries covering every category and every status, plus the three seeded users; changes made during a session persist until the page is reloaded.
64	- **R9:** Every screen this epic delivers meets WCAG 2.2 AA, can be operated with the keyboard alone, and never uses status colour without an accompanying icon or text label.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Business Rules
69	
70	- **BR1:** A user who is not signed in and opens any app page is sent to the sign-in screen.
71	- **BR2:** After sign-in, routing is decided only by the user's role: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent or Admin → Inbox.
72	- **BR3:** Actions and menu items a role is denied are hidden, never rendered disabled (`requirements.md` §6.5 notes).
73	- **BR4:** Reaching a role-restricted page by direct link shows the permission-denied banner in the page, not a 403 page (`requirements.md` BR-05).
74	- **BR5:** A locked account cannot sign in, even with the correct password, until the 15-minute lockout has passed.
75	- **BR6:** Session timeouts and lockout are simulated in the browser (PI-01); there is no server-side enforcement.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## Key Workflows
80	
81	### Sign in
82	
83	1. An unauthenticated user opens the app and is shown the sign-in screen.
84	2. They enter their email and password and submit.
85	3. On success they land on their role's page: Visitor → Contact form; Support Agent / Admin → Inbox.
86	4. On failure an inline error explains whether the credentials were wrong or the connection failed; the entered email is kept.
87	5. On the 5th consecutive failure the account is locked for 15 minutes and the screen says so.
88	
89	### Navigate the app shell
90	
91	1. A signed-in user sees a top navigation with only the items their role allows (Visitor: Contact, My messages; Support Agent / Admin: Inbox).
92	2. They can sign out from the shell and return to the sign-in screen.
93	
94	### Open a page you can't use
95	
96	1. A signed-in user follows a direct link to a page outside their role (for example, a Visitor opens the Inbox).
97	2. The page shows a permission-denied banner naming the missing permission.
98	3. The banner offers a link back to their own landing page.
99	
100	### Session expiry
101	
102	1. A signed-in user is inactive for 30 minutes, or has been signed in for 12 hours.
103	2. The session ends and they are returned to the sign-in screen with a message that their session expired.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## Feature NFRs
108	
109	- **NFR1:** The sign-in form is fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: labelled fields, errors announced to assistive technology and linked to their fields, focus moved to the error summary on a failed submit.
110	- **NFR2:** The permission-denied banner is announced to assistive technology when the page loads and its "back" link is reachable by keyboard.
111	- **NFR3:** Password field input is masked and the password is never shown or logged.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Out of Scope
116	
117	- The Contact form, confirmation page, My messages list, Inbox table, enquiry detail, status changes and delete. Later epics deliver these; this epic only routes to their pages and guards access to them.
118	- The reviewer role switcher (`requirements.md` PI-05), dropped by user decision. Reviewers sign in as each seeded user instead.
119	- Real authentication, password reset, registration, and account management.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Notes & Caveats
124	
125	- **Landing pages before their epics exist:** the Contact form, My messages and Inbox are built in later epics. This epic needs a minimal destination for each so that sign-in routing, navigation and the permission-denied banner can be tested. Later epics replace these placeholders.
126	- **"Connection problem" under simulated auth:** auth is simulated in the browser (PI-01), so there is no real network failure. The way BUILD triggers and tests the connection-problem error (for example, a stub failure mode) still needs deciding.
127	- **Session and lockout values are inferred:** `requirements.md` §6.6.1 marks the 30-minute idle timeout, 12-hour absolute timeout and 5-failure / 15-minute lockout as inferred defaults (project.md NFR-base-6). Confirm before BUILD if they matter.
128	- **Server-side auth vs. simulated auth:** project.md records the method as `server-side` (BFF), but every auth endpoint is N/A because auth is simulated client-side. Confirm the stub follows the server-side auth pattern's shape (for example, session handling behind a route) rather than a purely client-side flag.
129	- **Wording of the "missing permission":** the banner must name the missing permission (UF-09), but project.md's permissions matrix only has "View main dashboard" so far. Permission names such as "View inbox" or "Submit an enquiry" will be added to project.md during BUILD, with your approval.
130	- **Seed data is defined here, used later:** the seeded enquiries are only displayed in later epics. This epic delivers the data layer and seed. Its tests can check the seed's shape (every category and status present) but not how it is shown on screen.
131
