1 # Testing Policy 2 3 Canonical operational checklist for testing, referenced by [`test-generator`](../agents/test-generator.md) and [`developer`](../agents/developer.md), and enforced by the `test-quality` gate in `quality-gates.js`. CLAUDE.md covers rationale. 4 5 --- 6 7 ## Where each scenario belongs 8 9 Every acceptance criterion carries **exactly one** coverage tag, assigned by the [feature-planner](../agents/feature-planner.md#coverage-tagging) at PLAN and rendered mechanically by `test-generator` (one tag → one test). Tag by **where the behaviour lives**, not by how thorough it would feel: 10 11 | The behaviour lives in… | Tag | Examples | 12 |---|---|---| 13 | the **React render** (jsdom-observable) | `vitest` (`web/src/__tests__/`) | role-gating, conditional UI, form-state, loading/empty/error states, hook behaviour, schema-driven form validation | 14 | the **browser + mocked-backend round-trip** | `playwright` (`web/e2e/`) | navigation/redirects, submit-and-see-next-page, the app's real `authorize()` against a mocked backend, role-aware visibility, route guards (middleware), localStorage across a real reload, filter/sort/pagination against mocked responses, drag/drop, downloads, file picker, **accessibility** (one real-browser `@axe-core/playwright` scan), **time-dependent flows** (`page.clock`) | 15 | **visual / assistive-tech / OS**, or **absorbed by a sibling AC's test** | `none` | screen-reader announcements, OS-level theme, human-eye contrast, cross-browser parity; or "another AC's test in this story already proves this" | 16 17 **One tag, one layer — no sibling tests across layers.** A sign-in redirect belongs in Playwright; the Vitest version would mock `signIn()` and recreate the exact blind spot the pipeline exists to close. The Playwright spec *is* the test. Vitest stays a respected, narrow tier — written exactly where it has value, never as a default or a "for completeness" duplicate. 18 19 **`none` is first-class.** Static chrome ("page has the heading 'File Logs'") and visual/AT/OS checks are tagged `none`; a `none` AC the user can still eyeball belongs in `manualTestChecklist`. 20 21 --- 22 23 ## Time-dependent behaviour 24 25 Timeouts, polling, debounce, auto-dismiss, countdowns — anything driven by the clock. 26 27 **Time-driven *flows* belong in Playwright, via [`page.clock`](https://playwright.dev/docs/clock) — not Vitest fake timers.** `page.clock.install()` then `fastForward('15:00')` / `runFor(1000)` / `pauseAt(...)` advances the browser clock deterministically against the **real** configured durations — no injected short values, no real elapsed time, and (the part that matters) **no test-only hooks in production code**. It also sidesteps the jsdom failure modes that make `vi.useFakeTimers()` fragile: it deadlocks RTL's `waitFor`/`findBy*` and hangs `axe()`. 28 29 Split the layers: 30 31 - **Flow** — warning modal appears before expiry, countdown ticks down, redirect fires on expiry, a control disables during a cooldown → `playwright` + `page.clock`. 32 - **Pure time arithmetic** — the idle-vs-absolute decision, "seconds remaining" math → extract it into a plain function/hook and unit-test with **explicit inputs in Vitest, no timers at all**. Prefer a timestamp-derived value (`Math.ceil((expiresAt - now) / 1000)`) over a `setInterval` that mutates its own state — it's deterministic and needs no clock to test. 33 - `vi.useFakeTimers()` is the **last resort** — only a genuinely component-local timer with no observable flow. If you reach for it, never run `axe()` in the same test (axe defers on `setTimeout` and will hang under a frozen fake clock) — accessibility is asserted by the Playwright `@axe-core/playwright` scan anyway. 34 35 **"Mounted app-wide / no page of its own" is not non-routable.** A session-timeout manager lives in the shell, but its effects are observable on any signed-in page — drive a browser to one and use `page.clock`. See [Non-routable Playwright stubs](#non-routable-playwright-stubs). 36 37 Two consequences worth banking: 38 39 - **Don't add test-only timing config to production.** Shortened-duration props/env switches exist only to make fake-timer tests bearable; `page.clock` exercises the real 15-min / 8-hr values instantly, so production keeps its real defaults and gains no test scaffolding. 40 - **Don't duplicate the durations as a manual step.** Because `page.clock` verifies the real configured values automatically, a `manualTestChecklist` item like "confirm the timeout fires at 15 minutes" is redundant — drop it. 41 42 --- 43 44 ## Accessibility 45 46 Asserted by a real-browser `@axe-core/playwright` scan in the routable story's Playwright spec — **not** `vitest-axe` in jsdom (which can't see contrast, layout, or focus order). 47 48 - **Scope to the standard.** Use the axe tags for every WCAG version and level up to `NFR-base-1`'s — 2.1 AA (the default) is `.withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])`; 2.2 AA adds `'wcag22aa'`. Axe's defaults also run *best-practice* rules; leaving them on fails specs on issues outside the agreed bar. 49 - **Scan each distinct state the story introduces** — happy path plus error / empty / open-modal / disabled — not just the default render. axe violations are usually state-specific, and a page-level scan only sees the states the spec drives to. 50 - **Scan a settled DOM** — await a stable element before scanning so the scan isn't racing a loading skeleton or an animation. 51 - A component with no routable surface of its own is covered when a routable page renders it; it is not separately axe-scanned in Vitest. The automated in-loop signal is the routable page's `@axe-core/playwright` scan (run batched at epic-end); the epic-end `/code-review` pass is a further backstop for semantic-HTML / ARIA / keyboard concerns. 52 53 --- 54 55 ## Test organization 56 57 | Directory | Contents | 58 |---|---| 59 | `web/src/__tests__/integration/` | Integration tests (primary focus) | 60 | `web/src/__tests__/scripts/` | Template tooling and script tests | 61 | `web/src/__tests__/api/` | API endpoint tests (if needed) | 62 | `web/e2e/` | Playwright specs | 63 64 File naming: `.test.ts` for non-React code, `.test.tsx` for React components/pages. Use descriptive names tied to the behavior under test. 65 66 --- 67 68 ## Per-epic baseline 69 70 Cross-story invariants live in **one file per epic**, not duplicated across every story's test file: 71 72 - File: `web/src/__tests__/integration/epic--baseline.test.tsx`. 73 - Created by **Story 1's** `test-generator` when the planner set `epicIntroducesSharedSurface: true` (the epic introduces a shared shell, `layout.tsx`, route group, or provider). 74 - Covers epic-wide invariants: role-gating that spans the epic's pages, shared-shell navigation, shared layout. (The epic's accessibility baseline is a `@axe-core/playwright` scan in the shared-surface story's Playwright spec — not this Vitest file.) 75 - **Later stories in the epic do NOT re-assert these** — their test files cover only the story's delta. If a later story introduces a *genuinely new* shared surface, extend the baseline (add only the new invariants) rather than recreating it. 76 77 --- 78 79 ## Test budget 80 81 **Tests = coverage tags.** The feature-planner assigns one `coverage` tag per (consolidated, ≤6) AC; `test-generator` renders one test per tag. There is no separate count target — the count is whatever the tags produce. 82 83 **Hard ceiling: 12 `it()` blocks per Vitest file and 12 `test()` blocks per Playwright spec.** A story file won't reach it — ≤6 ACs per story, one test per tag — so in practice the ceiling binds on the **per-epic baseline**, which grows as later stories extend it. A baseline at the ceiling means the epic carries more shared-surface invariants than one file should hold: `test-generator` emits at the ceiling and flags it for consolidation on its one-line `NOTE:` rather than letting the file grow. 84 85 ### Representative vs exhaustive 86 87 Consolidation happens at PLAN (one AC = "validates fields per the brief", not one AC per field), so one tag yields one representative test, not one per data point. 88 89 | Behavior | Representative (correct) | Exhaustive (wrong) | 90 |---|---|---| 91 | Pagination | Forward, backward, first-page disables prev, last-page disables next (4) | Pages 1–10 individually (10) | 92 | Sorting | Click → asc, click again → desc, verify one column (2-3) | Every column × both directions (12+) | 93 | Filtering | Apply filter → narrows, clear → restores, combine two (3) | Every filter value × every combination (20+) | 94 | Validation | One required empty, one invalid format, all valid (3) | Every field × every rule (15+) | 95 | Empty / error / loading | One each (3) | Multiple error codes × multiple empty scenarios (10+) | 96 97 When multiple tests differ only by a data value (column name, page number, filter option), that's a signal to test the mechanism once and trust the implementation. Use `it.each` sparingly — only for genuinely distinct edge cases (number vs date vs string formatting), never data variations. Keep `it.each` tables ≤5 rows. 98 99 --- 100 101 ## Query priority (accessibility-first) 102 103 | Priority | Query | When to use | 104 |---|---|---| 105 | 1 | `getByRole` | Buttons, links, headings, forms — **preferred for most elements** | 106 | 2 | `getByLabelText` | Form inputs with labels | 107 | 3 | `getByPlaceholderText` | Inputs without visible labels | 108 | 4 | `getByText` | Non-interactive content | 109 | 5 | `getByDisplayValue` | Filled form inputs | 110 | Last resort | `getByTestId` | Only when no semantic query works | 111 112 **`getByTestId` is an anti-pattern in most cases.** If you find yourself adding `data-testid` attributes, first ask: "Is there a semantic HTML element or ARIA role I should use instead?" The answer is usually yes. 113 114 --- 115 116 ## AC traceability 117 118 Every `it()` / `test()` block carries a `// AC-N` comment on the line above it. Multiple ACs can be comma-separated: 119 120 ```typescript 121 // AC-1, AC-3 122 it('displays payment list and handles API errors', () => { ... }); 123 ``` 124 125 --- 126 127 ## Anti-patterns (forbidden) 128 129 Tests must fail before implementation, import real production code (never mock the code under test), assert user-observable behavior, and follow the **No Error Suppressions** rule in CLAUDE.md. The patterns below are the recurring ways those principles get violated: 130 131 ### 1. No placeholder components inside test files 132 133 Every `import` must point to production code. If the component doesn't exist, that's the expected TDD failure — don't define a placeholder. 134 135 ```typescript 136 // WRONG — tests zero production code 137 const ExamplePage = () =>
Example
; 138 139 // CORRECT — import will fail until implemented 140 import { ExamplePage } from '@/app/example/page'; 141 ``` 142 143 ### 2. No `||` query fallbacks 144 145 `getBy*` throws on no match, so the `||` branch never executes. 146 147 ```typescript 148 // WRONG 149 screen.getByLabelText(/date/i) || screen.getByPlaceholderText(/date/i) 150 151 // CORRECT — use queryBy for conditional checks 152 screen.queryByLabelText(/date/i) ?? screen.getByPlaceholderText(/date/i) 153 ``` 154 155 ### 3. No speculative normalization tests 156 157 Don't test multiple casings of the same enum value unless the spec documents mixed casing. 158 159 ### 4. Every `it()` must have a meaningful assertion 160 161 Rendering a component and asserting only that a hardcoded input value appears verifies nothing. Either add an assertion that would fail if the feature broke, or don't generate the test. 162 163 ### 5. No library-internal assertions 164 165 No assertions on third-party library internals (Recharts SVG, Zod schemas, mock call counts). Assert user-observable outcomes. 166 167 ```typescript 168 // WRONG 169 expect(container.querySelector('.recharts-bar-rectangle')).toHaveAttribute('fill', '#8884d8'); 170 expect(mockFn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3); 171 expect(button).toHaveClass('btn-primary'); 172 173 // CORRECT 174 expect(screen.getByText('Sales: $1,234')).toBeInTheDocument(); 175 expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })).toBeDisabled(); 176 ``` 177 178 **Charts and visualizations specifically:** jsdom cannot render SVG/Canvas, so any test querying internal `` / `` elements is meaningless. Test that the component renders without crashing, that data transformation/formatting functions work (test those separately), that loading/error/empty states render, and use accessibility features (aria-labels, sr-only text) to verify data display. Defer visual correctness to E2E or manual QA. 179 180 ### 6. No placeholder-removal-only tests 181 182 Don't test that template placeholder text is absent. Real content rendering implicitly proves it. 183 184 ### 7. No fragile index-based row selection 185 186 Use `within()` to scope queries to a row, not array indices. 187 188 ```typescript 189 // WRONG — assumes API ordering 190 const links = screen.getAllByRole('link', { name: /view/i }); 191 const firstRowLink = links[0]; 192 193 // CORRECT — scoped to the row containing the expected text 194 const row = screen.getByText('ABC Realty').closest('tr')!; 195 const link = within(row).getByRole('link', { name: /view/i }); 196 ``` 197 198 ### 8. No loose range comparisons on count assertions 199 200 `toBeLessThanOrEqual(20)` passes even if the component renders zero rows. When the fixture has N items and you expect N visible, assert the exact count. 201 202 ```typescript 203 // WRONG — passes on an empty render 204 expect(screen.getAllByRole('row').length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(20); 205 206 // CORRECT — pins the contract to the fixture 207 expect(screen.getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(N); 208 ``` 209 210 ### 9. No unscoped numeric or short-string `getByText` 211 212 `screen.getByText('6')` matches any "6" anywhere in the DOM. For text shorter than ~4 chars, or any value that could appear in more than one place, scope it with `within()`. 213 214 ```typescript 215 // WRONG 216 expect(screen.getByText('6')).toBeInTheDocument(); 217 218 // CORRECT 219 const card = screen.getByRole('group', { name: /pending/i }); 220 expect(within(card).getByText('6')).toBeInTheDocument(); 221 ``` 222 223 ### 10. No conditional assertions that pass under either implementation 224 225 A test that asserts one thing if an element exists and the opposite if it doesn't pins no contract. Pick the expected behaviour and assert that. 226 227 ```typescript 228 // WRONG — green whether the button is disabled OR absent 229 if (button) expect(button).toBeDisabled(); 230 else expect(button).not.toBeInTheDocument(); 231 232 // CORRECT — decide the contract and assert it 233 expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })).toBeDisabled(); 234 ``` 235 236 ### 11. No empirical Playwright locator probing 237 238 When a value appears in more than one place (e.g. a reference shown in both a filter chip and the results table), `getByText` matches 2+ elements and throws Playwright's strict-mode error. Reason out a scoped locator — don't write throwaway probe specs to discover which element matches, and never write scratch specs into `web/e2e/` or `/tmp`. 239 240 ```typescript 241 // WRONG — matches the chip AND the table cell → strict-mode violation 242 await expect(page.getByText('TXN-20260415-0002')).toBeVisible(); 243 244 // CORRECT — scope to a region/role, or use exact / filter({ hasText }) 245 await expect(page.getByRole('table').getByRole('cell', { name: 'TXN-20260415-0002' })).toBeVisible(); 246 ``` 247 248 --- 249 250 ## Forbidden test files 251 252 - `constants.test.ts`, `types.test.ts`, `*-schemas.test.ts` — tests for things TypeScript already proves 253 254 --- 255 256 ## Mocking strategy 257 258 | Scenario | Mock? | How | 259 |---|---|---| 260 | API client | Yes | `vi.mock('@/lib/api/client', () => ({ get: vi.fn() }))` | 261 | External services | Yes | `vi.mock` the service module | 262 | Child components | No | Test the real component | 263 | React hooks | No | Test through behavior | 264 | Date/time | Prefer not to mock | Time-driven *flows* → Playwright `page.clock`; pure time math → plain inputs in Vitest (no timers). `vi.useFakeTimers()` only for a component-local timer with no flow — see [Time-dependent behaviour](#time-dependent-behaviour) | 265 266 **Do not "fix" data-contract tests** by using the real API client or real MSW handlers inside Vitest. The convention `vi.mock('@/lib/api/client', () => ({ get: vi.fn() }))` is fixed. 267 268 ### Playwright runs against mocks, never live 269 270 Playwright specs **never contact a live backend** and **never require real credentials** — every backend call is intercepted by `page.route()` (default) or MSW (when `web/src/mocks/` is wired), and login is faked with a mock session cookie. Keeps the gate deterministic and CI-runnable, needs no credentials (so never `test.skip()` on env vars), and can't pollute a real database. Real end-to-end checks happen at the human MANUAL-TEST approval. Anchor mock shapes to the brief's Data Model / OpenAPI spec. 271 272 ### Playwright mocking — declare it in the spec header 273 274 Playwright specs MUST open with a `Mocking strategy:` block (see [test-generator.md](../agents/test-generator.md) template). **Always mock the backend — never live.** `page.route()` (default) only intercepts browser-side fetches — it cannot intercept Server Actions, which forces a client-side implementation. MSW (Node) intercepts both but needs `web/src/mocks/` wired. The developer reads this in Step 1 and implements to it. 275 276 ### Common mock pitfalls 277 278 **Multiple API calls** — `mockResolvedValue` returns the same value for all calls. Use `mockResolvedValueOnce` for different sequential responses: 279 280 ```typescript 281 mockGet 282 .mockResolvedValueOnce(firstResponse) 283 .mockResolvedValueOnce(secondResponse); 284 ``` 285 286 **Context providers** — mock both the hook and the Provider: 287 288 ```typescript 289 vi.mock('@/contexts/ToastContext', () => ({ 290 useToast: () => ({ showToast: vi.fn() }), 291 ToastProvider: ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => children, 292 })); 293 ``` 294 295 **Navigation hooks** — mock all the Next.js navigation imports the component uses: 296 297 ```typescript 298 vi.mock('next/navigation', () => ({ 299 useRouter: () => ({ push: vi.fn(), refresh: vi.fn() }), 300 usePathname: () => '/current-path', 301 useSearchParams: () => new URLSearchParams(), 302 })); 303 ``` 304 305 **Async state updates** — wrap assertions in `waitFor`: 306 307 ```typescript 308 await waitFor(() => { 309 expect(screen.getByText('Expected')).toBeInTheDocument(); 310 }); 311 ``` 312 313 --- 314 315 ## Mock data: entity factories + scenario fixtures 316 317 Mock data has **one home per entity, shared project-wide** — not one file per epic. A per-epic file just relocates duplication to the epic boundary: three epics that all touch `Transaction` would each redefine it and drift apart — the same all-green-all-wrong failure, moved one level up. Two layers instead: 318 319 **Entity factories — `web/src/mocks/data/.ts`, one per entity, project-wide.** The single source of truth for an entity's shape **and** its canonical default values: a `create(overrides?)` factory typed against `web/src/types/api-generated.ts` when it exists (else the brief's Data Model). Every epic and every test layer that touches that entity imports the same factory. 320 321 ```typescript 322 // web/src/mocks/data/transaction.ts 323 import type { Transaction } from '@/types/api-generated'; 324 325 export const createTransaction = (overrides: Partial = {}): Transaction => ({ 326 id: 'TXN-0001', 327 amount: 125430.5, 328 status: 'pending', 329 ...overrides, 330 }); 331 ``` 332 333 **Identity / auth is project-wide.** Roles and permissions are project facts (`project.md` §Roles & Permissions), inherited across every epic — so the userinfo contract lives once in `web/src/mocks/data/identity.ts`, exporting `userInfoFor(roleName)` (the `Roles[]` / `Pages[]` shape the app gates on). One definition, exercised identically by both test layers and the manual-test approval — this is exactly the contract the v07 nav bug diverged on. 334 335 **Scenario fixtures — thin compositions, per epic/story.** A list with mixed statuses, the empty state, a rejected transaction with a note. Compose the entity factories inline in tests (`createTransaction({ status: 'approved' })`); only promote a composition to a named export (in the entity file, or a small `web/src/mocks/scenarios/epic-.ts`) when it's reused across stories or across the Vitest/Playwright boundary. Scenario fixtures carry **no** shape definitions. 336 337 **Both test layers consume the same factories.** Vitest imports via the `@/` alias (`@/mocks/data/transaction`); Playwright imports via a **relative** path from `e2e/` (`../src/mocks/data/identity`) to dodge alias resolution at Playwright runtime. So every module under `web/src/mocks/` that the e2e layer can import — entity factories in `data/` **and** scenario fixtures in `scenarios/` — must import **types** with `import type` only (erased at compile) and import **sibling/peer factories** by relative path (`./user`, or `../data/transaction` from a `scenarios/` file), never the `@/` alias — that keeps each module importable from the e2e layer without any alias plumbing. (The `@/` alias is fine in Vitest test files and in app-runtime code like `web/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, which Playwright never imports relatively — the rule is only for the modules an e2e spec reaches through a relative import.) 338 339 **The runtime mock layer consumes them too.** When the project ships MSW handlers (`web/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, the running-app mock used in mock mode), they compose the same factories — `createX(overrides)` for entity bodies, `userInfoFor(role)` for auth — so the dev/demo app and the tests can't drift onto different contracts. The handler keeps the *serving* logic (filtering, pagination, ≥2-per-enum dataset sizing); only the entity *shape + defaults* come from the factory. So all three mock surfaces — Vitest, Playwright, and the MSW runtime — draw from one source. See [mock-setup-agent § Generate handlers](../agents/mock-setup-agent.md#step-3--generate-websrcmockshandlersts). 340 341 **Evolving an entity:** when an epic genuinely adds a field, **extend** the one entity file (a deliberate, reviewable edit — journal it as a Tier-2 factual addition); never copy the entity into a new file. The per-entity files are a coordinated shared surface across epic branches: real edit-conflicts are rare (definitions are append-mostly), and when they do happen they're a genuine shared-contract change governed by [epic-branch-concurrency §6.2](./epic-branch-concurrency.md). Duplication, by contrast, guarantees silent drift. 342 343 --- 344 345 ## Mock data accuracy 346 347 Before creating mocks, check for OpenAPI specs at `generated-docs/specs/api-spec.yaml` (canonical) or `documentation/*.yaml` (user-provided). Specs don't always reflect reality (string enums, unexpected nulls, extra fields), so when sample data exists, use it as the basis. Type your factories so TypeScript catches obvious mismatches. 348 349 When a quirk is discovered (spec says enum, API returns string), document it in the type definition so both tests and implementation benefit: 350 351 ```typescript 352 export interface Portfolio { 353 /** API returns 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' as string, not a typed enum */ 354 status: string; 355 } 356 ``` 357 358 --- 359 360 ## Render scope — component vs full page 361 362 Default to the narrowest scope that covers the ACs. Full-page renders cascade failures across every suite when one component breaks; component-level renders isolate them. 363 364 | Story type | Render | 365 |---|---| 366 | Targets a specific component (chart, grid, form) | That component directly | 367 | Covers page layout / cross-component interactions | Full page | 368 | Story 1 (page setup) with many sections | Full page (first story establishes the page) | 369 370 --- 371 372 ## Testability classification (inline tags) 373 374 The `coverage` tag decides the layer (and therefore the file). These inline annotations are a **secondary** note for the residual jsdom-blindness *inside* a `vitest`-tagged test — they never override the tag or add a cross-layer sibling: 375 376 - **Runtime-only** (a `vitest`-tagged AC whose render you can assert, but whose middleware/server-component/layout-composition aspect jsdom can't exercise) — keep the Vitest test for component-level regression, add `// Runtime-only: verified during manual checklist` above it. If the *primary* behaviour is the redirect/guard itself, it should have been tagged `playwright`, not `vitest`. 377 - **Data-contract** (Vitest mocks `@/lib/api/client`, so the test verifies component behaviour with a mocked response but cannot verify real client → handler → dataset wiring) — add `// Data-contract: full chain verified during manual checklist` 378 - **Manual-only** — this is what a `none` tag with a user-eyeball nature means: do NOT generate a test, and do not report it. The manual checklist is assembled at the manual-test approval from the planner's per-story `manualTestChecklist` and the `coverage: none` tags recorded in the story file 379 380 --- 381 382 ## Mock boundary blindness 383 384 Vitest + RTL runs in jsdom, which cannot exercise certain Next.js integration layers. Tests that mock each boundary independently will pass even when the boundaries aren't connected at runtime — this is why [Testability classification](#testability-classification-inline-tags) exists. 385 386 **jsdom CAN verify (unit-testable):** 387 388 - Component rendering and conditional content 389 - Form interactions and validation feedback 390 - Hook behavior and state changes 391 - Error message display 392 393 **jsdom CANNOT verify (runtime-only):** 394 395 - Whether the page actually changed or stayed (test that in Playwright) 396 - Middleware actually intercepts requests and redirects 397 - Server-component auth (`requireSession()`) actually blocks rendering 398 - Layout composition (a page inside `(authenticated)/` inherits the protected layout) 399 - Multi-layer redirects (middleware → login → return-to-original-page) 400 - `"use client"` boundaries (server-side auth in a client component is silently skipped) 401 402 **jsdom CANNOT verify (data-contract):** 403 404 A component that calls the API client with mocked HTTP passes its Vitest tests but doesn't exercise: 405 406 - Query-param serialization (repeated vs comma-joined arrays) 407 - `buildUrl` correctness for array values 408 - MSW handler contract (does it actually read declared query params?) 409 - Mock dataset realism (≥2 items per enum so filters visibly narrow) 410 - Empty-filter semantics (no filters → all items, not zero) 411 412 A list with a broken status filter passes every component test because the test never touches the actual URL. The bug only appears when the real API client meets the real MSW handler in the browser. 413 414 **How the workflow handles it:** the `developer` performs integration-wiring checks and synthesizes runtime verification items from the story's ACs — so the manual checklist always surfaces runtime-only and data-contract concerns — and the epic-end `/code-review` pass is a further backstop. `mock-setup-agent` generates handlers that honor their OpenAPI contract (query params read and applied; ≥2 items per enum value) to prevent the most common data-contract bugs from shipping as mocks. 415 416 The most dangerous case is when a behaviour depends on a backend response shape the brief *assumed* rather than *verified*: the mocks are built from that same assumption, so the code, the mocks, and every test agree — all green, all wrong (e.g. deriving nav from a `Pages[]` array the real backend returns sparsely). These are captured at PLAN as the epic's [`unverifiedAssumptions`](../agents/feature-planner.md#unverified-assumptions-the-manual-test-approval-ledger) and floated to the **top** of the manual-test approval as a "check these first" list — the human is the only place reality enters the loop, so point their attention at exactly what the pipeline couldn't prove. 417 418 --- 419 420 ## Non-routable Playwright stubs 421 422 Stories with `route === null` still get a Playwright spec file (so the file structure exists for later promotion), but each test is a `test.fixme()` stub — using the **version-agnostic** form below: a real `test(...)` whose body calls `test.fixme()` to skip at runtime. Prefer this form; it behaves consistently across Playwright versions. Avoid the declarative `test.fixme('title', fn)` overload, which has produced version-dependent parse errors. 423 424 ```ts 425 import { test } from '@playwright/test'; 426 427 // Non-routable: 428 test('Epic N, Story M: (deferred to consumer stories)', () => { 429 test.fixme(); // skips at runtime; behaves consistently across Playwright 430 // versions, unlike the declarative test.fixme('title', fn) form 431 }); 432 ``` 433 434 `test.fixme()` is **only** permitted for explicitly non-routable stories (`route === null`). Never as a tool to avoid failing tests. 435 436 **Time-driven ≠ non-routable.** Do not downgrade a routable story (`route !== null`) to a stub because its behaviour is timer-driven or because the component is mounted app-wide with "no surface to navigate to." `page.clock` advances the clock deterministically with no production hooks, and an app-wide manager's effects are observable on any real page — so session-timeout / polling / auto-dismiss stories get a **live** `page.clock` spec (see [Time-dependent behaviour](#time-dependent-behaviour)). `test.fixme()` is for stories with no observable browser surface at all, not for ones that are merely awkward to time. 437

1	# Server-Side Authentication Pattern
2	
3	## Core Principle
4	
5	When `project.md` §Authentication records `Method: server-side`, the developer agent implements the **Next.js client-side integration** with a separate auth service — a backend process that holds the session cookie, talks to whatever identity provider the project uses, and exposes a small set of auth endpoints back to the frontend. The frontend never sees a token in JavaScript; the browser holds a single HttpOnly session cookie, and protected routes are gated server-side.
6	
7	This policy is **applied inline during BUILD** by the `developer` agent (when implementing auth stories) and **verified at epic-end** by the `/code-review` pass over the epic diff (continue.md Step B7.0.5), which surfaces a client-reachable token or auth origin as a correctness/security finding.
8	
9	This is the **encouraged path** because it is the most secure of the three auth options ([authentication-intake.md](./authentication-intake.md)). Tokens stay in HttpOnly cookies server-side; JavaScript can't read them, so XSS can't exfiltrate them. The client bundle ships no auth library. CSRF is handled by `SameSite=Strict` cookies. Auth/authz can be enforced uniformly across all API consumers by the backend.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## What "Server-Side Authentication" Means in This Repo
14	
15	The starter template generates **only the Next.js client side** of the integration. The auth service itself (Node, .NET, Go, Linx, etc.) is a separate process at `AUTH_BASE_URL`, owned by the project's backend team. This policy describes:
16	
17	1. **The endpoint contract** the auth service must satisfy — so the frontend integration code can be written against a stable shape
18	2. **The security best-practices** that must hold inside the auth service — regardless of which runtime implements it
19	3. **The Next.js integration pattern** the developer agent writes when an auth story comes up
20	
21	When the auth service is implemented in-house, the security rules below are the developer agent's responsibility to surface and enforce. When it is implemented by another team, the policy doubles as the integration spec the frontend will hold them to.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Endpoint Contract
26	
27	All endpoints live under `/auth/`. JSON bodies. Error envelope:
28	
29	```json
30	{ "error": "STRING_CODE", "message": "human-readable" }
31	```
32	
33	Error codes: `INVALID_REQUEST`, `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `SESSION_INVALID`, `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`.
34	
35	| Method | Path | Auth | Body | Response |
36	|---|---|---|---|---|
37	| POST | `/auth/login` | none | `{ username, password }` | 200 `{ message }` + session cookie; 400 / 401 / 500 |
38	| POST | `/auth/logout` | cookie | none | 200 `{ message }` + cookie clear |
39	| GET | `/auth/userinfo` | cookie | none | 200 `{ username, displayName }`; 401 |
40	| GET | `/auth/health` | none | none | 200 |
41	
42	**No refresh endpoint.** Sessions extend on access (sliding window) and are capped by an absolute lifetime.
43	
44	The `/userinfo` response **must include both `username` and `displayName`** — a single field that conflates them is a bug seen in early reference implementations. The frontend may show `displayName` in UI and use `username` for identity.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Cookie Defaults
49	
50	```
51	Name:     session
52	Value:    opaque base64url (32 random bytes; stored hashed server-side)
53	HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; Secure
54	Max-Age:  idle TTL (default 30 min)
55	```
56	
57	- `Secure` is **on by default**. In local development on plain HTTP, opt out via an explicit `AUTH_INSECURE_COOKIE=1` env var. Never hardcode `Secure=false` in the cookie template — that silently breaks production HTTPS deployments if the value sticks.
58	- `Path=/` is required. A missing `Path` defaults to the request path and can cause subtle "logged in on /app but not on /api" bugs.
59	- The cookie name `session` is the contract value the Next.js integration expects. If the auth service picks a different name, it must be configurable on the Next.js side.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## Session Storage (server-side, inside the auth service)
64	
65	Reference table shape:
66	
67	```sql
68	session (
69	  id_hash         varchar(64) primary key,  -- SHA-256 of raw token
70	  user_id         int not null,
71	  created_at      timestamp not null,
72	  last_access_at  timestamp not null,
73	  expires_at      timestamp not null,       -- absolute cap
74	  ip_address      varchar(45),
75	  user_agent      varchar(512)
76	)
77	```
78	
79	- **Tokens generated as 32 random bytes** (256 bits — well above the OWASP minimum of 128). 96-bit / 16-character tokens are too small.
80	- **Only the SHA-256 hash is stored.** A database compromise must not yield session takeover. Compare hash on lookup.
81	- **Idle expiry** via `last_access_at + idle_ttl`. Refresh `last_access_at` on each successful request.
82	- **Absolute expiry** via `expires_at` — capped regardless of activity. Default 12h. Prevents indefinite session extension through continued use.
83	- **Logout filters by `id_hash`, NOT by `user_id`.** Logging out one device must not kill the user's concurrent sessions on other devices.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Mandatory Security Rules
88	
89	These hold inside the auth service runtime. The developer agent surfaces them in code review / integration discussions when the auth service is built by another team.
90	
91	1. **Password hashing:** bcrypt (cost ≥12) or argon2id, with a per-user salt. **Never SHA-512.** Never unsalted. The salt is per-user and stored alongside the hash.
92	
93	2. **Constant-time hash compare** for both passwords and session tokens. `==` on a hash value leaks timing information. Use the runtime's `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (Node), `subtle.constantTimeCompare` (Web Crypto), or equivalent.
94	
95	3. **Login rate limit:** token-bucket per IP + per username. Lockout after N failures in M minutes (sensible defaults: 5 failures / 15 min). Both axes — per-IP alone misses credential-stuffing from a botnet; per-username alone is bypassable by IP rotation.
96	
97	4. **Server-error suppression:** stack traces and internal error messages **never** reach the client. The response is `{ error: "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR", message: "An error occurred" }`. Detailed errors go to the server log only.
98	
99	5. **Audit log:** structured JSON lines for `auth.login.success`, `auth.login.failure`, `auth.logout`, `auth.session.invalid`. Include: timestamp, username (for failure cases too — for monitoring), IP, user-agent, session id hash (for success). Never include the raw token or password.
100	
101	6. **HSTS header on all responses** in production. `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`. Combined with an HTTP → HTTPS redirect at the edge.
102	
103	7. **CSRF protection:** `SameSite=Strict` on the session cookie is acceptable when the auth service and frontend share the same registrable domain. If the deployment topology requires cross-site cookies (the auth service on a different eTLD+1 from the frontend), layer token-based CSRF on top — generate a CSRF token bound to the session, surface it to the frontend, require it on state-changing requests.
104	
105	8. **Logout response handling on the frontend:** the client-side `handleLogout` **must branch on `res.ok`** before redirecting. A failed logout that redirects unconditionally looks identical to a successful one and leaves the cookie alive on the auth service.
106	
107	9. **Cookie clear on logout** uses the **same attributes** as the original set (Name, Path, Domain, Secure, SameSite) plus `Max-Age=0`. A mismatch silently fails to clear the cookie. A common bug is clearing `key=` when the cookie was actually `session=`.
108	
109	10. **Secrets never in source control.** Database passwords, JWT signing keys (if used internally by the auth service), OAuth client secrets — all live in environment variables. Reference samples that ship with literal secrets in committed config files are wrong; rotate any leaked secret and externalise it.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## Next.js Integration Pattern
114	
115	Two shapes, by backend topology — and the choice matters (the wrong one ships a working-but-weaker app: cross-origin CORS and client-only gating). **Either way the browser only ever calls same-origin paths, and the `(authenticated)` layout is gated server-side.**
116	
117	- **A single auth service you control** (reachable at `AUTH_BASE_URL`) → the route-handler flow below: `authClient.ts` fetches server-side and `requireSession()` gates the layout.
118	- **An existing backend, or more than one** (a backend team owns the API) → same-origin **rewrites** (next subsection), keeping the same invariant.
119	
120	When implementing a server-side auth story, the developer agent produces approximately the structure below. Names and paths are the canonical shape; deviate only when the brief calls for it.
121	
122	### Existing or multiple backends — same-origin rewrites
123	
124	Map same-origin paths to the real origins in `next.config` so the browser never calls a backend cross-origin (no CORS, origins stay server-side):
125	
126	```typescript
127	// web/next.config.ts — the browser only ever calls same-origin /v1/* paths.
128	const AUTH_API = process.env.AUTH_API_BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:10010';
129	const TX_API = process.env.TRANSACTIONS_API_BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:10005';
130	
131	export default {
132	  async rewrites() {
133	    return [
134	      { source: '/v1/auth/:path*', destination: `${AUTH_API}/v1/auth/:path*` },
135	      { source: '/transactions-api/:path*', destination: `${TX_API}/:path*` },
136	    ];
137	  },
138	};
139	```
140	
141	Gate the `(authenticated)` layout server-side either way — the `requireSession()` shape below, or a lighter `next/headers` cookie-presence redirect when you don't want a per-navigation `/userinfo` round-trip (client revalidation covers liveness).
142	
143	**Anti-pattern:** backend base URLs as `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` fetched cross-origin from the browser, gated only by a client `<AuthProvider>` that redirects after render — it forces a CORS preflight on every call (which silently fails when the origin isn't allowed), ships gating to the client, and leaks origins into the bundle. Use a rewrite instead.
144	
145	### Environment variables (`web/.env.example` + `web/.env.local`)
146	
147	```
148	AUTH_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5120
149	AUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000
150	AUTH_SESSION_TTL_MINUTES=30
151	AUTH_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_TTL_HOURS=12
152	# AUTH_INSECURE_COOKIE=1   # local dev only; opt-out from Secure cookie
153	```
154	
155	`AUTH_BASE_URL` is server-side only — **not** prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`. The browser never talks directly to the auth service in the canonical pattern; it talks to Next.js route handlers that proxy through.
156	
157	### `web/src/lib/auth/authClient.ts`
158	
159	```typescript
160	export async function authFetch(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}) {
161	  return fetch(`${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL}${path}`, {
162	    ...init,
163	    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...init.headers },
164	  });
165	}
166	```
167	
168	Server-side fetch wrapper. Cookie forwarding is the **caller's** responsibility — pass an explicit `Cookie:` header from the incoming request (as `requireSession()` does below). `credentials: 'include'` is a browser-fetch concept and has no effect server-side; don't add it.
169	
170	### `web/src/lib/auth/requireSession.ts`
171	
172	```typescript
173	import { cookies } from 'next/headers';
174	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
175	import { authFetch } from './authClient';
176	
177	export async function requireSession() {
178	  const cookieStore = await cookies();
179	  const session = cookieStore.get('session');
180	  if (!session) redirect('/login');
181	
182	  const res = await authFetch('/auth/userinfo', {
183	    headers: { Cookie: `session=${session.value}` },
184	  });
185	  if (!res.ok) redirect('/login');
186	
187	  return res.json() as Promise<{ username: string; displayName: string }>;
188	}
189	```
190	
191	Server-component helper. Used by protected route group layouts to gate access.
192	
193	### Protected route group: `web/src/app/(authenticated)/layout.tsx`
194	
195	```typescript
196	import { requireSession } from '@/lib/auth/requireSession';
197	
198	export default async function AuthenticatedLayout({
199	  children,
200	}: {
201	  children: React.ReactNode;
202	}) {
203	  await requireSession();
204	  return <>{children}</>;
205	}
206	```
207	
208	The route group's layout calls `requireSession()` and `redirect()`s on 401. Every page that lives under `(authenticated)/` is gated by this layout. There is **no client-side auth state**, no `<SessionProvider>`, no `useSession()` hook.
209	
210	### Login form (server action)
211	
212	```typescript
213	// web/src/app/login/page.tsx (Server Component with Server Action)
214	import { cookies } from 'next/headers';
215	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
216	import { authFetch } from '@/lib/auth/authClient';
217	
218	export default function LoginPage() {
219	  async function login(formData: FormData) {
220	    'use server';
221	    const res = await authFetch('/auth/login', {
222	      method: 'POST',
223	      body: JSON.stringify({
224	        username: formData.get('username'),
225	        password: formData.get('password'),
226	      }),
227	    });
228	    if (!res.ok) {
229	      redirect('/login?error=invalid');
230	    }
231	
232	    // Server actions don't auto-pipe Set-Cookie back to the browser.
233	    // Use getSetCookie() (returns array — get() would mangle multi-cookie
234	    // responses) and forward Max-Age so the auth service's sliding-window
235	    // TTL holds.
236	    const COOKIE_NAME = 'session';
237	    const header = res.headers.getSetCookie().find((c) => c.startsWith(`${COOKIE_NAME}=`));
238	    if (!header) {
239	      redirect('/login?error=invalid');
240	    }
241	    const value = header.split(';', 1)[0].slice(COOKIE_NAME.length + 1);
242	    const maxAge = header.match(/Max-Age=(\d+)/i)?.[1];
243	    const cookieStore = await cookies();
244	    cookieStore.set(COOKIE_NAME, value, {
245	      httpOnly: true,
246	      secure: process.env.AUTH_INSECURE_COOKIE !== '1',
247	      sameSite: 'strict',
248	      path: '/',
249	      maxAge: maxAge ? parseInt(maxAge, 10) : undefined,
250	    });
251	
252	    redirect('/');
253	  }
254	  return (
255	    <form action={login}>
256	      <input name="username" type="text" required />
257	      <input name="password" type="password" required />
258	      <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
259	    </form>
260	  );
261	}
262	```
263	
264	The cookie-forwarding block is non-optional — `Set-Cookie` from a backend response isn't auto-piped to the browser by server actions. Change `COOKIE_NAME` if the auth service uses something other than `session`.
265	
266	### Logout (route handler or server action)
267	
268	```typescript
269	// web/src/app/logout/route.ts
270	import { cookies } from 'next/headers';
271	import { authFetch } from '@/lib/auth/authClient';
272	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
273	
274	export async function POST() {
275	  const cookieStore = await cookies();
276	  const session = cookieStore.get('session');
277	  if (session) {
278	    const res = await authFetch('/auth/logout', {
279	      method: 'POST',
280	      headers: { Cookie: `session=${session.value}` },
281	    });
282	    if (!res.ok) {
283	      // Branch on res.ok per Rule 8 — don't redirect silently on failure
284	      return new Response(null, { status: 500 });
285	    }
286	  }
287	  // Clear with matching attributes per Rule 9 — cookies().delete() does NOT
288	  // preserve SameSite / Secure / Path, which silently fails to clear the cookie
289	  // when those attributes were set on the original.
290	  cookieStore.set('session', '', {
291	    httpOnly: true,
292	    secure: process.env.AUTH_INSECURE_COOKIE !== '1',
293	    sameSite: 'strict',
294	    path: '/',
295	    maxAge: 0,
296	  });
297	  redirect('/login');
298	}
299	```
300	
301	Branches on `res.ok` (Rule 8) — a 500 surfaces the failure rather than hiding it behind a redirect. Clears the cookie with explicit attributes matching the original `set` (Rule 9) — `cookies().delete('session')` would silently fail to clear a cookie that was set with `SameSite=Strict; Secure`.
302	
303	---
304	
305	## What This Policy Does Not Cover
306	
307	- **SSO / OIDC integration.** A separate pattern (`server-side-auth-sso`) lands after the without-SSO version is solid. Until then: when the brief calls for SSO, the developer agent surfaces the gap rather than improvising.
308	- **Token-based CSRF.** Default scaffold relies on `SameSite=Strict`. Projects needing token-based CSRF layer it on top per Rule 7.
309	- **Frontend-only (next-auth) and Custom auth paths.** Those follow next-auth's documentation or the brief's bespoke description, respectively. This file is specific to server-side authentication.
310	- **User management / provisioning UI.** Sign-up, invite, password reset, account disable — separate concerns, scaffolded by stories per the brief.
311	
312	---
313	
314	## Rationale
315	
316	The 10 mandatory rules above each correspond to a real bug seen in the wild — most of them in a single reference auth-service sample reviewed before this policy was written. Concrete examples behind each rule:
317	
318	| Rule | Real failure it prevents |
319	|---|---|
320	| 1 | Unsalted SHA-512 password hashes that look secure but are GPU-cracked in hours |
321	| 2 | `==` compare on session id leaking timing information to a network attacker |
322	| 3 | Credential-stuffing succeeding because no rate limit existed |
323	| 4 | Stack traces returned in 500 responses exposing internal paths and library versions |
324	| 5 | No audit trail to investigate "did this account actually log in last Tuesday?" |
325	| 6 | Production accidentally served over plain HTTP for hours, sessions cleartext on the wire |
326	| 7 | Cross-origin POST silently authenticating because no SameSite / CSRF guard |
327	| 8 | `handleLogout` redirecting on `fetch()` reject, leaving the auth-service session alive |
328	| 9 | `Set-Cookie: key=; Max-Age=0` failing to clear `session=...` because of name mismatch |
329	| 10 | Database password committed to git, found by a public-repo scan service |
330	
331	Codifying the rules in this policy means the developer agent applies them by default and the epic-end `/code-review` pass checks for them — without re-deriving the threat model on every project.

1 # Testing Policy 2 3 Canonical operational checklist for testing, referenced by [`test-generator`](../agents/test-generator.md) and [`developer`](../agents/developer.md), and enforced by the `test-quality` gate in `quality-gates.js`. CLAUDE.md covers rationale. 4 5 --- 6 7 ## Where each scenario belongs 8 9 Every acceptance criterion carries **exactly one** coverage tag, assigned by the [feature-planner](../agents/feature-planner.md#coverage-tagging) at PLAN and rendered mechanically by `test-generator` (one tag → one test). Tag by **where the behaviour lives**, not by how thorough it would feel: 10 11 | The behaviour lives in… | Tag | Examples | 12 |---|---|---| 13 | the **React render** (jsdom-observable) | `vitest` (`web/src/__tests__/`) | role-gating, conditional UI, form-state, loading/empty/error states, hook behaviour, schema-driven form validation | 14 | the **browser + mocked-backend round-trip** | `playwright` (`web/e2e/`) | navigation/redirects, submit-and-see-next-page, the app's real `authorize()` against a mocked backend, role-aware visibility, route guards (middleware), localStorage across a real reload, filter/sort/pagination against mocked responses, drag/drop, downloads, file picker, **accessibility** (one real-browser `@axe-core/playwright` scan), **time-dependent flows** (`page.clock`) | 15 | **visual / assistive-tech / OS**, or **absorbed by a sibling AC's test** | `none` | screen-reader announcements, OS-level theme, human-eye contrast, cross-browser parity; or "another AC's test in this story already proves this" | 16 17 **One tag, one layer — no sibling tests across layers.** A sign-in redirect belongs in Playwright; the Vitest version would mock `signIn()` and recreate the exact blind spot the pipeline exists to close. The Playwright spec *is* the test. Vitest stays a respected, narrow tier — written exactly where it has value, never as a default or a "for completeness" duplicate. 18 19 **`none` is first-class.** Static chrome ("page has the heading 'File Logs'") and visual/AT/OS checks are tagged `none`; a `none` AC the user can still eyeball belongs in `manualTestChecklist`. 20 21 --- 22 23 ## Time-dependent behaviour 24 25 Timeouts, polling, debounce, auto-dismiss, countdowns — anything driven by the clock. 26 27 **Time-driven *flows* belong in Playwright, via [`page.clock`](https://playwright.dev/docs/clock) — not Vitest fake timers.** `page.clock.install()` then `fastForward('15:00')` / `runFor(1000)` / `pauseAt(...)` advances the browser clock deterministically against the **real** configured durations — no injected short values, no real elapsed time, and (the part that matters) **no test-only hooks in production code**. It also sidesteps the jsdom failure modes that make `vi.useFakeTimers()` fragile: it deadlocks RTL's `waitFor`/`findBy*` and hangs `axe()`. 28 29 Split the layers: 30 31 - **Flow** — warning modal appears before expiry, countdown ticks down, redirect fires on expiry, a control disables during a cooldown → `playwright` + `page.clock`. 32 - **Pure time arithmetic** — the idle-vs-absolute decision, "seconds remaining" math → extract it into a plain function/hook and unit-test with **explicit inputs in Vitest, no timers at all**. Prefer a timestamp-derived value (`Math.ceil((expiresAt - now) / 1000)`) over a `setInterval` that mutates its own state — it's deterministic and needs no clock to test. 33 - `vi.useFakeTimers()` is the **last resort** — only a genuinely component-local timer with no observable flow. If you reach for it, never run `axe()` in the same test (axe defers on `setTimeout` and will hang under a frozen fake clock) — accessibility is asserted by the Playwright `@axe-core/playwright` scan anyway. 34 35 **"Mounted app-wide / no page of its own" is not non-routable.** A session-timeout manager lives in the shell, but its effects are observable on any signed-in page — drive a browser to one and use `page.clock`. See [Non-routable Playwright stubs](#non-routable-playwright-stubs). 36 37 Two consequences worth banking: 38 39 - **Don't add test-only timing config to production.** Shortened-duration props/env switches exist only to make fake-timer tests bearable; `page.clock` exercises the real 15-min / 8-hr values instantly, so production keeps its real defaults and gains no test scaffolding. 40 - **Don't duplicate the durations as a manual step.** Because `page.clock` verifies the real configured values automatically, a `manualTestChecklist` item like "confirm the timeout fires at 15 minutes" is redundant — drop it. 41 42 --- 43 44 ## Accessibility 45 46 Asserted by a real-browser `@axe-core/playwright` scan in the routable story's Playwright spec — **not** `vitest-axe` in jsdom (which can't see contrast, layout, or focus order). 47 48 - **Scope to the standard.** Use the axe tags for every WCAG version and level up to `NFR-base-1`'s — 2.1 AA (the default) is `.withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])`; 2.2 AA adds `'wcag22aa'`. Axe's defaults also run *best-practice* rules; leaving them on fails specs on issues outside the agreed bar. 49 - **Scan each distinct state the story introduces** — happy path plus error / empty / open-modal / disabled — not just the default render. axe violations are usually state-specific, and a page-level scan only sees the states the spec drives to. 50 - **Scan a settled DOM** — await a stable element before scanning so the scan isn't racing a loading skeleton or an animation. 51 - A component with no routable surface of its own is covered when a routable page renders it; it is not separately axe-scanned in Vitest. The automated in-loop signal is the routable page's `@axe-core/playwright` scan (run batched at epic-end); the epic-end `/code-review` pass is a further backstop for semantic-HTML / ARIA / keyboard concerns. 52 53 --- 54 55 ## Test organization 56 57 | Directory | Contents | 58 |---|---| 59 | `web/src/__tests__/integration/` | Integration tests (primary focus) | 60 | `web/src/__tests__/scripts/` | Template tooling and script tests | 61 | `web/src/__tests__/api/` | API endpoint tests (if needed) | 62 | `web/e2e/` | Playwright specs | 63 64 File naming: `.test.ts` for non-React code, `.test.tsx` for React components/pages. Use descriptive names tied to the behavior under test. 65 66 --- 67 68 ## Per-epic baseline 69 70 Cross-story invariants live in **one file per epic**, not duplicated across every story's test file: 71 72 - File: `web/src/__tests__/integration/epic--baseline.test.tsx`. 73 - Created by **Story 1's** `test-generator` when the planner set `epicIntroducesSharedSurface: true` (the epic introduces a shared shell, `layout.tsx`, route group, or provider). 74 - Covers epic-wide invariants: role-gating that spans the epic's pages, shared-shell navigation, shared layout. (The epic's accessibility baseline is a `@axe-core/playwright` scan in the shared-surface story's Playwright spec — not this Vitest file.) 75 - **Later stories in the epic do NOT re-assert these** — their test files cover only the story's delta. If a later story introduces a *genuinely new* shared surface, extend the baseline (add only the new invariants) rather than recreating it. 76 77 --- 78 79 ## Test budget 80 81 **Tests = coverage tags.** The feature-planner assigns one `coverage` tag per (consolidated, ≤6) AC; `test-generator` renders one test per tag. There is no separate count target — the count is whatever the tags produce. 82 83 **Hard ceiling: 12 `it()` blocks per Vitest file and 12 `test()` blocks per Playwright spec.** A story file won't reach it — ≤6 ACs per story, one test per tag — so in practice the ceiling binds on the **per-epic baseline**, which grows as later stories extend it. A baseline at the ceiling means the epic carries more shared-surface invariants than one file should hold: `test-generator` emits at the ceiling and flags it for consolidation on its one-line `NOTE:` rather than letting the file grow. 84 85 ### Representative vs exhaustive 86 87 Consolidation happens at PLAN (one AC = "validates fields per the brief", not one AC per field), so one tag yields one representative test, not one per data point. 88 89 | Behavior | Representative (correct) | Exhaustive (wrong) | 90 |---|---|---| 91 | Pagination | Forward, backward, first-page disables prev, last-page disables next (4) | Pages 1–10 individually (10) | 92 | Sorting | Click → asc, click again → desc, verify one column (2-3) | Every column × both directions (12+) | 93 | Filtering | Apply filter → narrows, clear → restores, combine two (3) | Every filter value × every combination (20+) | 94 | Validation | One required empty, one invalid format, all valid (3) | Every field × every rule (15+) | 95 | Empty / error / loading | One each (3) | Multiple error codes × multiple empty scenarios (10+) | 96 97 When multiple tests differ only by a data value (column name, page number, filter option), that's a signal to test the mechanism once and trust the implementation. Use `it.each` sparingly — only for genuinely distinct edge cases (number vs date vs string formatting), never data variations. Keep `it.each` tables ≤5 rows. 98 99 --- 100 101 ## Query priority (accessibility-first) 102 103 | Priority | Query | When to use | 104 |---|---|---| 105 | 1 | `getByRole` | Buttons, links, headings, forms — **preferred for most elements** | 106 | 2 | `getByLabelText` | Form inputs with labels | 107 | 3 | `getByPlaceholderText` | Inputs without visible labels | 108 | 4 | `getByText` | Non-interactive content | 109 | 5 | `getByDisplayValue` | Filled form inputs | 110 | Last resort | `getByTestId` | Only when no semantic query works | 111 112 **`getByTestId` is an anti-pattern in most cases.** If you find yourself adding `data-testid` attributes, first ask: "Is there a semantic HTML element or ARIA role I should use instead?" The answer is usually yes. 113 114 --- 115 116 ## AC traceability 117 118 Every `it()` / `test()` block carries a `// AC-N` comment on the line above it. Multiple ACs can be comma-separated: 119 120 ```typescript 121 // AC-1, AC-3 122 it('displays payment list and handles API errors', () => { ... }); 123 ``` 124 125 --- 126 127 ## Anti-patterns (forbidden) 128 129 Tests must fail before implementation, import real production code (never mock the code under test), assert user-observable behavior, and follow the **No Error Suppressions** rule in CLAUDE.md. The patterns below are the recurring ways those principles get violated: 130 131 ### 1. No placeholder components inside test files 132 133 Every `import` must point to production code. If the component doesn't exist, that's the expected TDD failure — don't define a placeholder. 134 135 ```typescript 136 // WRONG — tests zero production code 137 const ExamplePage = () =>
Example
; 138 139 // CORRECT — import will fail until implemented 140 import { ExamplePage } from '@/app/example/page'; 141 ``` 142 143 ### 2. No `||` query fallbacks 144 145 `getBy*` throws on no match, so the `||` branch never executes. 146 147 ```typescript 148 // WRONG 149 screen.getByLabelText(/date/i) || screen.getByPlaceholderText(/date/i) 150 151 // CORRECT — use queryBy for conditional checks 152 screen.queryByLabelText(/date/i) ?? screen.getByPlaceholderText(/date/i) 153 ``` 154 155 ### 3. No speculative normalization tests 156 157 Don't test multiple casings of the same enum value unless the spec documents mixed casing. 158 159 ### 4. Every `it()` must have a meaningful assertion 160 161 Rendering a component and asserting only that a hardcoded input value appears verifies nothing. Either add an assertion that would fail if the feature broke, or don't generate the test. 162 163 ### 5. No library-internal assertions 164 165 No assertions on third-party library internals (Recharts SVG, Zod schemas, mock call counts). Assert user-observable outcomes. 166 167 ```typescript 168 // WRONG 169 expect(container.querySelector('.recharts-bar-rectangle')).toHaveAttribute('fill', '#8884d8'); 170 expect(mockFn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3); 171 expect(button).toHaveClass('btn-primary'); 172 173 // CORRECT 174 expect(screen.getByText('Sales: $1,234')).toBeInTheDocument(); 175 expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })).toBeDisabled(); 176 ``` 177 178 **Charts and visualizations specifically:** jsdom cannot render SVG/Canvas, so any test querying internal `` / `` elements is meaningless. Test that the component renders without crashing, that data transformation/formatting functions work (test those separately), that loading/error/empty states render, and use accessibility features (aria-labels, sr-only text) to verify data display. Defer visual correctness to E2E or manual QA. 179 180 ### 6. No placeholder-removal-only tests 181 182 Don't test that template placeholder text is absent. Real content rendering implicitly proves it. 183 184 ### 7. No fragile index-based row selection 185 186 Use `within()` to scope queries to a row, not array indices. 187 188 ```typescript 189 // WRONG — assumes API ordering 190 const links = screen.getAllByRole('link', { name: /view/i }); 191 const firstRowLink = links[0]; 192 193 // CORRECT — scoped to the row containing the expected text 194 const row = screen.getByText('ABC Realty').closest('tr')!; 195 const link = within(row).getByRole('link', { name: /view/i }); 196 ``` 197 198 ### 8. No loose range comparisons on count assertions 199 200 `toBeLessThanOrEqual(20)` passes even if the component renders zero rows. When the fixture has N items and you expect N visible, assert the exact count. 201 202 ```typescript 203 // WRONG — passes on an empty render 204 expect(screen.getAllByRole('row').length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(20); 205 206 // CORRECT — pins the contract to the fixture 207 expect(screen.getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(N); 208 ``` 209 210 ### 9. No unscoped numeric or short-string `getByText` 211 212 `screen.getByText('6')` matches any "6" anywhere in the DOM. For text shorter than ~4 chars, or any value that could appear in more than one place, scope it with `within()`. 213 214 ```typescript 215 // WRONG 216 expect(screen.getByText('6')).toBeInTheDocument(); 217 218 // CORRECT 219 const card = screen.getByRole('group', { name: /pending/i }); 220 expect(within(card).getByText('6')).toBeInTheDocument(); 221 ``` 222 223 ### 10. No conditional assertions that pass under either implementation 224 225 A test that asserts one thing if an element exists and the opposite if it doesn't pins no contract. Pick the expected behaviour and assert that. 226 227 ```typescript 228 // WRONG — green whether the button is disabled OR absent 229 if (button) expect(button).toBeDisabled(); 230 else expect(button).not.toBeInTheDocument(); 231 232 // CORRECT — decide the contract and assert it 233 expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })).toBeDisabled(); 234 ``` 235 236 ### 11. No empirical Playwright locator probing 237 238 When a value appears in more than one place (e.g. a reference shown in both a filter chip and the results table), `getByText` matches 2+ elements and throws Playwright's strict-mode error. Reason out a scoped locator — don't write throwaway probe specs to discover which element matches, and never write scratch specs into `web/e2e/` or `/tmp`. 239 240 ```typescript 241 // WRONG — matches the chip AND the table cell → strict-mode violation 242 await expect(page.getByText('TXN-20260415-0002')).toBeVisible(); 243 244 // CORRECT — scope to a region/role, or use exact / filter({ hasText }) 245 await expect(page.getByRole('table').getByRole('cell', { name: 'TXN-20260415-0002' })).toBeVisible(); 246 ``` 247 248 --- 249 250 ## Forbidden test files 251 252 - `constants.test.ts`, `types.test.ts`, `*-schemas.test.ts` — tests for things TypeScript already proves 253 254 --- 255 256 ## Mocking strategy 257 258 | Scenario | Mock? | How | 259 |---|---|---| 260 | API client | Yes | `vi.mock('@/lib/api/client', () => ({ get: vi.fn() }))` | 261 | External services | Yes | `vi.mock` the service module | 262 | Child components | No | Test the real component | 263 | React hooks | No | Test through behavior | 264 | Date/time | Prefer not to mock | Time-driven *flows* → Playwright `page.clock`; pure time math → plain inputs in Vitest (no timers). `vi.useFakeTimers()` only for a component-local timer with no flow — see [Time-dependent behaviour](#time-dependent-behaviour) | 265 266 **Do not "fix" data-contract tests** by using the real API client or real MSW handlers inside Vitest. The convention `vi.mock('@/lib/api/client', () => ({ get: vi.fn() }))` is fixed. 267 268 ### Playwright runs against mocks, never live 269 270 Playwright specs **never contact a live backend** and **never require real credentials** — every backend call is intercepted by `page.route()` (default) or MSW (when `web/src/mocks/` is wired), and login is faked with a mock session cookie. Keeps the gate deterministic and CI-runnable, needs no credentials (so never `test.skip()` on env vars), and can't pollute a real database. Real end-to-end checks happen at the human MANUAL-TEST approval. Anchor mock shapes to the brief's Data Model / OpenAPI spec. 271 272 ### Playwright mocking — declare it in the spec header 273 274 Playwright specs MUST open with a `Mocking strategy:` block (see [test-generator.md](../agents/test-generator.md) template). **Always mock the backend — never live.** `page.route()` (default) only intercepts browser-side fetches — it cannot intercept Server Actions, which forces a client-side implementation. MSW (Node) intercepts both but needs `web/src/mocks/` wired. The developer reads this in Step 1 and implements to it. 275 276 ### Common mock pitfalls 277 278 **Multiple API calls** — `mockResolvedValue` returns the same value for all calls. Use `mockResolvedValueOnce` for different sequential responses: 279 280 ```typescript 281 mockGet 282 .mockResolvedValueOnce(firstResponse) 283 .mockResolvedValueOnce(secondResponse); 284 ``` 285 286 **Context providers** — mock both the hook and the Provider: 287 288 ```typescript 289 vi.mock('@/contexts/ToastContext', () => ({ 290 useToast: () => ({ showToast: vi.fn() }), 291 ToastProvider: ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => children, 292 })); 293 ``` 294 295 **Navigation hooks** — mock all the Next.js navigation imports the component uses: 296 297 ```typescript 298 vi.mock('next/navigation', () => ({ 299 useRouter: () => ({ push: vi.fn(), refresh: vi.fn() }), 300 usePathname: () => '/current-path', 301 useSearchParams: () => new URLSearchParams(), 302 })); 303 ``` 304 305 **Async state updates** — wrap assertions in `waitFor`: 306 307 ```typescript 308 await waitFor(() => { 309 expect(screen.getByText('Expected')).toBeInTheDocument(); 310 }); 311 ``` 312 313 --- 314 315 ## Mock data: entity factories + scenario fixtures 316 317 Mock data has **one home per entity, shared project-wide** — not one file per epic. A per-epic file just relocates duplication to the epic boundary: three epics that all touch `Transaction` would each redefine it and drift apart — the same all-green-all-wrong failure, moved one level up. Two layers instead: 318 319 **Entity factories — `web/src/mocks/data/.ts`, one per entity, project-wide.** The single source of truth for an entity's shape **and** its canonical default values: a `create(overrides?)` factory typed against `web/src/types/api-generated.ts` when it exists (else the brief's Data Model). Every epic and every test layer that touches that entity imports the same factory. 320 321 ```typescript 322 // web/src/mocks/data/transaction.ts 323 import type { Transaction } from '@/types/api-generated'; 324 325 export const createTransaction = (overrides: Partial = {}): Transaction => ({ 326 id: 'TXN-0001', 327 amount: 125430.5, 328 status: 'pending', 329 ...overrides, 330 }); 331 ``` 332 333 **Identity / auth is project-wide.** Roles and permissions are project facts (`project.md` §Roles & Permissions), inherited across every epic — so the userinfo contract lives once in `web/src/mocks/data/identity.ts`, exporting `userInfoFor(roleName)` (the `Roles[]` / `Pages[]` shape the app gates on). One definition, exercised identically by both test layers and the manual-test approval — this is exactly the contract the v07 nav bug diverged on. 334 335 **Scenario fixtures — thin compositions, per epic/story.** A list with mixed statuses, the empty state, a rejected transaction with a note. Compose the entity factories inline in tests (`createTransaction({ status: 'approved' })`); only promote a composition to a named export (in the entity file, or a small `web/src/mocks/scenarios/epic-.ts`) when it's reused across stories or across the Vitest/Playwright boundary. Scenario fixtures carry **no** shape definitions. 336 337 **Both test layers consume the same factories.** Vitest imports via the `@/` alias (`@/mocks/data/transaction`); Playwright imports via a **relative** path from `e2e/` (`../src/mocks/data/identity`) to dodge alias resolution at Playwright runtime. So every module under `web/src/mocks/` that the e2e layer can import — entity factories in `data/` **and** scenario fixtures in `scenarios/` — must import **types** with `import type` only (erased at compile) and import **sibling/peer factories** by relative path (`./user`, or `../data/transaction` from a `scenarios/` file), never the `@/` alias — that keeps each module importable from the e2e layer without any alias plumbing. (The `@/` alias is fine in Vitest test files and in app-runtime code like `web/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, which Playwright never imports relatively — the rule is only for the modules an e2e spec reaches through a relative import.) 338 339 **The runtime mock layer consumes them too.** When the project ships MSW handlers (`web/src/mocks/handlers.ts`, the running-app mock used in mock mode), they compose the same factories — `createX(overrides)` for entity bodies, `userInfoFor(role)` for auth — so the dev/demo app and the tests can't drift onto different contracts. The handler keeps the *serving* logic (filtering, pagination, ≥2-per-enum dataset sizing); only the entity *shape + defaults* come from the factory. So all three mock surfaces — Vitest, Playwright, and the MSW runtime — draw from one source. See [mock-setup-agent § Generate handlers](../agents/mock-setup-agent.md#step-3--generate-websrcmockshandlersts). 340 341 **Evolving an entity:** when an epic genuinely adds a field, **extend** the one entity file (a deliberate, reviewable edit — journal it as a Tier-2 factual addition); never copy the entity into a new file. The per-entity files are a coordinated shared surface across epic branches: real edit-conflicts are rare (definitions are append-mostly), and when they do happen they're a genuine shared-contract change governed by [epic-branch-concurrency §6.2](./epic-branch-concurrency.md). Duplication, by contrast, guarantees silent drift. 342 343 --- 344 345 ## Mock data accuracy 346 347 Before creating mocks, check for OpenAPI specs at `generated-docs/specs/api-spec.yaml` (canonical) or `documentation/*.yaml` (user-provided). Specs don't always reflect reality (string enums, unexpected nulls, extra fields), so when sample data exists, use it as the basis. Type your factories so TypeScript catches obvious mismatches. 348 349 When a quirk is discovered (spec says enum, API returns string), document it in the type definition so both tests and implementation benefit: 350 351 ```typescript 352 export interface Portfolio { 353 /** API returns 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' as string, not a typed enum */ 354 status: string; 355 } 356 ``` 357 358 --- 359 360 ## Render scope — component vs full page 361 362 Default to the narrowest scope that covers the ACs. Full-page renders cascade failures across every suite when one component breaks; component-level renders isolate them. 363 364 | Story type | Render | 365 |---|---| 366 | Targets a specific component (chart, grid, form) | That component directly | 367 | Covers page layout / cross-component interactions | Full page | 368 | Story 1 (page setup) with many sections | Full page (first story establishes the page) | 369 370 --- 371 372 ## Testability classification (inline tags) 373 374 The `coverage` tag decides the layer (and therefore the file). These inline annotations are a **secondary** note for the residual jsdom-blindness *inside* a `vitest`-tagged test — they never override the tag or add a cross-layer sibling: 375 376 - **Runtime-only** (a `vitest`-tagged AC whose render you can assert, but whose middleware/server-component/layout-composition aspect jsdom can't exercise) — keep the Vitest test for component-level regression, add `// Runtime-only: verified during manual checklist` above it. If the *primary* behaviour is the redirect/guard itself, it should have been tagged `playwright`, not `vitest`. 377 - **Data-contract** (Vitest mocks `@/lib/api/client`, so the test verifies component behaviour with a mocked response but cannot verify real client → handler → dataset wiring) — add `// Data-contract: full chain verified during manual checklist` 378 - **Manual-only** — this is what a `none` tag with a user-eyeball nature means: do NOT generate a test, and do not report it. The manual checklist is assembled at the manual-test approval from the planner's per-story `manualTestChecklist` and the `coverage: none` tags recorded in the story file 379 380 --- 381 382 ## Mock boundary blindness 383 384 Vitest + RTL runs in jsdom, which cannot exercise certain Next.js integration layers. Tests that mock each boundary independently will pass even when the boundaries aren't connected at runtime — this is why [Testability classification](#testability-classification-inline-tags) exists. 385 386 **jsdom CAN verify (unit-testable):** 387 388 - Component rendering and conditional content 389 - Form interactions and validation feedback 390 - Hook behavior and state changes 391 - Error message display 392 393 **jsdom CANNOT verify (runtime-only):** 394 395 - Whether the page actually changed or stayed (test that in Playwright) 396 - Middleware actually intercepts requests and redirects 397 - Server-component auth (`requireSession()`) actually blocks rendering 398 - Layout composition (a page inside `(authenticated)/` inherits the protected layout) 399 - Multi-layer redirects (middleware → login → return-to-original-page) 400 - `"use client"` boundaries (server-side auth in a client component is silently skipped) 401 402 **jsdom CANNOT verify (data-contract):** 403 404 A component that calls the API client with mocked HTTP passes its Vitest tests but doesn't exercise: 405 406 - Query-param serialization (repeated vs comma-joined arrays) 407 - `buildUrl` correctness for array values 408 - MSW handler contract (does it actually read declared query params?) 409 - Mock dataset realism (≥2 items per enum so filters visibly narrow) 410 - Empty-filter semantics (no filters → all items, not zero) 411 412 A list with a broken status filter passes every component test because the test never touches the actual URL. The bug only appears when the real API client meets the real MSW handler in the browser. 413 414 **How the workflow handles it:** the `developer` performs integration-wiring checks and synthesizes runtime verification items from the story's ACs — so the manual checklist always surfaces runtime-only and data-contract concerns — and the epic-end `/code-review` pass is a further backstop. `mock-setup-agent` generates handlers that honor their OpenAPI contract (query params read and applied; ≥2 items per enum value) to prevent the most common data-contract bugs from shipping as mocks. 415 416 The most dangerous case is when a behaviour depends on a backend response shape the brief *assumed* rather than *verified*: the mocks are built from that same assumption, so the code, the mocks, and every test agree — all green, all wrong (e.g. deriving nav from a `Pages[]` array the real backend returns sparsely). These are captured at PLAN as the epic's [`unverifiedAssumptions`](../agents/feature-planner.md#unverified-assumptions-the-manual-test-approval-ledger) and floated to the **top** of the manual-test approval as a "check these first" list — the human is the only place reality enters the loop, so point their attention at exactly what the pipeline couldn't prove. 417 418 --- 419 420 ## Non-routable Playwright stubs 421 422 Stories with `route === null` still get a Playwright spec file (so the file structure exists for later promotion), but each test is a `test.fixme()` stub — using the **version-agnostic** form below: a real `test(...)` whose body calls `test.fixme()` to skip at runtime. Prefer this form; it behaves consistently across Playwright versions. Avoid the declarative `test.fixme('title', fn)` overload, which has produced version-dependent parse errors. 423 424 ```ts 425 import { test } from '@playwright/test'; 426 427 // Non-routable: 428 test('Epic N, Story M: (deferred to consumer stories)', () => { 429 test.fixme(); // skips at runtime; behaves consistently across Playwright 430 // versions, unlike the declarative test.fixme('title', fn) form 431 }); 432 ``` 433 434 `test.fixme()` is **only** permitted for explicitly non-routable stories (`route === null`). Never as a tool to avoid failing tests. 435 436 **Time-driven ≠ non-routable.** Do not downgrade a routable story (`route !== null`) to a stub because its behaviour is timer-driven or because the component is mounted app-wide with "no surface to navigate to." `page.clock` advances the clock deterministically with no production hooks, and an app-wide manager's effects are observable on any real page — so session-timeout / polling / auto-dismiss stories get a **live** `page.clock` spec (see [Time-dependent behaviour](#time-dependent-behaviour)). `test.fixme()` is for stories with no observable browser surface at all, not for ones that are merely awkward to time. 437
